532636|2026-03.headline: IIFL Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated PAT of INR623 crore (up 24% QoQ) and loan AUM of INR1,08,180 crore (up 38% YoY), with gold AUM up 150% YoY to INR52,581 crore.
532636|2026-03.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT before minority interest of INR623 crore, up 24% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit of INR1,173 crore, up 80% YoY and 9% QoQ. Loan AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, growing 10% QoQ, with gold the primary growth engine at 62 tonnes of tonnage. Asset quality improved, with GNPA about 1.5% and NNPA 0.7%, while the housing finance arm stayed flat and weak on profitability. Management guided to FY27 AUM growth of 20-25% for gold, 18-20% for housing, a credit cost fall to 1.5-1.7%, and a 100-120 bp cost-of-funds reduction on a rating upgrade. The income tax special audit outcome remained pending, with management expecting orders within days and saying it would appeal any demand.

segments.commentary: Collection efficiency is recovering and asset quality is stabilising; management is growing cautiously, targeting about 20% growth with average microfinance ticket of about INR68,000 and micro-LAP ticket of about INR4.8 lakh, and aims to return to AUM levels of March 2024.

A credit rating upgrade from AA (stable) to AA+ could lower cost of funds by 100-120 bp.

Interest rates: management said money-market rates spiked in March and early April on war-related liquidity tightness, and are now normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax special audit and the likely impact (rumoured INR300-400 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on speculative reports. The special audit (mainly gold loans) is complete and the assessment order is expected within days or about a week; the company will appeal any demand and does not expect a material adverse outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an option to demerge into three entities (for ADIA's exit from home finance), but this is a Board decision with no timeline and no active process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 credit cost and ROA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is guided to 1.5-1.7% (against 2.7-3% in FY26) and ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%. Credit cost applies only to the on-balance-sheet book (about 10-20% of AUM), not to assigned loans.

qa_highlights.question: How will IIFL adapt to new gold-loan rules (cash-flow assessment for loans above INR2.5 lakh) and branch expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Detailed credit assessment is in place for all loans above INR2.5 lakh and the branch model already does cash-flow assessment. Gold AUM growth is guided at 20-25%, with more branches in underserved areas.

qa_highlights.question: What are the leverage and capital plans, and is equity needed for 20%+ growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow without equity if co-lending and DA reach 40-45%; it is comfortable with leverage up to 4.5x and will raise debt periodically and equity when the time is right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was housing AUM muted in FY26, and why are home finance ROE and ROA weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the exit of micro-LAP (overlapping with MFI borrowers) and reduced leverage after an equity raise 2-3 years ago. Growth is expected to lift ROE back toward double digits, and LAP is being focused on at about 18% of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rating upgrade roadmap and its impact on cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, GNPA is 1.5%, and profitability is improving; the remaining gap is capital adequacy, which needs more off-book growth or equity. A move to AA+ could cut funding cost by 100-120 bp, but management would not quantify the rating-upgrade impact.

532636|2026-06.headline: IIFL Finance Q1 FY27 PAT before NCI rose 14% QoQ to INR713 crore, with AUM up 38% YoY to INR1,15,523 crore and ROE at 19.5%.

532636|2026-09.headline: IIFL Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 93% YoY to INR805 crore, first quarter above INR800 crore, with AUM up 38% YoY to INR1,24,268 crore.

532648|2026-03.headline: YES Bank Q4 FY26 net profit rose 44.7% YoY to INR 1,068 crore, with ROA of 1.0% and GNPA at a record-low 1.3%.

Asset quality improved sharply, with GNPA at 1.3% and NNPA at 0.2%, while INR 341 crore of one-time standard-asset provisioning was taken in Q4. qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift between Retail, Wholesale and Commercial after the SMBC induction?

qa_highlights.question: How did the bond yield spike affect treasury and AFS reserves?

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 340 crore one-time standard-asset provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 341 crore of provisioning was taken in Q4 under evolving and prudent policies, not linked to any credit issue. It was funded by SR recoveries of ~INR 450 crore and a INR 288 crore write-back from one corporate account.

qa_highlights.question: What is the next ROA milestone, and how sustainable is 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank exited FY26 at 1% ROA. Internal aim is 25-50 bps core ROA improvement, with some JC Flowers ARC write-backs still to come in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were credit card and personal loan slippages in INR crore?

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion and branch share of disbursals change?
qa_highlights.answer: The plan is about 80 branches a year, aligned to deposit growth, credit growth and credit quality in each pin code. Branches supply ~60% of the ~50% of disbursals sourced internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff profile beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 and FY29 will see equal reductions, similar to FY27, with thinner runoff in FY29-FY30 as maturities taper.

532648|2026-09.headline: Yes Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 65% YoY to INR 1,080 crore, but a Supreme Court ruling reinstating INR 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds cuts pro forma CET-1 to about 11.4%.
532648|2026-09.overview: Net profit was INR 1,080 crore (up 65% YoY) with operating profit up 29.4% to INR 1,678 crore and NII up 22.7% to INR 2,822 crore. NIM fell 12-14 bps QoQ to 2.6%, attributed mainly to FCNR(B) mobilisation that was not yet deployed, and management guided to a stable Q3 and a positive bias in Q4.

Recognised P&L gains of INR 395 crore from the Security Receipts portfolio in Q2.
demand_pricing: Reported advances grew 23.7% YoY; excluding FCTL linked to FCNR mobilisation, growth was 17.6%.
Deposits grew 19.5% YoY (end-period) and 22.1% (average). CASA average balances grew 15.5% YoY: current accounts +21.8%, savings +11.6%.
Certificates of deposit rose from about INR 6,000 crore to about INR 11,000 crore. Management called this tactical, citing the long-term rating upgrade above AA and LCR/NSFR considerations.

Floating-rate book is about 65% (linked to repo or T-bill), with the rest fixed. Management said a 25 bps repo move could lift margins by a high single-digit bps, subject to competition and liquidity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AT-1 accounting and cash impact if the write-down is reversed, and is the coupon payable?

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM sensitivity to repo changes, and how should Q3 and Q4 margins be framed?

qa_highlights.question: What is the RIDF runoff plan, and is there quantitative NIM guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 ROA exceed 1%, and how much capital can growth absorb without a raise?

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank raise capital, and what is the rating agency view?

qa_highlights.question: Why did CD issuance rise, and what is the ECL impact?

532652|2026-03.headline: Karnataka Bank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% QoQ to INR408.19 crore; FY26 PAT record INR1,310.50 crore, GNPA down to 2.78%.
532652|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp sequential improvement: NIM rose to 3.07% from 2.92%, cost-to-income fell to 50.47% from 58.72%, and GNPA fell 54 bps QoQ to 2.78%. Business reached INR192,118 crore with gross advances up 8% QoQ to INR83,340 crore, and CASA rose to 33.61%. Management said FY26 guidance was met on most metrics, but advances (INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000–85,000 crore guidance) fell short. Much of the Q4 earnings lift came from lower employee cost, higher fee and technical write-off recovery income, and accelerated provisioning, which analysts questioned on sustainability.

segments.name: Mid-corporate
segments.commentary: Mid-corporate advances grew about 13% QoQ in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: IBPC and food credit book

segments.commentary: Aggregate deposits INR108,779 crore (+4% QoQ). Retail term deposits INR67,648 crore (+2% QoQ, +5% YoY). Bulk deposits fell to 4.2% of total deposits from 4.8%.

guidance_outlook: Business growth around 15%; deposit growth 10% to 15%; advances growth 15% to 20% for FY27.
CASA to be maintained at 33% plus; CD ratio around 80%.
ROA to remain 1% plus, with management saying improvement is expected.
Cost-to-income to be 52% to 53% going forward, from 50.47% in Q4 and 56.34% in FY26.
PCR to rise about 1% every quarter; Q4 rise was larger than that.
Management said NIM margin floor has been reached ("I feel it has bottomed out"), with ongoing focus on 3% plus NIM; NIM had fallen to as low as 2.72% in earlier data.
Business growth phasing: H1 about 39% and H2 about 61% of annual growth; management also cited a monthly target path.
ECL transition impact estimated at 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over about 4 to 5 years (roughly 25 to 30 bps of credit cost per year).
Management targets recovering 50% of NPA and technical write-off books; called it ambitious and gave no figure.

FY27 product launches: tobacco agri input loans, programmable CBDC, NFC-based QR/Tap and Pay, surrogate-based housing lending, MSME dropline OD and LAP; major IT solutions due in FY27 include loan origination revamp, HRMS, treasury and BHIM 3.0.
capex_capacity: Around 31 branches opened in FY26; management said branch expansion plans may be revised in view of West Asia-related uncertainty.
Employee count fell in Q4 with about 350 to 400 retirements per month and no recruitment in Q4; some recruitment planned for IT and expansion.
Technical written-off portfolio about INR2,500 crore.
IT spending rising; major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27 include loan origination system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.
demand_pricing: Advances fell from about INR78,000 crore to about INR71,000 crore in FY25 before recovering to INR83,340 crore in FY26; management said retail and mid-corporate growth is the focus and bulk advances will be reduced.
About INR2,000 crore of sanctioned loans were pending disbursal as of March 2026; management said disbursement began post April.
Loan repayments were about INR26,000 crore in FY26; management estimated total disbursements at about INR31,000 to 32,000 crore.
Around 60% to 65% of the book is EBLR linked to T-bill rates (about 55% per management figures), 2.31% EBLR linked to G-sec, MCLR 5.59%, base rate 0.31% at March 2026.
Management said EBLR is at its lowest and any upward move in market rates would help interest income; ALCO will respond as required.

qa_highlights.question: Why did advances rise sharply in the quarter and how does it fit funding and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR was strong so it prioritised advances; funding came from available resources and some short-term borrowings, and funding was not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 across advances, ROA, credit cost, GNPA, NNPA and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Business growth around 15%, deposits 10% to 15%, advances 15% to 20%, CASA 33%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 52% to 53%. Credit cost was not given a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 employee cost fall while other opex rose, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any one-time shift. Employee cost cannot be cut but was held down through staff utilisation; attrition of about 350 to 400 a month and selective recruitment for IT and expansion. No FY27 employee cost figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income driven by core fees or treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income rose on fee income (processing charges, one-time ATM card fees, guarantee commission) and recovery from the technical write-off book; treasury gain about INR13 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield pressure from growth squeeze margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBLR is at its lowest and margins have bottomed; upward rate moves would help; ALCO will manage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were gross slippages so low in Q4 and what is the interest reversal impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited SMA and CMA stress controls and recovery efforts; slippage was 0.20% in Q4 vs 0.47% in Q3. It did not quantify interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Will PCR keep rising, and what are the FY27 provisioning and technical write-off recovery expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is to rise about 1% a quarter; Q4 rose more. Recovery targets are ambitious (50% of NPA and technical write-off books) with no specific figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G-sec versus EBLR book mix and the gratuity impact on employee cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said both figures would be shared later by email; the call gave only the rate-linked mix (EBLR linked to T-bill about 55%, G-sec 2.31%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on net worth and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ECL impact is about 1% to 1.5% of capital, spread over four to five years, with about 25 to 30 bps of credit cost each year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East deposit exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East and NRI deposits are a small share; the majority of deposits are domestic.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q4 earnings lift: PAT jump was helped by lower employee cost (management did not give a FY27 employee cost figure or gratuity impact), higher fee income and technical write-off recoveries, and accelerated provisioning; track whether these recur in Q1 FY27.

Advances shortfall vs guidance: gross advances INR83,340 crore vs INR84,000-85,000 crore guidance; FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-20% depends on converting INR2,000 crore pending disbursal and on shifting mix from bulk/IBPC to retail and mid-corporate.
Margin path: management said NIM has bottomed and ALCO will respond to rate moves, but ~55% of book is T-bill linked EBLR and rate direction is market-driven; watch NIM vs the 3% plus target.

Slippage and recovery sustainability: Q4 slippage of 0.20% vs 0.47% in Q3 is well below prior run rate; the 50% NPA and technical write-off recovery target (technical write-off book ~INR2,500 crore) was called highly ambitious with no figure given.

Macro and external risks: West Asia conflict, energy prices and supply-chain pressure; branch expansion plans may be revised; ECL transition impact of 1-1.5% of capital, spread over 4-5 years (about 25-30 bps credit cost per year), not yet quantified in FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we have witnessed meaningful improvement in all the ratios and have delivered on the guidance given during my previous interactions with the investor community
Growth for the business is also target, there is a target for recovery also.
What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.
I feel it has bottomed out. There may not be any chance it is coming down further.
We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on.

Management repeatedly described the outlook as measured and prudent given West Asia and macro uncertainty.

532652|2026-06.headline: Karnataka Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 43% YoY to INR418.95 crores, NIM widened to 3.20%, and Gross NPA fell to 2.58%.

Business reached a record INR1,97,007 crores, with gross advances up 4% QoQ and 17% YoY, and CASA and CD ratio both improving. Management guided to around 15% overall business growth in FY27 and an ROA of 1.35% to 1.40%, but gave limited detail on SMA-2 rise, mid-corporate growth and the ECL transition.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank expanding branches and what is the sanctioned and pipeline book to support growth, given guidance looks conservative?

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank provide more provisions given SMA-2 rose to INR750 crores from INR635 crores and special mention accounts are at INR3,435 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on controlling SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2, attributed the Q1 rise partly to holidays and single-day defaults before 30 June, and said no additional provisioning is required for slippages going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What will the ECL transition require in additional provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR is comfortable and a dedicated team has been working since 1 April on Stage 1, 2 and 3 impact; it does not foresee a problem from ECL.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost increase and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost has not gone up, citing yield-movement-related gratuity and retirement benefit provisions, and expects it in the same range next quarter onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA sustain at 1.35% to 1.40% for the full year, and what are the FY27 and FY28 ROA and ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for ROA of 1.35% to 1.40% from 1.29% in Q1 and said it will keep improving, without giving a full-year ROE target or FY28 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 'other' (non-RAM) advances segment growing faster than RAM, and when will RAM outgrow corporate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail growth requires better turnaround time and that retail hubs in 15 regional offices are driving business; it said large corporate is restricted to protect yield and bulk advances will reduce in percentage terms.

qa_highlights.question: Is mid-corporate growth returning after several quarters of YoY decline?

532652|2026-09.headline: Karnataka Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 4% QoQ to INR435.89 crores, with gross NPA down to 2.27% and aggregate business at a record INR2,07,132 crores.
532652|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed sequential gains across most metrics: PAT up 4% QoQ to INR435.89 crores, NII up 5% QoQ to INR982.44 crores, and cost-to-income down to 52.68% from 55.14%. Gross NPA fell 31 bps QoQ to 2.27% and slippage eased to 0.11%. NIM dipped to 3.17% from 3.20% in Q1, which management attributed to averaging effects and a one-off income-tax-related item in Q1. Advances grew 6% QoQ and 25% YoY, led by the retail, agri and MSME (RAM) book. Management reiterated FY27 growth guidance of 15% to 20% in advances and 10% to 15% in liabilities.

532662|2026-03.headline: HT Media Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 5% to INR 131 crore with margin up 100 bps to 23% on ad yields, while radio and OTTplay drag continued.
532662|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat for FY26 and down 2% in Q4 to INR 558 crore, but EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps both in the quarter and the full year. Print drove the result, with advertising revenue up 10% in Q4 on higher ad yields, while volumes were broadly flat. Radio revenue fell on a high events base, and management surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies and exited the OTTplay subscription business effective 1 April 2026. Net cash remains above INR 1,000 crore, though other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR 218 crore in FY25 (about INR 50 crore)

segments.name: Print (combined)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue INR 427 crore (up ~8%-level growth stated for FY) with operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23% margin; FY26 operating revenue INR 1,500 crore (up 8%), operating EBITDA INR 208 crore (14% margin). Q4 ad revenue INR 313 crore (up 10%); FY ad revenue INR 1,148 crore (up 8%); circulation nearly flat for FY.

Copy share gains in selected markets, funded by ad yield gains; copy investment described as a conscious, market-by-market strategy.

Investment of INR 22 crore by HMVL in Assetvault Limited (AasaanWill), described as an AFE investment with no cash outflow.

OTTplay failed to reach unit economics despite content, acquisition and retention changes; telcos' presence made the market difficult. Strategic partner and sale talks did not conclude, and management said there is no residual value.

qa_highlights.question: Ad revenue growth in English and Hindi: volumes or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly pricing and yield; volumes flat, in line with industry. Management said it is unclear how much of the yield gain is structural.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income rise sharply in HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: It reflects forfeiture of contractual AFE-related revenue that was not received within the specified period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HMVL's Print segment revenue for the prior year change by about INR 6 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pervez Bajan said it is an intersegment revenue elimination for OTTplay advertising in print, reclassified because OTTplay moved to discontinued operations; the amount was written off with a matching PBIT impact.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further exceptional losses from radio or OTTplay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further closure losses are expected. A possible statutory charge from the new labour codes could hit exceptional items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about INR 50 crore, and why invest INR 22 crore in Assetvault?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings as yields rose to record highs; the 10-year is near 7%. Management plans to hold to maturity. Assetvault is an AFE investment with no cash outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ad yield sustainable, and what is the cash plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly sustainable, but competitor reactions are a risk. Management aims to keep deals at or above current levels. The Board is investing the cash pile in core and digital and has no current capital return plan.

Radio sector pressure despite portfolio cleanup; management will review on a close basis.
Residual OTTplay servicing costs through September 2026 and cash outflows from contract exits.

532662|2026-06.headline: HT Media Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to INR 90 crore, while a preferential issue drew shareholder pushback.
532662|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up about 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, and management credited yield improvement. Digital operating revenue fell about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore, as the portfolio was deliberately reset, and Radio was flat with negative INR 3 crore EBITDA after surrendering licences for non-viable stations. The board approved a preferential issue of equity to HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (not HMVL), priced at the SEBI formula (around INR 24-25 per share), which drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing.

segments.commentary: Advertising revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 156 crore; circulation revenue grew 14% to INR 13 crore (about INR 1.5 crore absolute change, mostly pricing and mix).

segments.name: Hindi Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue rose YoY to INR 139 crore; circulation revenue flat.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Licences surrendered for certain non-viable stations.

segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%) after deliberate portfolio reset; OTTplay decision taken around 31 March 2026 per management.

Government ad and circulation rates were raised in November 2025 after seven years, so the price benefit continues for the next two quarters.

Radio footprint reduced by surrendering licences for non-viable stations.

HMVL cash (where most of the INR 922 crore net cash sits) to be deployed at HMVL board's discretion; no preferential issue at HMVL.
demand_pricing: Commercial print revenue held on volume with yield improvement as the main driver; government revenue grew on both volume and the November 2025 rate increase.

Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

risks_watch: Newsprint at about USD 650-700 per tonne, the highest since COVID, with no forward market; Q2 newsprint guided slightly higher than Q1, and a weaker dollar adds to cost pressure on the 13% Print margin.

Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent: ~15% dilution at roughly INR 24-25 per share versus book value of about INR 70; shareholder voting is ongoing and at least one minority holder has voted against, so approval and final pricing remain open.
Debt at HT Media and DCL: management said 30-50% of debt will be retired from the issue proceeds; the net cash of INR 922 crore sits in HMVL, and the consolidated figure masks standalone net debt.
Other income at HMVL (treasury gains and profit on asset sales) is not predictable and depends on yield curve movements, so the Q1 profit level may not repeat.

Digital operating revenue down about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore after the portfolio reset; Radio EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Track whether these turn profitable next quarter and whether the Q1 earnings step-up holds once government rate benefits cycle out after two quarters.

Debt has been building in HT Media for the last 4-5 years post-COVID because of the Print English operations and Radio operations, etc.
Treasury gains is basically mutual funds and the NA V based process and not a MTM valuation-based process.

Hareesh Ramanna said the Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive, so no commercial order is yet in hand.

532663|2026-09.headline: Sasken Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.6% YoY to Rs.321 Cr with EBITDA margin up 330 bps QoQ to 12.9%, driven by software services.

532667|2026-03.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.
532667|2026-03.overview: Suzlon reported record Q4 FY26 India deliveries of 830 MW and FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW (up 58%). Consolidated Q4 revenue was INR5,468 crore with EBITDA of INR964 crore (up 39% YoY) and reported PAT of INR1,114 crore, while FY26 PAT of INR3,153 crore includes a INR742 crore deferred tax asset recognition. Management highlighted a shift toward EPC and development (DevCo) contracts, with EPC share of the order book rising to 28% from about 20% in Q2, and a 2.1 GW Andhra Pradesh development right extended by 24 months. Order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW at the start of the year, while commissioning reached 332 MW in Q4 and 744 MW for the year, with 971 MW erected but not yet commissioned.

532667|2026-09.headline: Suzlon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27% QoQ to INR4,869 crores, but WTG contribution margin fell to 21.2% and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was cut to about 15%.

532668|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, but Q4 missed plan on Middle East deal slippage and hyperscaler revenue timing; no FY27 growth number given.
532668|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 was below its own standards: revenue rose 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.02% and PAT margin at 15.02%, toward the lower end of guided ranges. The original plan was close to 30% growth, and Q4 fell short on Middle East license deal closures and project completions, a delayed hyperscaler data center project, and a one-time labour code charge. Management is stepping up expensed and capitalised investment in AI-native banking software, transit back-office software, payments and data centers, and expects higher working capital and balance-sheet pressure in FY27. It declined to give a numerical FY27 growth guide, saying only that it expects to grow ahead of industry rates.

Management expects a short spurt of capitalised and expensed investment, tapering over the next couple of quarters, with a larger upfront investment year than usual in FY27.
Management expects no debt increase in FY27. Pressure is expected in working capital and growth-oriented balance-sheet items.
Management expects Middle East deal activity to restart, though not at full pace. It expects the MEA slowdown may extend into Q1 FY27.

Management said a large part of the development spend will be routed to the P&L where client projects back it. Some will be built ahead of client contracts and capitalised.
Transit software stack work for MMRDA is described as a one-off, with later spend expected to be expensed.
Data center: investment in long-lead project execution ahead of revenue recognition, with some of the early work deferred into Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Middle East: banks halted late-stage buying processes in Q4. Management said some restarts of deal activity and POCs are now visible, but full buying has not resumed. Pre-war Saudi bank wins are in execution but have been slowed by inability to station teams on site.

Pricing: management did not address pricing pressure directly. It said that larger contracts (INR 100-350 crore) are carrying higher working capital and that contracting and payment terms are being tightened.

Cross-sell: average banking relationships are about 2 products per bank (up from about 1.5), with some banks using 5 or 6 products. Management said mature software could grow 10%-12% without new logos.

532684|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT rose 50.1% to Rs. 146.7 crore on revenue of Rs. 1,470.6 crore, with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 13.8%.
532684|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong FY26 with consolidated EBITDA up 15.7% to Rs. 203 crore and PAT up 50.1%, driven by product mix and realisations. Q4 consolidated revenue was Rs. 358.2 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.1% versus 9.0% a year earlier. Standalone FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 16.0% from 10.6%. Greenfield Mundra capacity has started production and the Egypt plant is expected to start operations shortly. The Board recommended a dividend of Re. 0.70 per share.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Management cited strong demand across CNG and industrial gas applications, with industrial applications up healthily in the year. Early traction in semiconductors and defence supported mix. No segment-level figures were given.

segments.name: US business
segments.commentary: Order book of about US$75 million, to be executed over 18 to 24 months. Management described momentum as steady, with clean energy and specialised industrial applications as opportunities.

segments.name: Middle East (Dubai) business
segments.commentary: Management said the unit is running at around 50% utilisation and its order book is improving, but shipment disruption from the Middle East situation is a constraint. Analyst said the business was under pressure through FY26 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: Mundra greenfield plant has started production; ramp-up expected about 6 months after start, with India targets to be achieved soon.
Egypt plant may be operational by end of June 2026; ramp-up to start about 6 months later, with immediate target around 40% of capacity and about 80% over time.
Management expects the Dubai business to be better in FY27 as the order book improves, subject to shipment constraints.
GST classification (HSN) clarification sought by industry; management said resolution could take 6 months to a year.
New CEO (Mr. Gupta) has been proposed but has not yet joined; background details to be shared after joining.
capex_capacity: Mundra greenfield facility in India has commenced production.
Egypt facility is progressing steadily and may be operational by end of June 2026; ramp-up expected 6 months after start.
CWIP of Rs. 162 crore covers uncapitalised projects in Egypt, USA and India together.
Management said capacity expansion continued during the year while maintaining financial discipline.
demand_pricing: Management said CNG passenger vehicle demand is resilient to modest CNG price increases; PV trend depends on petrol price movement.
CNG accounted for nearly 22% of passenger vehicle sales in FY26, second-largest fuel type for the second consecutive year, ahead of diesel (industry reports as cited).
Management said commercial vehicle segment continues to perform well and does not see demand dropping; no figure given for CV growth.
Fuel price volatility, particularly LNG supply and pricing, was flagged as a factor to monitor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Dubai business improve in coming years given Middle East geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement this year. The unit is running at around 50% and the order book is building, but shipment issues in the Middle East are the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How will higher LNG costs and CNG price increases affect India demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CNG price rises so far are modest and customers are switching from petrol and diesel, so PV sales should not be materially affected. PV demand depends mainly on petrol price movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US order book and its execution period?
qa_highlights.answer: Around US$75 million, to be executed over 18 to 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the background of the proposed new CEO, Mr. Gupta?
qa_highlights.answer: Details will be shared after he joins; he has not yet joined.

qa_highlights.question: When will Mundra and Egypt ramp up and to what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mundra production has started, with ramp-up about 6 months out and India targets expected soon. Egypt may start by end of June, with ramp-up after 6 months to about 40% of target initially and about 80% later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs. 162 crore CWIP?
qa_highlights.answer: It covers projects not yet capitalised across Egypt, USA and India.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on the GST case?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry has made a representation seeking HSN clarification on the product; management is positive and expects a timeline of 6 months to a year.

Slow ramp-up of Mundra and Egypt plants; Egypt starts at about 40% of target.

532689|2026-03.headline: PVR INOX Q4 FY26 PAT rose to INR178 crores from a loss of about INR10 crores; FY26 net debt cut to INR161 crores and FCF hit a record INR790 crores.
532689|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 25% to INR1,577 crores and EBITDA rose nearly six-fold to INR169 crores, with PAT helped by the gain on divesting 4700BC to Marico. FY26 was the best year on record: 150 million guests (+10%), ATP INR280 (+8%), SPH INR147 (+10%), and IND AS 116-adjusted revenue of INR6,742 crores (+16%). The company pivoted to capital-light formats (55% of 93 FY26 screen additions), cut screen exits to 18 from 72, and reduced net debt to INR161 crores. Management guided FY27 capex to INR375-400 crores and 120+ new screens, with gross debt targeted at about INR500 crores.

segments.name: Exhibition (multiplex operations)
segments.commentary: FY26 footfall 150 million (+10%) and occupancy of 26.2% per management; Q4 footfall 31 million, a record Q4 driven by Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Border 2 and Project Hail Mary.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management called advertising growth subdued this year; Gautam Dutta said Jana Nayagan and Toxic moving out of their slots cost about 7-8% growth, with primary advertising growth expected in H2 from October-December releases.

segments.name: Franchise / FOCO management fees
segments.commentary: FY26 management income close to INR10 crores; run-rate INR13-14 crores per annum, with run-rate growth of 40-50%. Fee is 10-14% of cinema top line.

guidance_outlook: FY27 new screen additions of 100-plus, around 120 visible; 55-60% expected in FOCO and asset-light formats.
FY27 capex INR375-400 crores: about INR225-250 crores new projects, INR80-100 crores renovation, balance maintenance and IT.
Signed capital-light pipeline of 138 screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light), expected to execute over about 18 months.
Gross debt about INR760 crores at 31 March 2026, to be brought down to about INR500 crores; net debt to zero possible in 1H FY27 (not committed on timing).
First smart screen pilots to open by mid-July 2026, targeting 28-30 screens this financial year; smart screen capex at least 30-40% below mainstream cinemas.
Capital allocation (dividend or buyback) to be decided by the Board after the company turns net cash; no incremental guidance given.
capex_capacity: FY26: 93 screens added, 55% capital-light (51 screens: 29 asset-light, 22 FOCO); 18 screen exits vs 72 in FY25.
Capex intensity down 24% YoY in FY26.
FY27 capex guided at INR375-400 crores; new screens planned 120+ per year.
Asset-light: developer funds 40-80% of capex; balance capitalised as ROU asset and lease liability, with rent paid as yield.
FOCO: company does not capitalise screens; books only management fee.
demand_pricing: Indian box office FY26 INR13,519 crores, up 11%; Bollywood up 55%, English up 54%.
Mid-scale films grossing INR100-200 crores rose from 12% to 20% share of box office.
Management expects occupancy to rise, citing 470 theatrical vs 30 OTT releases in CY2025 per an EY report (vs 217 vs 105 in CY2022).
Management says IPL has no measurable impact on cinema attendance; IPL playoff matches screened in its cinemas.
Management sees no direct macro impact from West Asia crisis measures; cites cinema as resilient in downturns.
Management says 27-28% occupancy can still deliver pre-COVID EBITDA margins because of post-merger cost efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Given debt is negligible, what is FY27 screen addition and own vs asset-light mix, and would dividends follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 120-odd screens in FY27, with 55-60% in FOCO/asset-light; aim to become cash positive, with the Board to decide on accrual use later.

qa_highlights.question: Why pursue asset-light if the balance sheet can fund growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO improve ROCE; own capex will continue in high-competition markets, especially South India, while partner models suit markets with strong share and lower competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 capex INR375-400 crores when most new screens are capital-light?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR225-250 crores for new projects (fit-out payments and handovers), INR80-100 crores for renovations, and the rest for maintenance and IT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets fall from about INR4,900 crores to INR4,600 crores despite screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation exceeded gross ROU additions; FOCO and asset-light screens add much less ROU than fully leased screens.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a buyback given strong cash flow and low net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first goal is positive net cash, then the Board will discuss capital allocation; buyback is on the list but no guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How do FOCO economics work for PVR INOX on the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the management fee (10-14% of top line) is booked; the landlord keeps the property P&L, and PVR INOX incurs no capex or opex on FOCO screens, per management.

risks_watch: Occupancy stuck near 26% (26.2% FY26) despite the target of rising levels; management says 27-28% can restore pre-COVID margins.
Advertising growth subdued; big films shifting dates cut growth by about 7-8%, with dependence on H2 releases.
Macro risk from West Asia crisis and possible fuel price hikes on urban discretionary spend; management says no direct impact seen.
Q4 PAT includes a one-time divestment gain (4700BC to Marico), so underlying earnings are not clear from the call.
Execution of 138 signed capital-light screens over about 18 months and first smart screen pilots by mid-July 2026.

Lease and rent cost trend as capital-light share rises; no quantified rent-to-revenue guidance given.

532689|2026-06.headline: PVR INOX Q1 FY27 PAT of INR71 crore vs loss of INR34 crore a year ago; net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026.
532689|2026-06.overview: Revenue on an Ind AS 116 adjusted basis rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore, with EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crore at a 14% margin. Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million, with ATP at INR273 (+8%) and SPH at INR161 (+9%). The company turned net cash of INR80 crore, and management said growth can now be funded from internal cash flows. No new screens opened in Q1 because completed sites were awaiting regulatory licences; openings are expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR34 crore in Q1 FY26
company describes it as debt-free; peak debt cited as INR1,450 crore
up from about 63-64%; convenience fee income +29% YoY

segments.name: Exhibition (cinemas)
segments.commentary: Footfalls 36.6 million (+8%), ATP INR273 (+8%), SPH INR161 (+9%). Premium formats are 16% of the circuit (IMAX, 4DX, ICE, ScreenX, recliners, Insignia, Director's Cut, LUXE).

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management said ad revenue is still below its post-COVID peak and expects about a year to fully recover. Growth is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 with large titles; it did not give a figure.

segments.name: Alternate content and F&B
segments.commentary: Alternate content (live sports, concerts, events) ATP is about INR409; artist cost ranges from 35% to 65-70% of ticket. Food court JV with Devyani has 3 outlets open, with more in the pipeline. Web and app monetisation launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); Q1 had no openings and few closures are expected for the rest of the year.
FY27 capex now about INR350 crore, down from the earlier INR400 crore, including the food court JV and a higher renovation share.
Film hire cost guided at 45% to 45.5% of revenue for full-year FY27; F&B COGS expected to fall YoY.
Near-term target is a return to pre-COVID ROCE levels; no FCF target was given.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 expansion: about 300 cities identified, first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly, with asset-light and FOCO models; growth expected to accelerate from FY28.
Management expects margins of pre-COVID levels even at 27-28% occupancy.
capex_capacity: Screen count about 1,790 today, up from about 1,650 at the merger; about 120 net screens added over the last 4 years.
FY27 screen openings were held back by pending regulatory licences; openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.
Closed screens in Q1 were loss-making and more than 18-20 years old; bulk of FY27 closures done in Q1.
Around 600 screens are in South India; southern concentration is about 34%, according to an analyst's estimate.
Asset-light and FOCO models are the main route for new sites; the 15 million sq ft of leased space is being offered for sublease where it is not needed.
demand_pricing: India box office grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY27 across metros, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and across languages.
North America box office was up 14% YoY at $4.8 billion in H1 2026, per management.

ATP growth was driven by dynamic pricing plus premium mix; discounts are offered on Tuesdays, morning shows and front seats.

Management sees no INR500 crore-plus film so far in the year, but says mid-scale films are performing; it views the upcoming slate (Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three) as strong.
Management said the occupancy trend is recovering as release windows return to 8 weeks, but did not disclose a current occupancy figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the screen closures and asset-light mix affecting the FY27 screen and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross screen additions are still 90-100 and net additions about 80. Capex is now about INR350 crore versus INR400 crore earlier, because FOCO and capital-light demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revisit asset-light models now that it is net cash, and is more real estate monetisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO will continue and will not limit growth of 100-120 screens a year. Capital will be deployed where needed without borrowing. Real estate monetisation is not planned at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why have footfalls stayed flat at 14-15 crore over rolling 12 months despite southern screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the southern skew reflects where opportunities are; 150 million admissions last year was the post-COVID high. It said occupancy is recovering and that margins at 27-28% occupancy can match pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 FCF target and what is the plan for surplus cash, including buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Sharma said there is no FCF target. The immediate goal is pre-COVID ROCE. Shareholder returns, including buyback, are being evaluated and will be disclosed when the Board decides.

qa_highlights.question: What are the unit economics of properties on the capital-light models?
qa_highlights.answer: Properties take 12-18 months to mature. FY24 and FY25 vintages are at margins above company level, and first-vintage performance will be shared by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did online penetration rise and what is the app/web monetisation revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Online penetration rose to about 69% on marketing and content mix. Growth will slow from here. The app/web ad product launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did film hire and COGS fall about 200 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Film hire fell because Dhurandhar was in its lower-rate third and fourth weeks, and there was no mega-blockbuster to trigger bonus payouts. F&B COGS have fallen YoY for two years.

Advertising has not yet recovered to post-COVID levels; management expects about another year.
Online penetration growth is slowing near 70%, so convenience fee growth will depend on ATP and admits.

Yes, it would take another maybe a year before we get to the post-COVID and go ahead of that.

rows.why: Tier 2/3 first opening in Muzaffarpur is imminent, food court JV has 3 outlets with more in the pipeline, and the web/app ad product launched a month ago at INR2-3 crore annualised.

rows.label: Buyback or shareholder returns decision
rows.why: Company is net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026 and says shareholder returns including buyback are being evaluated, with disclosure only once the Board decides.

rows.label: Net cash position and self-funded growth
rows.why: Net cash of INR80 crore versus peak debt of INR1,450 crore, and management says growth can now be funded from internal cash flows.

rows.label: Upcoming film slate
rows.why: Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three are cited as strong, but no INR500 crore-plus film has yet been released in FY27 and the brief gives no box office estimate for them.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the balance sheet and the content slate, but cautious on advertising recovery (about a year), undisclosed occupancy, and capital use with buyback left open; analysts probed screen additions, asset-light economics, footfall stagnation and FCF targets.

532689|2026-09.headline: PVR INOX Q2 FY27 adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to INR 475 crores at a 22.3% margin, with PAT more than doubling to INR 273 crores.
532689|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was described as the best-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by a record industry box office of INR 4,433 crores (up 23% YoY) and footfalls up 4% to 46.3 million. Ind AS 116 adjusted total income grew 17% to INR 2,133 crores, with operating leverage lifting EBITDA margin about 420 bps. Management turned net cash (INR 141 crores at September-end), executed a maiden INR 300 crore buyback, and adopted a capital allocation policy targeting around 30% of annual surplus cash flow returned to shareholders. Screen growth is guided to accelerate, with 90-100 openings in FY27 and a new capital-light SMART Cinema format piloted in Muzaffarpur.

segments.name: Movie exhibition
segments.commentary: Footfalls 46.3 million (+4% YoY), occupancy 30.4%. Company says it under-indexed industry growth (18% vs 23%) because content was spread across single screens in Tier 2-4 towns.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: F&B spend per head INR 153 (+14% YoY). Popcorn and Pepsi make up about 60% of F&B sales; management says gross margin rose from about 74% to 77-78%. About 85% of footfalls buy F&B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films. Management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War; a pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

segments.name: Network and expansion
segments.commentary: Network at 1,797 screens across 114 cities (India and Sri Lanka). H1 added 24 screens across 6 cinemas and exited 25 mostly loss-making screens.

guidance_outlook: Open 90-100 new screens in FY27, mostly in H2 and mainly capital-light formats.
Next year (FY28) screen openings guided to about 150-175 per year, with about 60-70 possibly SMART screens; roughly 500 screens over three years was accepted by management.
Overall FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores (H1 spend INR 132 crores); FY28 capex likely above INR 350 crores, plus or minus.
Depreciation to fall by INR 35-40 crores a year after a useful-life change for projectors and IT equipment.
Capital allocation policy: keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x after distributions, invest for growth, and return about 30% of annual surplus cash flow via dividends or buybacks.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to benefit from a strong film slate; said it was 'very hopeful and optimistic' about H2 but did not give a Q3 footfall number.
Target payback of 3-4 years per unit; SMART Cinema capex 25-30% below normal screens and opex about 25% lower.
capex_capacity: Network 1,797 screens across 114 cities; 24 screens added and 25 exited in H1 FY27.

First SMART Cinema opened in Muzaffarpur, Bihar in September 2026 (capex 25-30% lower, opex about 25% lower, ATP about INR 190); two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur) and about 100 more signed for opening in the next 12-18 months.
300 cities identified for SMART Cinemas; expected two or three more SMART openings this fiscal.
Expansion mix is asset-light, FOCO and lease; for FOCO, only management fees are booked; for asset-light, full P&L is consolidated.
Around 35-40% of new screens in the last 2-3 years opened in South India.
demand_pricing: Industry box office INR 4,433 crores in Q2 (record, first quarter above INR 4,000 crores); H1 INR 7,618 crores (+22%).
English cinema INR 1,024 crores (+87%); Spider-Man: Brand New Day INR 608 crores; Odyssey INR 233 crores.
Hindi led by Hanuman Ansh (INR 351 crores) and Mirzapur: The Movie (INR 267 crores). Management argued Hindi growth is understated due to dubbed English films being reported under English.
Value offers: weekday morning shows at INR 99, Friday first shows at INR 149, front-row seats from INR 79.
South India average ticket price about 25% below the rest of India; management said higher occupancy more than offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How are SMART Cinemas priced, what is the capex, and what is the 2-year opening plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower than normal cinemas; ATP around INR 190 at the pilot. About 100 more are signed for 12-18 months. Management said growth will not be compromised while keeping paybacks within 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hindi incremental box office so small in H1 versus regional and English?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 had a high Hindi base; Hollywood was recovering. It added that dubbed English films (about INR 200 crores from Spider-Man) count as English, so Hindi growth is understated.

qa_highlights.question: Will screen additions accelerate after the cleanup of underperforming screens?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Past closures were of dilapidated mall screens. Management guided to 150-175 openings a year from next fiscal, with about 500 screens over three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are FOCO and asset-light revenues and costs accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light is fully consolidated. FOCO books only management fees, with operating costs at the franchisee. Lease screens are traditional leases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets and lease liabilities decline despite openings?
qa_highlights.answer: About 23-24 loss-making screens closed in H1, which offset new openings. ROU assets and liabilities also decline through depreciation and repayment under Ind AS 116.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion in F&B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a high-margin mix (popcorn and Pepsi are about 60% of sales), supplier renegotiation, a 4PL logistics migration that cuts wastage, and volume growth from weekend and weekday promotions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PVR's box office growth (18%) lag the industry (23%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to content mix: Hanuman Ansh, Mirzapur and regional films did well in Tier 2-4 towns where single screens dominate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the depreciation and capex numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year from the useful-life change. FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores; FY28 above INR 350 crores.

risks_watch: Ad revenue recovery depends on the Q3-Q4 tentpole slate (Ramayana, King, Avengers, Love & War) and the digital pay-per-eyeball platform, due in 8-10 months.
SMART format is a pilot with only about two months of data; the 150-175 screen FY28 target depends on the pipeline converting.
Lower rent-to-revenue in Q2 is tied to revenue-share terms on legacy screens (minimum guarantee or revenue share, whichever is higher); rent rose about 11% YoY in Q2.
Q2 other income includes INR 7 crores of one-off provision reversals.
Pending southern state ticket-price issues: management said no conversations are underway.
532689|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the film slate, with repeated emphasis on capital discipline and unit paybacks. Management was evasive on specifics for Q3 footfalls (no number given) and on the Hindi box office data, which it disputed.
key_quotes: This is also our best ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Unit level economics, even if you open 200 screens a year will not be compromised.
Hindi is not struggling. Hindi has been doing well since last year.
So we are trying to build on a digital platform.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose about 420 bps to 22.3% in Q2 on operating leverage, F&B gross margin moved from about 74% to 77-78%, and depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year; H2 tentpole films support it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 90-100 new screens guided for FY27 with the bulk in H2, from 24 added and 25 exited in H1, and about 100 SMART screens signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Footfalls rose 4% to 46.3 million in Q2 against industry box office up 23%, and management is 'very hopeful and optimistic' on H2 with Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, though no Q3 footfall number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 30.4% so capacity is not constrained, but FY28 capex is guided above INR 350 crores for 150-175 SMART screens a year and about 300 cities are identified, so a capex plan is likely to be formalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA rose 56% and H1 PAT rose 233%, and management is confident on the H2 film slate, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised numerically.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Screen additions (90-100) and capex (INR 300-330 crores) are held or cut, and the ad revenue risk depends on the Q3-Q4 slate and an 8-10 month digital platform.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SMART Cinema format is piloted in Muzaffarpur at about INR 190 ATP with two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur), and the pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

rows.label: SMART Cinema low-price format rollout
rows.why: SMART ATP is about INR 190 against INR 298 company-wide, with capex 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower, and about 100 more signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet and cash returns
rows.why: Net cash of INR 141 crores at end-September after H1 FREE cash flow of INR 604 crores, with a policy to return about 30% of surplus cash flow and keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x.

rows.label: Ad revenue recovery on tentpole films
rows.why: Advertising was weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films, and management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, but no ad figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, F&B gross margin, the SMART format's paybacks and H2 films, and stayed evasive on Q3 footfalls and disputed the Hindi box office data. Analysts pressed on the lag versus industry growth, the SMART pilot's short data history and the 150-175 screen FY28 target.

532698|2026-03.headline: Nitin Spinners Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR859.8 crore (+7.4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin rose to 15.17%, with management guiding to a 16-20% normalised margin in FY27.
532698|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR859.8 crore, up 7.4% QoQ and 2.2% YoY, driven by better demand and yarn prices. EBITDA rose 16.9% QoQ to INR130.4 crore, with margin up 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, and PAT reached INR57.4 crore. For full FY26, revenue fell 2.8% to INR3,213.9 crore and EBITDA fell 4% to INR452.8 crore, while PAT rose 1.2% to INR177.6 crore. Management said the capex programme (fabric and spinning expansion, renewable power) is on track for H2 FY27 commissioning.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Yarn was 74% of FY26 revenue; spinning capacity ran at over 98% utilisation in Q4 FY26, with management guiding 97-98% going forward. Average yarn spread (realisation over cotton cost, around 33-34 count) is about INR120-125/kg, up from about INR110/kg last quarter.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric was 21% of FY26 revenue (woven about 18%, knitted about 4%, per the Q&A corrections). Woven capacity ran at over 90% utilisation in Q4; woven realisation rose about 2-2.5% QoQ and knitted about 5% QoQ. Knitted utilisation is below normal, with a 65-70% normal level expected to return in 1-1.5 years.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Others contributed 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 63% of Q4 FY26 revenue (61.9% for FY26); domestic was 37% in Q4 (31.8% for FY26).

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin range of 16-20%, which management expects to reach in FY27.

Fabric capex adds 35 million metres, taking capacity to 75 million metres (errata to 70 million metres as stated), and spinning adds 22,000 tonnes to about 130,000 tonnes. Commissioning in H2 FY27: fabric from October-December 2026 and spinning from January-February 2027.

Capex of about INR1,000-1,100 crore is expected to add more than INR1,000 crore to top line. Normalisation of yarn prices may add 5-7% to existing turnover. Management expects 30-35% revenue growth on the existing base over time.

Renewable power: about 75 MW added including PPAs, reaching close to 100 MW installed. A 10 MW hybrid PPA is due by Q3 FY27. Expected savings of INR50 crore per year at full run-rate, with INR30-35 crore in the current year.
Total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crore after commissioning, including working capital. Average borrowing cost about 5.6%, working capital under 7%, blended about 6.5%.
Asset turn of about 1.2-1.3x at company level; new capex expected at about 1:1 excluding renewable capex.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion adds 35 million metres (to about 75 million metres, errata). Spinning adds 22,000 tonnes (to about 130,000 tonnes). Commissioning in H2 FY27.

Over INR300 crore spent so far, including about INR140 crore in capital advances, about INR55-60 crore capitalised from modernisation and balancing, and capital WIP of about INR100 crore. The balance is to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Additional energy capex of about INR230-240 crore, not planned before last year. Renewable power capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme incentives include capital subsidy (about 20-27% of eligible investment, paid over 10 years), interest subsidy (5% of term loan or 2.5% of eligible fixed investment, whichever is lower, for 5 years), plus electricity duty and mandi tax rebates. Management did not quantify the total.
demand_pricing: Demand improved in Q4 FY26 in both domestic and export markets, driven by US tariff removal, downstream restocking and longer transit times. Management said exports of about 100 million kg of yarn a year are steady, with a possible 5-10% increase.

Yarn spread (realisation over cotton) rose to about INR120-125/kg from about INR110/kg last quarter. Management called INR120-125 the median and said it should be sustainable, with a minimum of INR100/kg against an earlier floor of INR90/kg.
Polyester prices rose more than 20% after the West Asia conflict, but synthetic yarn spreads stayed flat. Blended yarn margins improved marginally.

Cotton: domestic prices were INR52,000-55,000 per candy in the lowest period, around 4 years low, and have been rising since recent weeks. Duty on imported cotton was removed Aug-Dec 2025; the industry is asking for a repeat removal.
Fabric prices lag yarn: the company has already raised fabric prices, and management expects further improvement. The India-UK and India-EU FTAs are expected to add European and UK orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised yarn spread and margin, excluding inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spread was about INR90/kg at the low end historically and about INR140-150/kg at the high end; a minimum of INR100/kg is now the floor, and INR120-125/kg is sustainable. Last year's margin at INR110 was about 11.5-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the freight and gas cost impacts from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sea freight is up 75-80% and other regions 15-20% versus February, but freight is normally passed on under FOB terms and has normalised since March. Gas-based yarn is a very small share, with under a day of disruption and gas costs up about 1.7x since February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the duty removal on cotton and the top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty removal is up to the government, with a possible permanent fix in 5-6 months. Top-line growth is expected from the INR1,000 crore+ capex, yarn normalisation (5-7%) and recovery, for 30-35% growth on the existing base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the fabric and knitted utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Knitted utilisation is expected to recover to the normal 65-70% within 1-1.5 years, as US tariffs were reduced from 50%. Some customers were lost to competing countries and are being regained.

risks_watch: Cotton import duty status and cotton availability. The industry wants duty removed; government has not committed to a timeline.
West Asia conflict: transit times up about 2 weeks, sea freight volatile, and polyester and gas costs rising. Management says these are passed on, but synthetic spreads have not widened.
Capex execution: commissioning slips from H2 FY27, and ramp-up of new fabric and yarn capacity. Management said it can increase the reach of fabric to European and UK buyers under the FTAs.
Knitted fabric utilisation is well below normal, at the 65-70% benchmark, and customers were lost in the US tariff period.
Future capex plans are not yet quantified. Management declined to give future capex or fabric margin targets.
532698|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the near-term outlook, with management pointing to a record quarter, a 124 bps margin gain and firm yarn spreads. Cautious where the questions turned to the war, cotton duty and timing of FTAs, and it declined to give timelines for government action or future capex.
key_quotes: This is our highest ever quarterly revenue, driven by improvement in demand and yarn prices.
As regards to the present ongoing capex, the plan is progressing very well. It is expected to commercialize in second half of FY '27.
So instead of per unit capex, we need to look at what is the total saving which we can generate out of this.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, yarn spread is INR120-125/kg vs about INR110/kg last quarter, and management guides a normalised 16-20% margin in FY27 with renewable savings of INR30-35 crore this year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spinning at 98%+ utilisation and woven fabric at 90%+; 35m metres fabric and 22,000 t spinning (to ~130,000 t, +20%) are under construction with commissioning dates set, though fabric and spinning start is the second half of the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Spinning capacity goes from about 110,000 t to about 130,000 t (+20%) and fabric to about 75 million metres (+35m) in H2 FY27, with exports steady at about 100 million kg of yarn a year and a possible 5-10% increase.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has not quantified future capex and declined to give a timeline, but utilisation at 98% spinning and 90%+ woven means a further expansion could follow once the current INR1,000-1,100 crore programme is commissioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects 30-35% revenue uplift on the existing base and a yarn floor of INR100/kg (vs INR90/kg earlier), but no contracted orders are cited and the uplift timing is open-ended.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cotton duty and cotton availability are unresolved, West Asia freight and gas costs are rising (Europe sea freight up 75-80% vs February), and capex commissioning could slip from H2 FY27.

rows.label: Yarn spread floor raised to INR100/kg
rows.why: Spread at INR120-125/kg, median and sustainable per management, versus a floor of INR90/kg earlier and INR110/kg last quarter.

rows.label: India-UK and India-EU FTAs adding European and UK orders
rows.why: Management expects FTAs to add European and UK orders, but no timing or order value was given, and FTA timing was one of the topics where management was cautious.

rows.label: Renewable power savings INR50 crore a year at full run-rate
rows.why: About 75 MW added via PPAs to reach close to 100 MW installed, with a 10 MW hybrid PPA due by Q3 FY27, and the capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q4 (INR859.8 crore revenue, 15.17% margin) and the 16-20% normalised margin, but cautious and non-committal on the war, cotton duty, FTA timing and future capex; analysts probed these areas.

532698|2026-06.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.
532698|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR875 crore was the company's highest ever quarter for a second straight quarter, up 10.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, driven mainly by yarn realisations. EBITDA before other income was INR155.6 crore (+39.85% YoY), with margin at 17.78% versus 14.02% a year earlier and 15.17% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. Management guided that the new capacities (fabric +35 million metres, spinning +74,000 spindles) will add INR200-300 crore revenue in the near term, though the commissioning timeline has since been reset.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. Management said yarn price increases outpaced cotton, and a fall in outside yarn sales was due to higher in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 92%. Fabric margins have not expanded like yarn; pass-through is only of actual cotton increases. Fabric revenue was about INR700 crore plus in FY26 and is about 20-21% of revenue, targeted at about 30% after expansion.

segments.name: Knitted fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 55-60%, below the pre-US-tariff norm of 60-65%, because of US tariff uncertainty; the US had been a major market for knit fabric.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay in the company's 16-20% band; management said it aims for the upper end but gave no firm guidance on reaching it. Management said it expects current margins to be maintained, and declined to comment on improvement.

Renewable power capacity expected operational by end Q3 FY27; management estimates about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit, with about INR1.2-1.5 crore already in Q1 and an analyst assumption of about INR12.5 crore per quarter from Q4.
Blended power cost expected around INR5.50/unit once solar covers about 60% of requirements.

New capacity: weaving starts in about two months, processing in about 1.5 months later (around Diwali), spinning on stream by about December; utilisation to ramp to 31 March 2027, with fabric 100% ramp taking a quarter or two into FY28.

Expansion adds about INR1,000-1,100 crore of turnover at full run-rate, of which about INR500 crore is fabric (FY28 fabric revenue targeted at INR1,200 crore) and yarn about 40% for external sale; management said incremental fabric revenue is 'not factoring in' the price volatility.
Management said no new capex is planned until after FY28 beyond the announced expansion.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion of 35 million metres (weaving plus finishing; solid and yarn-dyed fabrics; no printing capacity added).
Spinning expansion of 74,000 spindles; about 22,000 metric tons of new yarn capacity, of which 16,000-18,000 MT goes into fabric and some to yarn dyeing.
Capex of about INR1,100 crore; Rajasthan textile scheme incentives apply, with capital subsidy booked in other income.
Renewable power expansion on schedule for end Q3 FY27.
Spinning utilisation 98%; woven fabric utilisation over 92%; knit fabric 55-60%.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about 8-10% in Q1 on lower global output and West Asia-related logistics issues; India removed cotton import duty.
Indian cotton had been priced above the Cotlook index in 2023-24 (about +5-7%); it now trades at about -1 to -2% versus Cotlook, a delta of about 7-8 points.
Indian yarn exports to China rose to about 110-115 million kg in CY26 from 90-100 million kg in 2025; management sees China's import demand continuing.
Management said spinning capacity exits in the last 1-2 years and the post-US-tariff demand slump have rebalanced supply.

Volumes: management said yarn outside sales fell because of in-house consumption by fabric units and about some stock held at quarter-end due to vessel shortages; these were said to have dispatched in July.
Price pass-through: yarn price increases exceeded cotton increases (management cited about 120-125% pass-through on a 100% cotton increase); fabric pass-through is only 1:1 on cotton.
India crop: about 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26, versus 326-327 lakh bales in 2024-25; 2026-27 acreage about 0.5-1% lower; rainfall over the next month is the key factor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the yarn spreads in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about INR110 in the last quarter of FY26 and are now about INR130, and management said this is sustained at current conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Are current margins of 17-18% sustainable for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to maintain the current level, with cost savings helping, but declined to comment on any further improvement or on a decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 EBITDA expansion is from power savings, realisation, and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Power savings contributed about 0.5% of EBITDA and a similar amount from solar; the gross margin rise to about 40% came mainly from yarn realisation. Inventory gains were described as very small, and the working capital cycle is broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What share of new capacity revenue goes to fabric, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600-plus crore of the expansion's turnover is fabric, with yarn ramp-up complete by 31 March 2027 and fabric taking a quarter or two more into FY28; fabric revenue is expected at INR1,200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, as it is in a growth phase funding capex through internal accruals and loans, so a buyback would not be prudent now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning garmenting or home textiles as the next growth leg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said garmenting is only an idea with nothing firmed up, and home textiles and garmenting are both seen as equally good opportunities, with Europe the key opening for home textiles after the US slump.

risks_watch: Commissioning timeline: weaving in about two months, processing about 1.5 months later, spinning by about December; fabric ramp-up may take a quarter or two into FY28 (management also cited 6-8 months for fabric ramp-up in one answer).

Cotton price volatility and pass-through: fabric margins expand only 1:1 with cotton, while yarn spread (about INR130/kg) is sustained only under current conditions; management declined to commit to margin levels beyond maintaining current ones.
US tariff uncertainty keeps knitted fabric utilisation at about 55-60% versus 60-65% pre-tariff norm; knit fabric exposure to the US remains a drag.
Monsoon/rainfall over the next month will determine the 2026-27 Indian cotton crop size; quality outlook depends on the same.
Yarn outside-sales volumes fell QoQ and YoY due to in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit; shipment logistics (vessel availability) to be monitored for July dispatches.

Renewable power capacity due by end Q3 FY27; about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit is management's estimate, and the blended power cost target of about INR5.50/unit depends on solar covering about 60% of requirements.
key_quotes: So there is no issue at all for absorbing the yarn capacity.
Improvement I cannot comment upon at this point of time.
We are expecting same. In view of the cost initial cost saving initiatives going forward which is also going to kick in and also the margins looking reasonable.
It is always the endeavour of the management to go to the upper level of the band which we have discussed and that is a continuous effort.
We are not able to improve upon the margins as we are able to improve upon the margins in the yarn business.

Cautious and evasive on forward margins: it would only say it expects to maintain current levels, declined to comment on improvement or on any decline, and gave no firm timeline for reaching the upper end of the 16-20% band.

532699|2026-03.headline: Royal Orchid FY26 consolidated revenue rose to INR384 crore and EBITDA to INR110 crore, but ICONIQA Mumbai's Ind AS hit cut PAT to INR33 crore; management gave no FY27 guidance.
532699|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations rose to INR384 crore from INR319 crore, with EBITDA of INR110 crore and PAT of INR33 crore after exceptional items (EPS INR11.74). Management said PAT growth excluding ICONIQA Mumbai was about 16.8%, with ICONIQA's first-year Ind AS hit of about INR15-16 crore (notional) and INR7.5 crore of pre-operating expense write-offs weighing on reported profit. Management said the West Asia conflict hit March cancellations and April-May ADR and occupancy, and declined to give FY27 or FY28 revenue and EBITDA guidance, saying it would revisit after Q1. A final dividend of INR2.5 per share was recommended.

financial_highlights.change: PAT growth excluding ICONIQA stated at about 16.8%

segments.commentary: Revenue about INR55-56 crore and EBITDA about INR20 crore for FY26, which an analyst said is roughly flat versus last year. Management did not give a FY27 segment outlook.

segments.commentary: EBITDA about INR103 crore. Managed hotels existing last year run at about 67-68% occupancy, and the blended managed occupancy of about 62% reflects new openings.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance; management will revisit after Q1 FY27.
Management says FY27 will be a better year than FY26 and that more hotels will be added in FY27 than in FY26.
