Management cited the IndiGo disruption (about 15 days of lower occupancy across the group), Middle East carriers (about 40% of inbound India share) disrupted by the war, rising costs and labour codes, and tile supply delays from Morbi due to the LPG crisis.
Management said the last month post-war had hit ADR and occupancy and that costs were rising, including labour wages and fuel.

qa_highlights.question: Strategic levers for FY27 expansion, growth corridors and asset-light versus own-property balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 52 signed hotels (about 3,600 keys), a beefed-up development team, and inbound approaches from owners. The model is mostly managed, with some franchise and flexi-lease (revenue share with minimum guarantee).

qa_highlights.question: Debt and refinancing frameworks, given consolidated PAT of about INR25.11 crore for 9M FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cash is about INR100 crore including the associate, bank borrowings about INR91 crore (including INR45 crore for ICONIQA), and the company could become debt-free at once. Funds are earmarked for flexi-lease capex.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia crisis on Q4 and ICONIQA, and medium-term FY27-28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given because of geopolitical uncertainty. Management said the last month post-war had hurt ADR and occupancy, and it will revisit after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why take small managed hotels (e.g. a 70-key Hyderabad hotel) and what is the managed-segment profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said there are per-hotel minimum monthly fee thresholds, rising yearly. Portfolio brands are Regenta (60-80+ keys), Regenta Place (40-80) and Z by Regenta (about 50 keys, franchise). Chairman said scale matters, with about 100 hotels at INR3-5 lakh per month each.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash PAT inflect, and could it reach INR100 crore by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited cash growth and said FY26 PAT was hit by ICONIQA's notional Ind AS charge. Chairman declined to give forward-looking statements on cash PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ICONIQA's EBITDA swing small after INR7 crore of top-line growth, and when does it become PAT-profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said launch and marketing costs (classified as operating expense) drove the weak EBITDA. Management expects PAT positive in FY27-28 excluding notional Ind AS, but PAT likely negative in FY27 including it.

risks_watch: Auditor disagreement led to INR5.5 crore of pre-operating expenses (plus INR2 crore earlier) being written off; management said all write-offs are now taken.
Revenue-share ramp-up (about 522 keys) depends on owner construction, which is affected by cost increases, Morbi tile shortages and LPG disruption; no opening dates given.
Ind AS notional charge on ICONIQA will weigh on PAT in FY27.
Managed-segment earnings flat in FY26; minimum-fee and portfolio restructuring is planned.
Management flagged proposed minimum-wage increases and the new labour code as cost risks.
Hampton by Hilton ramp-up and key count not quantified; first signings expected in FY27.

532699|2026-06.headline: Royal Orchid Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, but PAT fell to INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore.
532699|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, with EBITDA up 39% to about INR 33 crore and margin at roughly 30.7% versus 30%. Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

segments.commentary: Occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 vs INR 5,488 a year earlier. These hotels account for the bulk of revenue; ICONIQA is the newest asset, opened November 2025.

segments.name: Managed and franchised portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said April was about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%; Q4 about 80%. Q1 is seasonally weak and the war hit inbound travel. August occupancy was hit by heavy Mumbai rains.

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said no date is committed for INR 150 crore; fees grew about 14% last year, and the company aims to double fees as quickly as possible.

532700|2026-03.headline: ENIL FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3.9% to INR565 crore; digital grew 84% to INR112.4 crore while Q4 non-FCT weakened on war-related event disruptions.
532700|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was INR565 crore (+3.9% YoY), with domestic revenue up 4% to INR548 crore led by digital. EBITDA excluding digital was INR76 crore (18% margin) and PAT excluding digital was INR22 crore, which includes a INR17.2 crore one-time gain from reversing deferred tax liability under the Finance Act 2026. Radio faced subdued demand and the Middle East conflict hurt international operations, while non-FCT grew strongly in the first nine months but was hit in Q4 by cancelled international artist concerts. Management reiterated that Gaana should reach breakeven in FY27 and recommended a dividend of INR2 per share.

financial_highlights.value: INR22 crore (includes INR17.2 crore one-time deferred tax reversal)

segments.name: Radio (FCT)
segments.commentary: Demand stayed subdued through FY26 amid macro uncertainty and the Middle East conflict; volume market share cited at 25.2% (25.6% in a later answer). International operations, especially the Middle East, were hit. Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore.

segments.name: Non-FCT (events and experiential)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR148 crore; grew strongly in the first nine months (described as double digit) but Q4 was hit by travel constraints and cancellation of some international artist concerts. Q4 non-FCT revenue was about INR38 crore.

segments.name: Digital (Gaana and pure digital)
segments.commentary: FY26 digital revenue INR112.4 crore (+84%), about 48% of radio revenue. Q4 pure digital revenue about INR29 crore (+61%) per one answer, while Gaana Q4 revenue about INR21 crore (+42%). Gaana revenue has been roughly flat at about INR20 crore in the last two quarters per the analyst; management cited 10-15% sequential growth from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gaana: management targets operating breakeven in FY27, with a possibility of achieving it within FY26 itself; quarterly losses have been reduced sequentially.
Gaana subscriber growth expected to continue at about 15% CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with focus on unit economics over subscriber count.
Gaana pricing: annual plan raised to INR799 from INR499; management sees headroom toward a steady-state price of about INR1,200 a year.
Dividend of INR2 per share recommended for FY26; management said the company will keep evaluating inorganic opportunities.
Radio and experiential business expected to recover; management called the Q4 shortfall momentary.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call.
Radio volume market share cited at 25.2% in prepared remarks and 25.6% in a later answer; management said it may have gained some basis points.
Radio inventory utilisation described as roughly flat quarter on quarter in Q4; effective rates (ERs) said to be at similar levels, not up since COVID.

Non-FCT events and experiential business is the capacity-linked segment; Q4 hit by event disruptions, execution delays and cancelled international artist concerts, with recovery expected from the H2-heavy event calendar.
Digital spend reduced 23% YoY in FY26; management said it would keep investing in digital and evaluating inorganic opportunities, with no specific capex amount given.
demand_pricing: Radio demand subdued through FY26 because of macro uncertainty and the West Asia conflict, which weighed on advertiser sentiment.
Gaana annual subscription raised to INR799 (from INR499); music label variable content cost cited at 60-70% of revenue.
Management said customer acquisition costs have risen across the subscription market; CAC and LTV figures were not disclosed.
Management estimates India's paid music subscribers at about 15 million (from about 8 million two years earlier, per EY-FICCI), against a 80-100 million paid-subscription pool across video/OTT.
Competition from free offerings such as YouTube and bundled products was cited; one competitor cut prices sharply in Q3 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business plan and subscriber trajectory for Gaana over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 15% subscriber CAGR to continue for 2-3 years, prioritises profitable growth over subscriber count, and sees FY27 as the year to reach breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Gaana Q4 and FY26 revenue split, and FCT/non-FCT split?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital revenue in Q4 was about INR21 crore (+42%) and INR81 crore for FY26 (+71%). Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore and non-FCT about INR38 crore. Volume growth was described as flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gaana revenue look flat over the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is seasonal Q3/Q4 churn, that prices were cut and then raised, and that revenue grew about 10-15% sequentially from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose CAC-to-LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share CAC or LTV metrics on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the income tax notice of INR111 crore about?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Ballabh said the notice relates to FY2023-24, with a demand of about INR113 crore after the department passed an order ignoring submissions; the company plans to appeal to the CIT and further authorities and is confident of the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line fall about INR15 crore in Q4 and how is radio doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said radio volume share is about 25.6% and possibly up slightly; the Q4 drop came mainly from non-FCT events after international concerts were cancelled. First nine months of non-FCT grew double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How many paid music subscribers are there and how long to reach the 100 million pool?
qa_highlights.answer: Music paid subscribers are about 15 million per the EY-FICCI report; management said timing depends on behaviour change and could not give a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash deployment or inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will pursue profitable growth rather than burn cash, is evaluating inorganic opportunities, and has kept dividends rising.

risks_watch: Income tax demand of about INR113 crore for FY2023-24 under appeal.
Q4 non-FCT weakness from geopolitical disruption and cancelled international artist concerts; watch recovery in events revenue.
Gaana Q4 sequential growth was modest, and CAC is rising; breakeven in FY27 depends on subscriber growth and pricing.
Middle East international radio operations remain disrupted.

532725|2026-06.headline: Solar Industries to acquire Omnia Holdings (South Africa) on an all-cash, 100% basis, funded by debt; ~$1.35bn deal value cited, FY28 leverage target below 2x EBITDA.

Management guided to combined FY28 revenue of about INR30,000-32,000 crore and EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore, and said net debt/EBITDA will stay below 2x. 532726|2026-06.headline: Gallantt Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 203 crore (18% margin) from INR 254 crore a year ago, though flat sequentially, on coal costs and a pellet plant shutdown.
532726|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2% year-on-year to INR 1,146 crore but fell from INR 1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was INR 203 crore (18% margin) versus INR 209 crore in Q4 and INR 254 crore in Q1 FY26, and PAT was INR 124 crore (11% margin). Management attributed the year-on-year decline to higher raw material costs (up 9%), the planned pellet plant shutdown, a seasonal monsoon-driven TMT price correction, and higher employee costs. The 1.23 million tonne capacity expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively.

qa_highlights.question: What is the iron ore and pellet sourcing strategy, and who are the top suppliers?
qa_highlights.answer: Gorakhpur sources iron ore fines from Odisha Mineral Corporation, multiple Madhya Pradesh concentrate suppliers and Lloyds (Maharashtra), mixed on price and quality. Gorakhpur coal for power is 100% Indian linkage coal; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian with the rest South African via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal via Mundra/Kandla for power and South African coal for process.

qa_highlights.question: Does high-phosphorus iron ore from Lloyds pose a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Lloyds supplies only low-phosphorus material, about 15-20% of the mix, roughly 15,000 tonnes a month. Pellet plant capacity is about 8 lakh tonnes against 9-9.5 lakh tonnes of raw feed a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and funding, and how will UP market share and adjacent expansion be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 3,000 crore, with about INR 800 crore spent so far; half goes to mining, with 85 MW solar and the 0.23 million tonne capacity addition in H2 FY27. All funded by internal accruals with no term loans. Management claims over 25% share of the addressable UP market and uses celebrity branding (Ajay Devgn, now Janhvi Kapoor), with other markets to follow as capacity grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports a realistic avenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a focus. Construction steel is logistically hard to export and Gorakhpur is inland; Gujarat billets are exported only occasionally.

qa_highlights.question: What drives margins and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have stayed around 17-18% across FY26 quarters, driven by pellet-to-TMT integration and no term debt. Management says margins are sustainable, with solar and FY28 captive mines expected to improve them.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat-product import pressure affecting long products, and what is the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat-product price pressure spills over to long products to some extent. Management expects 8-9% steel demand growth, sees Q1 and Q2 as muted by monsoon, and expects pick-up from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the captive iron ore mine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Exploration in UP is expected to finish in 2-3 months and in Rajasthan in about six months. Management reiterated that all three mines should commission in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact and outlook on iron ore and coal?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs rose 9% YoY, about half of which relates to the pellet plant shutdown; 4-5% is price-driven across iron ore and coal. Coal is the main driver, with iron ore impacted mainly by sea freight; management sees no substantial EBITDA erosion for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per tonne fall, and is it one-off or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with the historical 17-18% range. FY26 EBITDA per tonne was about INR 8,800 and it is about INR 8,700 now, so the decline is attributed to pressure rather than structural change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue growth slow, and will volumes return to double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the YoY revenue decline as marginal, about 2-2.5%. It expects volumes to be much higher once the H2 FY27 capacity comes in.

532726|2026-09.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.
532726|2026-09.overview: Revenue held at INR1,146 crores, up 13% year on year and flat quarter on quarter, as realisations offset lower volumes. TMT sales fell to 1,65,000 tons from about 1,92,000 tons in Q1 because of a planned Gorakhpur shutdown, and an unplanned extension of a captive power plant outage raised power costs. EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. Coal block allotment in Singrauli and a medium-term greenfield growth plan (to be presented in Q4 FY27) were the main strategic updates.

segments.name: Gorakhpur (UP) integrated plant
segments.commentary: Planned shutdown to integrate expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026, with 85-90% utilisation targeted by end-December. The captive power plant (78 MW, plus 22 MW being added) had an extended turbine-related outage, restart expected within a week.

segments.name: Kutch (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Rolling mill utilisation 68% in Q2 vs 66% in Q1, a 2 percentage point rise. Management expects further structural improvement in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Captive power and renewables
segments.commentary: 18 MW solar at Siddhpur, Gujarat, complete and due to resume by November 2026; 60 MW solar at Prayagraj for Gorakhpur due Q4 FY27. Together expected to save INR30-40 crores per year in power cost.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 recovery expected from Gorakhpur capacity, power plant restart and firmer steel prices; management says price increase of about 20-21% (TMT, September vs a year ago) only reflected from September, so benefit lands mainly in Q3.
Working capital (inventory) expected to normalise in Q3 once new Gorakhpur capacity is operational within 15-20 days.

Remaining FY27 capex of around INR500 crores, split INR400 crores Gorakhpur, INR240 crores mines, INR170 crores solar and INR100 crores Kutch, all to be funded from internal accruals. Note the split sums to more than INR500 crores as stated on the call.
Iron ore blocks targeted operational in FY28; captive mines expected to add about INR2,000 per ton to EBITDA once fully utilised, with partial feed in the first one to two years.
Medium-term greenfield growth plan, built around iron ore and coal blocks, to be presented in Q4 FY27; funding mix (internal accruals vs debt/equity) not yet decided.
Management expects utilisation to improve by 3-5% next year as shutdowns are synchronised and capacity is added.
capex_capacity: Gorakhpur expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026. Management also referenced a 1.3 million ton annual target. Gorakhpur capacity addition at every stage except sponge iron, including 22 MW additional generation to the 78 MW captive plant.

Singrauli coal block allotted August 2026; due diligence under way with a one-month decision window. Operations would take about 2-3 years after a decision; Gorakhpur intended to move fully to this coal, replacing imported South African coal.
Iron ore blocks in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan: exploration in progress, environment and forest clearances underway, FY28 target.
Gujarat: captive power debottlenecking completed in the last month (results in Q3); sponge iron (DRI) plant to commission in Q4 FY27, with benefits from next financial year.
Power outsourcing after the 22 MW addition is about 5-7 MW, to be covered by the 60 MW Prayagraj solar plant in Q4; until then 5-6 MW bought from grid and exchange.
demand_pricing: Management says India finished steel consumption grew 7.5% to about 85 million tons in H1; construction steel demand up about 7% per management. India remained a net importer of finished steel.

TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago; management says finished product prices rose about 20% while raw material cost rose about INR3,000 per ton in Q2 (coal about INR2,500 per ton, iron ore about 1%).
Brand premium: management says it commands 5-6% over unbranded TMT in UP and 3-4% in Gujarat; Ajay Devgn endorsement (four years) and Janhvi Kapoor recently added.
Gallantt Advance submersible: more than 25% share of the submersible market in UP, per management.
Management expects prices to stay firm into the November-December construction peak, though part of the price gain is being passed on to energy costs.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Singrauli coal block mean strategically and how does it change cost position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the block was only just allotted and is in due diligence; iron ore blocks are targeted for FY28, and securing both raw materials is a basis for the next growth phase.

qa_highlights.question: How will the medium-term growth plan be funded: internal accruals or debt and equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Vice Chairman Dindayal Jalan said the mix is undecided and depends on project size; the company historically relies on internal accruals and limited external borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are TMT prices into the construction season, and what is seen in October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects prices to remain strong as construction peaks from November-December, with some part of the gain absorbed by energy costs. Price rise came mainly in September, so the effect lands in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 margin fall is due to shutdowns versus input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both shutdowns and coal price increases (about 4.5-5% of revenue) with realisations lagging; the price rise only came through in September, so Q2 saw little benefit.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the price premium over unbranded TMT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 5-6% premium in UP and 3-4% in Gujarat, sustained by branding and dealer network.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise by about INR118 crores in H1 and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build came from the prolonged shutdown during hookup of new capacity and stock built to supply added capacity; expected to normalise in Q3 once the plant is running.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining FY27 capex and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jalan said about INR500 crores remains for FY27 (INR400 crores Gorakhpur, INR240 crores mines, INR170 crores solar, INR100 crores Kutch), funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will Gorakhpur ramp up and what utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up takes one to one-and-a-half months to reach 85-90% utilisation; start proposed 10 November, so stable running by December end.

532734|2026-03.headline: GPIL FY26 consolidated EBITDA flat at INR 1,253 crore, but Q4 EBITDA rose 91% QoQ to INR 439 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%.
532734|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and PAT were broadly stable, with consolidated PAT at INR 802 crore and EBITDA margin at 23%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 41% QoQ and PAT reached INR 280 crore, driven by higher pellet volumes, a one-time carry-over pellet inventory gain (about INR 20 crore) and March mining uplift after environmental clearance for Ari Dongri. Consolidated PAT was below standalone because Ardent Steel was de-recognised as an associate after the stake sale. Management guided FY27 revenue above INR 6,000 crore and EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels, while flagging price softness of about 10% in late April and early May.

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri / Boria Tibu)
segments.commentary: FY26 mining achieved 92% of target; FY26 mining was about 2.7-2.8 million tons versus 2.35-2.4 million tons in FY25. FY27 usable ore guidance is 3.4 million tons (4-4.25 million tons mined, including about 0.5 million tons from Boria Tibu).

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: FY26 pellet output reached 95% of target. Pellet capacity rose from 2.7 to 4.7 million tons after the 2 million ton gas-based grate-kiln plant commissioned in December 2025; FY27 pellet guidance is 4 million tons, with about 3 million tons for merchant sales.

segments.name: Sponge iron
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26. Capacity is being expanded from 0.59 to 0.65 million tons under a CTO received from CECB.

segments.name: Structural rolled products / RR Ispat
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26 and rose sharply from Q4 after mill modifications finished at end-Q3; order book is about six months. Total FY27 rolled output is guided at about 3.7-3.75 lakh tons.

segments.name: Ferroalloys
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26; no further figures given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanised / fabricated products and billets
segments.commentary: Billets reached 96% of target in FY26; sales volumes for galvanised fabricated products increased over the year.

segments.name: BESS (20 GWh project)
segments.commentary: Commissioning targeted March 2027, with long-term supply tie-ups with EVE Power (628 Ah LFP cells) and Shanghai Shenyi Roche. Phase-1 ramp is 5-6 GWh in FY28 (30-40%), about 12-14 GWh in FY29 and 17-18 GWh from FY30. Management guided a 7-8% margin, but said current margins are about 12-13%.

segments.name: CRM complex (0.7 million tons)
segments.commentary: Targeted commissioning March 2027; FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation, or 3-3.5 lakh tons. Management expects about 90% from FY29.

FY27 EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels; management said it expects to maintain about 25%.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant (6 million tons) to be commissioned by Q3 FY27; full-scale mining of 6 million tons in FY28, with about 4.5 million tons of usable ore.

qa_highlights.answer: Carry-over pellet inventory of about 89,000 tons sold in Q4, the new pellet plant ramp to 70% and about 2-2.5 lakh extra tons of mining in March after EC approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS margin and the lithium cost pass-through?

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel plant capex rise to INR 7,000 crore from the earlier INR 4,000 crore estimate?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CRM and FY28 utilisation outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company export pellets?

532734|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew both YoY and QoQ on higher volumes and better realisations, while EBITDA and PAT were broadly flat YoY and down sequentially on input costs. Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.
Boria Tibbu mine (0.7 mtpa now) expansion to 4 mtpa targeted for FY31, with a 4 mtpa beneficiation plant yielding 1.5-2 mt concentrate (about 40% yield). TOFR filing pending.
demand_pricing: Iron ore prices (global) expected to hover around USD90-100/t; management said it does not expect prices to fall below USD90 soon. Domestic ex-mine iron ore about INR5,500/t.

Industry pellet utilisation is about 65%, held back by lower exports, limited high-grade supply and margin pressure. Indian pellet production was about 120 mt in FY26, up from 109 mt in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Milestones needed before the board revives the 1 mtpa integrated steel plant, and should it now be treated as optional growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Water allocation is the gating item: an LOI was received but the confirmation letter has stalled, delaying the ~9.4 MCM allocation by 6-8 months. Management said to treat the steel plant as an option for medium-term growth, and that Vision 2030 was restated without it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mining production shortfall continue into Q2 and Q3, and when does merchant ore purchasing fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Government land approval for dumping (tree cutting) is expected by end-September, with Q2 mining at the same level as Q1. Mining ramps from Q3 and reaches full capacity by end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28. Merchant ore purchases stay at 25-30% in Q3, fall below 10% in Q4, and reach 100% captive in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the pellet plant shut, and is the gas issue expected to normalise after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas is fully supplied, but the PNGRB guideline has pushed gas purchase value up about 40-45%. Combined with market ore purchases, this made the plant commercially unviable, so one 2 mtpa plant was shut. No clarity on normalisation was given; GAIL has no guidelines, and August is expected to remain a shutdown month.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for iron ore and pellet prices, and what is the sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global iron ore is expected to hover at USD90-100/t, with management not expecting a fall below USD90 soon. Pellet prices were about INR10,000/t after a roughly 10% recovery from the early-July low of about INR8,700/t. Each INR100/t fall in pellet price cuts annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA benefit per tonne do beneficiation, EV fleet and mining cost cuts deliver from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining cost is INR3,000-3,500/t now, with a target below INR2,700/t from FY28. Each INR100/t saving on about 5-6 mt of ore is worth about INR45-50 crore EBITDA. Pellet output is expected to reach about 4.5 mt in FY28, and selling surplus ore is not planned in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised CRM capex, and what incentives and margins are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CRM capex rose to about INR1,100 crore from INR900-950 crore, which includes working capital margin money. The land is about INR50 crore for 35 acres. Management said incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from 7-8%. Commissioning is December 2027.

The pellet plant shutdown: restart is uncertain, with August expected to stay shut and September possible for the third plant. Gas prices are up about 40-45% under PNGRB guidance and there is no supplier clarity from GAIL.

Capex visibility: no FY29 projection given, and the BESS (commissioning Q1 FY28) and CRM (December 2027) timelines have slipped in the past. The BESS commercial ramp depends on tender wins.

532735|2026-03.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.
532735|2026-03.overview: Revenue grew 3.5% QoQ and 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore ($62.8 million), with Novigo consolidated for a full quarter and rupee depreciation supporting the numbers. Management said organic revenue was flat QoQ, citing fewer days and Q4 fixed-price true-ups, and that Novigo's restated revenue is about $21–22 million a year after accounting alignment versus the roughly $32 million quoted at acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 115.7 crore (20.1% margin), which management said is about 19% excluding the currency benefit. Utilisation was deliberately reduced to about 80.5% (from a peak of about 84%) to build AI and data bench and COE capacity. Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.

About 29% of revenue comes from AI and AI-enabled services (management noted this is not system-tracked).

Average deal sizes said to be rising for R Systems as end-to-end transformation deals replace feature-level work, even as AI lowers effort per deal (example: a 3-million-line legacy migration at about $1 million, versus $1.5–2 million traditionally).
Over 90% of revenue is discretionary project spend; a Novigo cross-sell pipeline includes close to a dozen joint deals and three clients receiving R Systems delivery.
Token costs for client output are borne by the client in almost all cases; R Systems bears its own token costs for training and R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI in SDLC threaten growth, and how will frontier-model firms entering IT services affect R Systems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI in SDLC expands the addressable market for a projects-based business with over 90% discretionary revenue; deal sizes per unit of work fall, but TAM expansion more than compensates. It views the frontier-lab services move as validation that AI is a people problem, and will assess competition as it develops.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q1 growth mainly from full-quarter Novigo consolidation, and is organic growth returning from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Novigo's accounting was aligned to R Systems policies, moving some licence revenue from gross to net and changing fixed-price accounting. Restated Novigo revenue is about $21–22 million a year versus about $32 million at acquisition. Organic growth was flat QoQ, attributed to fewer days and Q4 true-ups, and management said it sees no challenge to positive outlook for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Blackstone and Anthropic consulting venture: threat to mid-market players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the venture as early-stage and as validation of its playbooks; Blackstone portfolio access gives a faster path to some companies, but deals are still won on merit against competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A fall, and what is the normal run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop from INR 114.3 crore to INR 91.4 crore reflected reversal of a conservative AR provision after collections and year-end provision true-up, not lower investment. Normal run rate is about USD 11 million a quarter versus USD 10 million in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is organic growth and the FY outlook, and how is Novigo contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was flat in Q1, but it does not give forward guidance; it pointed to new wins and expects EBITDA margins to be sustained. Novigo cross-selling is active across close to a dozen deals.

qa_highlights.question: How are GCCs and token costs affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: R Systems has helped about 8–9 mid-market clients set up GCCs since launching the service about six quarters ago, which it sees as a growth lever. Token costs for client output are mostly borne by clients, and Optima AI FinOps tooling is used to meter them.

532755|2026-03.headline: Tech Mahindra Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.4% cc YoY to USD 1,625M, with EBIT margin at 13.8% and FY27 targets of 15% EBIT reiterated.

Full-year FY26 revenue was USD 6,385M (+0.6% cc) and operating margin expanded 290 bps to 12.6%. Deal wins for the year reached USD 3.79B (+42% YoY) and the company reiterated FY27 targets of above-peer-average organic cc growth and a 15% EBIT margin. The analyst day framed AI as a modernization opportunity and highlighted Orion, Helix and a new pricing model, but did not report a standalone AI revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: How achievable is FY27 outperformance versus peers when peers guide to slowing growth, and what is industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an improving exit trajectory, deal conversion and existing book expansion for confidence. It estimated industry growth at roughly 2%-4% or 3%-5%, and noted some clients may make discretionary cuts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 margin expansion is cost-led versus growth-led, and how do mega-deal margins compare with older vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said the cost/growth split is revised through the year and plans rely less on growth. As-sold margins on the large deals are accretive at portfolio level, per the board review.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with frontier model companies' agents, and how is it differentiated in BFSI and retail where its exposure is smaller?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said Orion focuses on agent orchestration and interoperability across agents. Mohit said focus is on four BFSI sub-areas (payments, asset and wealth, insurance, core banking), with industry experts hired, and cited retail CPG as a strong performer.

qa_highlights.question: Have clients delayed decisions or pushed for price deflation after the February Claude releases?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said there was no significant delay in large-deal signings. Some clients asked for higher outer-year productivity, but this was not common.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin of safety in the FY27 growth assumptions given telecom client pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said growth is linked to industry growth, and that the company's telecom business spans over 100 operators, plus BPS, network services and Comviva, which reduces single-client dependence.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth rely on telecom mega deals, and how will the company diversify away from telecom?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said the portfolio is diversifying into aerospace and defence, BFSI and retail CPG, and that pipeline BFSI and manufacturing deals should add meaningfully as they ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between fixed-price and T&M, and how will surplus margin be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said the gap is about 8%. The fixed-price margin improvement is the main lever for next year. Priorities for surplus are AI investment and growth.

532755|2026-06.headline: Tech Mahindra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.66bn with operating margin at 14.4%, and deal wins hit US$1.078bn.
532755|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 2.2% QoQ and 6.1% YoY in reported USD (6.6% YoY constant currency), with every vertical growing YoY. EBIT margin rose 60 bps QoQ and 330 bps YoY to 14.4%, led by volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partly offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix. Management said Q1 was stronger than expected, helped by early delivery on a European automotive programme that it expects to reverse in Q2. Management reiterated its FY27 ambition of growth above the peer average and an operating margin of 15%, with Q4 margin expected above 15%.

financial_highlights.change: +16.2% YoY in USD; PAT margin +80 bps YoY

segments.commentary: Grew 8.6% YoY; management described the macro as mixed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: growth above the peer average (management said it is already ahead in Q1) and an operating margin of 15%; management said Q4 margin must be above 15%.
Q2 growth expected to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months; the European auto acceleration will create about a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure in Q2.
Wage increases to take effect from Q2 in a phased manner.
Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing volatility; it said it expects to exceed peer-average growth, by an amount it did not quantify.

Margin levers: Project Fortius (fixed-price productivity, T&M utilisation) and SG&A savings from portfolio company consolidation. Management also flagged wage bill increases and AI-driven productivity pressure as headwinds.
capex_capacity: Communications experience centre in Pune opened in April 2026, with more than 10 executive sessions held in its first two months.
Management said it is investing in centres of excellence in Hyderabad (learning, engineering, retail CPG) and will calibrate investment to growth opportunities.
Investing in talent, IP and software licences; deals are screened to be margin-accretive over the long term.
Headcount in IT services fell 7% YoY because of AI-led productivity gains in fixed-price work. Management expects hiring to resume in the rest of FY27, mixing fresh and experienced talent.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,078 million, with the largest coming from manufacturing and HLS. Management said the pipeline looks strong but that large deals are binary and hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two.

Demand strengthening in ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and data and AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI). Weakness seen in manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM and legacy infrastructure admin.

Management walked away from deals with 70%-80% productivity benefits over 5-7 year contracts and from fixed price guarantees on infrastructure, citing memory and chip price inflation of about 20% YoY.
Auto sector: some customers are cutting costs with AI. Auto finance was resilient. Aerospace demand is rising, especially in IT and engineering.

BPS: AI operations made up most of the BPS deal TCV this quarter, including a large AI-led engagement with a high-tech client. Some clients are questioning in-house versus outsourcing decisions on multi-year deals, but management said it is not seeing outsized delays or cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth momentum carry into Q2 without the Comviva seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months, offset by a European auto slowdown; it expects to meet or exceed the peer-average growth for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion lever remains, and what is the exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an exit target, but said Q4 margin must be above 15%. Levers are gross margin from Project Fortius plus SG&A gains from portfolio company consolidation. Q1 had seasonal visa and travel costs and Comviva seasonality as negatives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO and free cash flow improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of Q1 was helped by accelerated customer payments and FX on receivables, which will normalise. Management said working capital remains a priority with a long-term improvement trend, though quarterly seasonality will persist.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Comms ramp impact is in Q1, and what is the full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: One of the two large Comms deals has not ramped at all yet, so impact comes in later quarters. Management said it would not give a specific full-year growth number, given the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Was the strong quarter a plan or a surprise, and is demand improving or is share being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarter was stronger than expected, helped by the European auto acceleration. It described a shift in demand toward modernisation and platform work, with the core stable and no 'SaaS eclipse' seen; it remains cautiously optimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Given the pricing comparisons with peers, can 15% margins go higher, and what competitor irrationality exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% is the target for FY27, with a path beyond FY27 to be set. Examples of irrational pricing included 70%-80% productivity assumptions in 5-7 year deals and holding infrastructure prices amid about 20% YoY inflation.

Management reiterated 15-20% revenue growth for FY27 and a roughly 14% EBITDA margin, and gave the first explicit 4-wheeler revenue range after the CEO's exit. Receivables rose because the company stopped discounting bills with its two major customers, not because of any change in payment terms.

segments.name: Automotive lighting (LED)
segments.commentary: LED share of automotive lighting was 63% in FY26 versus 60% in prior years; management says its pipeline is almost 100% LED and the share will keep rising, with 1-2% gains each quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler
segments.commentary: Current 4-wheeler business guided at INR100-150 crore for FY27, rising to INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; Mahindra & Mahindra orders start this year, and Mercedes is at testing and validation stage.

segments.name: Rear-view mirrors and plastic moulded parts
segments.commentary: Share of revenue is slipping slightly, but management says absolute amounts are growing, though more slowly than lighting; these are ancillary products sold to the same lighting customers.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 15-20% a year for FY27 and beyond, ahead of industry growth, despite possible El Nino or weak-monsoon moderation.
EBITDA margin guidance of around 14% or more, including the 4-wheeler business; 4-wheeler expected to be margin-neutral over the next 2-3 years.
4-wheeler revenue: INR100-150 crore in FY27, INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; management says impact is limited this year and more meaningful from next year.
Capex of about INR200 crore over the next two years at company level; no greenfield project envisaged.
Commodity and INR-depreciation cost pressures are treated as pass-through to customers, with a lag of a quarter at times.
Borrowing not needed given healthy cash; insurance premiums to be renegotiated at next renewal.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 75%; FY26 capex of about INR108 crore went mainly to debottleneck lines.
Projected capex of about INR200 crore over the next 2 years, which includes the 4-wheeler initiatives.
Solar and open-access renewable energy rollout across plants; Hosur plant gets about 65% of energy from solar and a further 20% from wind, with the model to extend to other plants.
An in-house EMI/EMC validation lab is being installed to cut product development time and reduce reliance on outside test agencies.
R&D spend is more than 2% of revenue (around 2%) in FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler production grew about 12% to a record roughly 26.7 million units in FY26, above the FY19 pre-pandemic peak.

Customers: TVS (iQube, Jupiter, Moped, motorcycles), Honda (Activa EV and new models), Royal Enfield (Classic, EV initiatives), Suzuki and Yamaha (healthy growth; 8-9 models in development), Hero (two recent launches running well, and a new EV platform approved).
4-wheeler RFQs of about INR700 crore; about 70% converted into business now under development (management said this does not equal fixed orders).

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables jump this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company stopped discounting bills with two major customers, TVS and one other, because cash flow is now strong; payment terms are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise faster than revenue, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was 13.80% of sales in FY26 versus 13.62% earlier, with part of the rise from recently notified labour-cost increases. Capex is about INR200 crore over two years at company level, and no greenfield project is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO exit a sign of a delay in the 4-wheeler strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Sahni left after a three-year term to pursue other interests. Rahul Jain and Rajesh Sharma now lead 4-wheeler, and management says there is no derailment and a detailed strategy will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still looking for a new 4-wheeler CEO?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management says there is enough bandwidth in-house and Rahul Jain, with Rajesh Sharma, will personally oversee 4-wheeler growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will 4-wheeler be margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is too small to judge separately and will be margin-neutral, with overall EBITDA guidance kept at around 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the other automotive lighting (non-LED) growth a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-LED share is declining and the chart cited covers the whole company, including rear-view mirrors, not just automotive lighting; it offered to clarify offline.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler execution: order book is still small, Mahindra and Mercedes timelines are not fixed, and the CEO has left.
Demand moderation risk from weak monsoon or El Nino on 2-wheelers.
Cost pass-through lag on commodity and INR-depreciation pressure, including imported LED chips.
Receivables trend after bill discounting was stopped.
Insurance premium increase after the Tapukara fire, to be negotiated at renewal.
Timing of new-product launches (POC stage; regulatory norms for touch and laser technology still awaited).

532768|2026-06.headline: Fiem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.6% to INR769.9 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 13.5%; FY27 4-wheeler ramp pushed out to FY28.
532768|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales grew 18.62% YoY to INR769.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR104.06 crore at a 13.5% margin, versus 13.46% a year ago. PAT increased 16.31% to INR65.19 crore. Management said raw material and employee cost increases will be passed on with a lag over the next few quarters, and reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and about 14% EBITDA margin. The main negative was the 4-wheeler lighting ramp, which management now expects to slip into FY28 from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 13.46% YoY; about 130 bps QoQ compression as stated by an analyst

financial_highlights.metric: LED share of automotive lighting revenue

financial_highlights.change: Analyst figure; company has no debt per analyst

segments.name: 2-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: Core growth engine. Management says volumes are in line with TVS, Honda and Suzuki; Yamaha lagged, with exports up only 2-3% against domestic up 40-50% per an analyst. Industry production reached 7.25 million units in Q1, about 22.8% growth per management.

segments.name: EV lighting
segments.commentary: EV share of 2-wheeler volume is above 9%, up from about 6% a year ago. Supplies commenced for Ather Konarc (sole supplier on the new model), River RX02 and Royal Enfield EV Flying Flea. Hero Vida lamps for its Andhra Pradesh plant will ship from Hosur from next quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler lighting
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of revenue. Management now expects FY27 to stay at a similar level, with meaningful scale-up pushed to FY28 because customer conversion is taking longer. Mahindra supplies are scaling as planned; Force Motors and other OEM development is ongoing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 15-20%, unchanged; management said this holds for the years to come until a significant move into another business.
EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for the full year; Q1 carried cost increases in employee cost and raw materials.
Raw material cost increase (about 80 bps of the margin impact per management) expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters.
Employee cost run-rate expected to stay at the Q1 level for the next three quarters after the minimum wage revision (Haryana first, about 35% increase there, other states following).
FY27 capex target about INR100 crore, versus about INR110 crore in FY26; most of it for Hosur (EV capacity for TVS and others), some at Tapukara.
4-wheeler lighting revenue for FY27 now expected at about 2.5% of revenue, versus the earlier INR100-150 crore indication; the ramp shifts to FY28.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR41.15 crore; FY27 target about INR100 crore, largely Hosur (Kelamangalam and Thally Road) for EV capacity.
Customers expanding: TVS 2-wheeler capacity 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by year-end; Hero Vida capacity 15,000 to 45,000 units per month.
Hands-off detection POC built and shown to almost all customers; light control module (LCM) expected to launch with 2-3 customers soon.
In-house EMI/EMC lab supports faster validation and shorter development time.
demand_pricing: Industry: record Q1 2-wheeler volume of 7.25 million units, supported by GST rationalisation, retail financing and rural demand; exports and EVs grew faster.
Management says wallet share with top customers is same or better; more than 100 models are with Fiem across customers.
Mercedes: samples submitted, with 1.5-2 years of vehicle-level testing before an RFQ/RFI for mass production.
Ambient lighting using optical fibre: technology not yet uniform; business expected to be cracked in about a year with customers.
LED share of automotive lighting at 63%; management expects new models to move to LED and targets about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY27 4-wheeler lighting guidance (INR100-150 crore in the prior quarter) cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is pushed out by about two quarters, with FY27 slightly lower and 4-wheeler at about 2.5% of revenue. Orders are lumpy and conversion cycles with customers are longer.

qa_highlights.question: How will LED penetration move in 2-wheeler lighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new models are coming with LEDs only and it expects about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months. It does not expect 100% because older models and aftermarket demand will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Yamaha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Yamaha to be flat to growing for the year. Exports were weak on the cycle of European and US demand; domestic models such as R15, Aerox and XSR were slower in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and cost pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 14% EBITDA margin for FY27. Raw material cost increases are expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters; the employee cost run-rate should hold for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is capital allocation given about INR280 crore cash and no debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited organic and inorganic opportunities, plus possible future 4-wheeler and electronics capex. It will fund capex from internal accruals and would raise debt if needed for a larger opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company disclose wallet share by customer and segment?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst asked for annual wallet share disclosure by segment. Management declined to share it in advance, citing customer confidentiality, and said it will announce models after customer launches.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler ramp has slipped again; FY28 is now the earliest meaningful scale-up, and analysts questioned competitive share gains.
Yamaha exports and domestic models slowed in Q1; management expects recovery but gave no quarterly targets.
Input cost and rupee pressure: pass-through has a lag, so margin in the next 1-2 quarters depends on recovery.
Employee cost step-up from minimum wage revisions across states, which management expects to persist for the next three quarters.
Hands-off detection and LCM remain at POC or pre-launch stage with no order value disclosed; ambient lighting timing is about a year away.
Analysts asked about share loss at top customers; management did not give a quantified wallet share figure.

532772|2026-03.headline: DCB Bank Q4 FY26 record PAT of INR 206 crore (FY26 INR 732 crore), NIM up 12bps QoQ to 3.39%, GNPA 2.45%, NNPA 0.89%.
532772|2026-03.overview: DCB Bank reported its third consecutive record quarterly profit, with Q4 PAT at INR 206 crore and FY26 PAT at INR 732 crore, with income growth of 16% against expense growth of 11%. Advances grew 18% YoY and 6% QoQ, deposits grew 21% YoY and 7% QoQ, and cost of deposits fell 44bps YoY. Asset quality improved, with slippage ratio down to 2.28% from 3.09%, FY26 credit cost at 40bps, and recoveries and upgrades at 109% of fresh slippage. Management flagged the West Asia conflict as a cloud on the horizon but said no immediate portfolio impact is visible yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Repricing benefit expected until late Q2 or early Q3; HL to BL sourcing is now about 70-30, helping yield and credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise 12bps QoQ when yield on advances was flat and cost of funds fell only slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no one-offs; the benefit came from a mix shift as lower-yield co-lending shrank while higher-yield book grew, absorbing the 25bps repo cut; better recoveries also helped.

qa_highlights.question: Gold slippage versus overall slippage numbers did not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishal Anchaliya said gold has 21% weightage with 5.3% slippage and other products 79% with 1.4%, giving 2.28% overall.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth be sustained with co-lending moderating and MSME flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending growth to match overall asset growth in FY27 (it grew 24.9% in FY26 versus 108% earlier); non-co-lending growth was 8.6% QoQ; mortgages reengineered and growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives NIM towards the 3.50-3.65% business-model target?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposit management, current account growth and not chasing high-yield segments; execution risk rather than strategic risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise plan and provision coverage level?
qa_highlights.answer: Raise about INR 1,100-1,200 crore around late Q2 or early Q3 FY27 at current prices; management said PCR above 75% is acceptable, 78%+ good.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline QoQ, and what is the outlook?

532777|2026-03.headline: Info Edge Q4 FY26 standalone billings rose 7% to Rs.1,057 crore and revenue 17% to Rs.805 crore, with 99acres billings flat at 2%.
532777|2026-03.overview: Standalone operating profit rose 39% YoY to Rs.323 crore at a 40% margin, helped by a one-time Rs.20.5 crore 99acres warranty provision write-back that lifted revenue. Recruitment billings grew 10% standalone (9% including Zwayam and DoSelect) amid a subdued hiring market, with GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4. 99acres billings grew only 2% after a sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls, while traffic share rose to 49% web and 52% in April. Management guided to double-digit Naukri topline growth as the threshold for holding margins, and said 99acres should turn cash-generative in FY27 if execution holds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring sentiment across GCCs, IT and non-IT, and what is driving 99acres margins and share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitesh Oberoi called the market lukewarm; larger GCCs have shrunk headcount while smaller ones hire. Share gains credited to execution, with 13-14 points added to traffic share in recent months; new-home responses up 33% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the adoption and willingness to pay for AI-Rex, and how does 99acres gain share in new homes?

rows.label: JobHai expansion to Mumbai and Bangalore
rows.why: JobHai is monetising in Delhi NCR, with about 100% YoY growth targeted for several years and more aggressive plans in Mumbai and Bangalore.

rows.label: 99acres double billings in 3 years, 25-30% EBITDA margin
