532777|2026-06.headline: Info Edge Q1 FY27: standalone billings up over 14% and recruitment billings up 17%, with underlying recruitment billings growth at about 15%.
532777|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.824 crores and operating profit rose 33% to Rs.334 crores, with cash from operations up 25% to Rs.225 crores. Naukri recruitment billings grew 17%, which management says is about 15% after adjusting for renewal timing, with revenue up 13% and a 58% operating PBT margin. 99acres billings grew 17% and its operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores, near break-even. Shiksha billings fell 23% on AI-driven search traffic loss, and matchmaking grew billings 20% and was near break-even.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash balance at end of Q1

segments.name: Naukri recruitment
segments.commentary: Billings up over 17% (about 15% normalised), revenue up 13%, operating PBT margin 58%. Tech/IT/BPM billings +15%, GCCs +31%, other sectors +12%, recruitment consultants +1%.

segments.name: Naukri Jobseeker (Naukri 360)
segments.commentary: Billings up over 35%, PBT margin 63%. Paid subscribers rose from 1.3% to 2.6% of MAU over six quarters.

segments.name: NaukriGulf
segments.commentary: Grew 12%, below the roughly 20% pre-geopolitical trajectory; operating margin above 35%.

segments.name: 99acres
segments.commentary: Billings and revenue both up about 17%; operating PBT loss of about Rs.2 crores versus Rs.17 crores underlying loss in Q4 FY26. Web timeshare 49%, app 55%, iOS 69%.

segments.name: Shiksha
segments.commentary: Billings down 23% and revenue down 12% as reduced Google referral traffic hit client delivery; US and Canada study-abroad softer.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Portfolio billings up 20%; Aisle +44%, Jeevansathi +14%; near break-even operating PBT; more than 45% profile share in Hindi-speaking markets.

segments.name: Job Hai
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled on a small base; about Rs.15 crores revenue last year, burn near Rs.50 crores a year.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is not guiding on billing growth; it is unsure whether volume growth can sustain 10% or 15%, but is more confident on new products than six months ago.
Margin expansion depends on topline growth in the teens; if topline grows 8-10%, margins will be hard to improve.
Heavy AI investment will continue, so margins are not expected to expand from AI monetisation alone.
99acres aims to become cash-generative during FY27 and to grow revenue 18-20% a year with cost control; ultimate goal of 30% margin.
Job Hai aims to more than double revenue this year, reach 18 cities in coming months, and could reach Rs.100 crores in two to three years.
Headcount is down YoY; management expects to resume hiring once the business grows in the teens.
capex_capacity: AI-Rex live across more than 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms by end-June, with over 10% converted to paid; free trial rolled out to 10,000 customers in Q2.
Talent Pulse has more than 600 paid customers; AI-Rex and Talent Pulse to be scaled to several thousand more customers over the next few quarters.
Coding Ninjas acquisition completed; short-form upskilling courses priced at Rs.5,000-7,000 being tested.
Over 150 people in GenAI and machine learning; AI efficiencies of 15-20% in some functions.
99Shorts (new project listings) launched in NCR, with plans to expand to more cities; new project segment estimated at over Rs.5,000 crores.
Naukri database of about 118 million resumes, with over 25,000 new profiles added daily.
demand_pricing: Growth split per management: about one-third from volume and renewals, about one-third from price increases, and about one-third from new offerings (AI-Rex, Talent Pulse, employer branding); customer-count growth is a small subset.
AI-Rex priced per mandate at Rs.3,500 for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants (launch prices); sold to over 400 clients in Q1 and about 300 more in July.
Recruitment consultants, about a quarter of revenue, grew only 1%; management attributes this to clients insourcing in a slow market.
99acres: primary about 45-47% of revenue, secondary about equal, owners 7-10%; NCR is the largest market and has been affected by sales-team restructuring.
Management says the JobSpeak index measures volume only, which does not capture premiumisation, pricing and new products.
Competitive pressure easing after Housing.com was acquired by Aurum, which management expects to reduce competitor marketing spend.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 13% revenue growth is from realisation versus customer count, and how much from AI products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one-third of revenue growth came from renewals and volume, and about one-third from newer offerings such as AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. Premium CV views are growing over 25% from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the normalised 15% recruitment billings growth adjusted for the favourable Q1 FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said normalisation nets out early and deferred renewals each quarter, which captures the prior-year base effect. GCC billings grew 31% reported, with about 2.5% of one-off timing shift from Q4 FY26 deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying separately for AI-Rex, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex is charged per mandate and sold separately in many cases, by the same sales team plus specialists. Of 4,000 free trials, 400 converted; management says cannibalisation is possible, mainly among consultants who downgraded.

qa_highlights.question: Will 99acres reach 30% margin faster after the Housing acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so: competitive intensity should fall as Aurum may cut marketing spend. Sales restructuring is mostly behind, and NCR may take one to two more months to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-Rex renewal cycle and how is value measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs one renewal cycle to confirm success. Customers buy mandate bundles (10, 20 or 30 mandates), and internal dashboards track shortlisting, screening and delivery time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 99acres billing reconciled against JobSpeak index trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JobSpeak index tracks volume only, while billings also include premiumisation, pricing and new products. Sanjeev Bikhchandani attributed faster billings to sales teams making more and better calls.

risks_watch: Volume growth depends on net hiring; management says mid-tier volume is weak and consultant (about a quarter of revenue) growth is flat.
Shiksha billings down 23% with no near-term recovery expected; AI-driven search changes and weakness in US and Canada study-abroad.
NaukriGulf growth slowed to 12% due to Middle East disruption.
AI-Rex and Talent Pulse have only one renewal cycle of evidence; possible cannibalisation of existing products.
Consultant and mid-market volume trends; watch whether July's AI-Rex sales convert to paid usage.
Job Hai burn of about Rs.50 crores a year, and 99acres NCR sales recovery.
532777|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Naukri product pipeline and 99acres traction, but cautious on volume: management repeatedly said it does not know whether growth will sustain at 10% or 15%. It was candid that Shiksha faces continued pressure and that 99acres monetisation lagged its traffic lead.
key_quotes: This was a better quarter than the ones we saw through FY26.
If you're able to grow topline in the teens, margins should improve. But if for some reason, top line growth comes at 8, 9, 10%, then it'll be hard to improve margins.
AI is also changing how we operate, driving efficiencies of 15-20% across some functions.
We're confident of being able to deliver revenue growth without adding too many people.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margins improve only if topline grows in the teens; recruitment revenue grew 13% with 58% PBT margin, and 8-10% growth would make margin gains hard, while heavy AI investment continues.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: AI-Rex (4,000+ customers) and Talent Pulse (600+ paid) are to scale to several thousand more customers over the next few quarters, and Job Hai plans 18 cities in coming months; these are rollouts, not physical capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Recruitment billings grew 17% (about 15% normalised) but management does not know if volume growth sustains 10% or 15%; about one-third of revenue growth is from volume and renewals, consultants grew only 1%, and Shiksha billings fell 23%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no billing growth guidance and is unsure whether volume sustains 10-15%; NaukriGulf slowed to 12% from roughly 20%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Shiksha billings down 23% with no near-term recovery expected, mid-tier volume weak, and consultant revenue (about a quarter of revenue) up only 1%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI-Rex (launch prices Rs.3,500 per company mandate) and Talent Pulse are scaling, 99Shorts is expanding beyond NCR to more cities, and Coding Ninjas short-form courses at Rs.5,000-7,000 are being tested.

rows.label: AI-Rex paid conversion and renewal cycle
rows.why: AI-Rex has 400+ clients from Q1 plus about 300 more in July, with over 10% of 4,000 customers converted to paid; management needs one renewal cycle to confirm success and flags possible cannibalisation.

rows.label: 99acres cash-generative during FY27
rows.why: Operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores from Rs.17 crores in Q4 FY26 (down 89%), and management targets revenue growth of 18-20% a year with cost control, with the Housing.com acquisition by Aurum expected to ease marketing spend.

rows.label: Job Hai scale-up
rows.why: Revenue roughly doubled from about Rs.15 crores last year, management targets more than doubling this year and 18 cities, but burn is about Rs.50 crores a year.

tone.note: Management was confident on Naukri's AI product pipeline and 99acres traction but cautious on volume, repeatedly saying it does not know if growth sustains at 10-15%; analysts probed normalisation of the 15% billings figure, AI-Rex cannibalisation and 99acres margin path.

532777|2026-09.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
532777|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri)
segments.commentary: Q2 billings +13%, revenue +13%, operating profit +20% at 59% operating PBT margin; H1 billings +15%. Q2 IT/Tech/BPM billings +3%, GCCs +7%, other sectors +18%, consultants +7%. Naukri 360 billings +37%; Job Hai billings +86%; NaukriGulf +9% at about 36% margin.

segments.name: Real Estate (99acres)
segments.commentary: Billings +21% YoY in Q2 (up from 17% in Q1), revenue +17%. Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore; operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago. Marketing spend down about 13% YoY while enquiries grew 33%.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Billings +23% in Q2 (Jeevansathi +18%, Aisle +40%). Segment near breakeven at operating PBT; Jeevansathi operating profit Rs.2 crore, Aisle operating loss Rs.3 crore. Segment cash generation Rs.3 crore vs cash loss Rs.2 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)
segments.commentary: Billings -27% and revenue -9% in Q2; near breakeven at operating PBT with cash loss of Rs.16 crore. AI-driven search changes cut referral traffic; company is pivoting to domestic counselling with AI voice bots and widening Study Abroad destinations (UK, UAE, continental Europe).

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Portfolio of about 135 companies across AI, deeptech and consumer tech, with about Rs.5,000 crore invested via balance sheet and AIFs.

guidance_outlook: Management views underlying business growth at about 14-15% and is setting sales team targets on that basis.

Target of 100% growth in Job Hai billings this year; Job Hai burn about Rs.45 crore a year, taking about 2-3% off overall Naukri margin; breakeven estimated at Rs.100-125 crore topline, possibly taking a couple of years (later framed as Rs.120-130 crore).
99acres expected to generate positive operating cash for FY27 and to see operating leverage progressively through the rest of FY27; aims for further traffic and revenue share gains in H2.
Jeevansathi billing growth expected to accelerate in H2; Aisle expected to continue high growth.
Management said margins are not the current focus; it aims to keep sales growing above 10% YoY, and does not expect margins to decline.
capex_capacity: Management continues to step up investment in AI infrastructure, talent and tools; Job Hai investment levels broadly unchanged in the quarter.
Job Hai and 99acres marketing spend managed for efficiency; 99Shorts being taken beyond NCR to more cities.
New Projects opportunity estimated at about Rs.6,000 crore across digital and non-digital spend; expansion is a strategic priority through content, product and client delivery.
demand_pricing: AI and data products now a high single-digit share of Recruitment topline; annualised run rate about Rs.240 crore (Q2 AI-first revenue about Rs.60 crore x4). AI-Rex had little revenue in Q1 and scaled sharply in Q2.
AI-Rex: about 2,000 accounts using it vs a potential base of about 40,000 large clients; rate card Rs.3,500 per mandate for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants. Talent Pulse used by 750 companies.
Clients buying AI offerings paid on average 10-15% more than non-buyers, per management.
Consultant revenue growth slowed to 5% in H1 (2-3% excluding AI-Rex); IT services hiring remains mostly replacement-driven.
Paid subscribers reached 2.7% of Naukri monthly active users vs 1.3% in January 2025.
99acres: about 50% revenue share in core categories per management; competitor revenue reportedly declined; Housing sold to Aurum, which targets breakeven in 4-5 quarters.
Naukri unique paying customers flat YoY at 46,000 (down from 49,000 QoQ), as the company reworked low-ticket e-commerce offers.

qa_highlights.question: Will Sanjeev be a full-time CEO or a stopgap, and what changes are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev said no decision has been taken on the long-term structure; he will consult the NRC, Hitesh remains available for counsel, and no hiring decision has been made.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 billings growth of 13% the new normal after Q1's 17.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing shifts are behind the swing; Q1 was about 14-15% underlying and business is growing about 14-15%. Revenue is recognised over 12 months, so renewal timing defers into later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-Rex lift margins, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: AI products are high gross margin, but the GTM is penetration-first over about 24 months; management declined to give a steady-state margin and said margins should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI revenue run rate additive, and is pricing bundled?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.240 crore is Q2 revenue x4; AI-first products contributed about Rs.60 crore in Q2 and are largely additive, with prior-year AI revenue mainly Talent Pulse and jobseeker services. Products are priced separately on rate cards but often sold as a negotiated bundle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unique customers stay flat at 46,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small low-ticket e-commerce buyers were pruned and offers repriced higher; e-commerce revenue is up even though buying customers fell.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Job Hai margin drag and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Job Hai burn about Rs.45 crore a year, 2-3% of Naukri margin; breakeven at Rs.100-125 crore topline, possibly over a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is IT and GCC growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: IT hiring is mostly replacement-led and Naukri's share is at risk in consultants; GCC growth in the teens is driven by mid-size and small GCCs, with larger GCCs more exposed to US layoffs.

risks_watch: CEO transition: Hitesh Oberoi leaves full-time role Dec 2; Sanjeev Bikhchandani (age 63) becomes Group CEO Dec 3 with no successor or CBO named; CBO roles at 99acres and other units are vacant or unclear, and Pawan left Naukri a few months ago.
Billings timing noise from renewal shifts; Q3 billings may swing again.
Shiksha billings -27% and cash losses of Rs.16 crore in Q2 while the business model pivots.
Consultant channel slowdown (H1 revenue growth 5%) as IT services firms cut costlier channels.
AI revenue durability: 2,000 AI-Rex accounts trying the product; management said the run-rate depends on these customers renewing next year.
Job Hai and Naukri 360 investment continues to dilute margins; NaukriGulf recovery depends on regional conditions.
532777|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics, 99acres and AI traction, but cautious on the Q2 billings slowdown, which management attributed to renewal timing. Evasive on succession details, with no named successor or CBO plan. Hitesh Oberoi framed the CEO exit as a planned handover to a strong internal team.
key_quotes: Excluding Shiksha, standalone billings grew over 14% in Q2 and about 16% in H1, against reported growth of 13% and 14%, respectively.
Our goal for the next, I would say, maybe 24 months is going to be to drive penetration, to get as many customers to use AI-Rex as possible, and then to get them to adopt it, use it and then renew.
Margins are not really our focus right now. It's about getting more sales, it's about getting more users, more clients, it's about getting adoption going.
We are hiring business, not the firing business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 operating PBT margin was 41% (up 541 bps) and 99acres loss fell from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore, but Job Hai burn of about Rs.45 crore a year takes 2-3% off Naukri margin and management says margins are not the focus.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Billings +13% in Q2 and +14% in H1, management guides underlying 14-15%, paid subscribers at 2.7% of MAU vs 1.3% a year ago, but unique paying customers flat at 46,000 and consultant revenue growth at 5% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex/utilisation not quantified; investment in AI infrastructure and Job Hai described as broadly unchanged, with no utilisation figure given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 billings +14% with AI-first run rate of about Rs.240 crore and Naukri 360 billings +37%, but management frames underlying growth at 14-15% rather than raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 billings growth slowed to 13% from Q1's 17.5% and Shiksha billings fell 27%, though management attributes the swing to renewal timing and guides underlying growth at 14-15%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Job Hai billings targeted to double this year, 99Shorts being extended beyond NCR, and Jeevansathi/Aisle growth to accelerate in H2; AI-Rex at about 2,000 accounts vs about 40,000 potential.

rows.label: AI product run-rate of Rs.240 crore
rows.why: AI-first products contributed about Rs.60 crore in Q2 (x4 = Rs.240 crore) and are largely additive, with AI-Rex at about 2,000 accounts vs about 40,000 potential large clients, though durability depends on renewals next year.

rows.label: 99acres operating cash positive in FY27
rows.why: Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore and operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago; management expects positive operating cash for FY27 and operating leverage through H2.

rows.label: CEO transition to Sanjeev Bikhchandani
rows.why: Hitesh Oberoi steps down as MD and CEO on Dec 2; Bikhchandani (age 63) becomes Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO, with no successor or CBO named and no long-term structure decided.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating metrics, 99acres and AI traction, and cautious on the Q2 billings slowdown blamed on renewal timing; it was evasive on CEO succession and long-term structure, while analysts probed billings durability and margin drag from Job Hai.

532782|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose over 115% YoY to INR37 crores at a 5.3% margin; FY26 EBITDA up 25% to INR85 crores on 3% lower income.
532782|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the best quarter of the year, with standalone total income of INR699 crores (up 4% YoY) and gross margin of 45% (up 329 bps YoY). For FY26, standalone income fell 3% to INR2,585 crores while EBITDA rose 25% to INR85 crores at a 3.3% margin, and management said the year was cash positive. Home textiles turned EBITDA-positive at INR8.4 crores (from negative INR3.5 crores), and the company is guiding FY27 as a year of margin expansion, profitability and deleveraging, without giving numeric targets. Management also flagged losses at the US subsidiary American Silk Mills, which is being closed or muted; India operations reported no inventory losses.

financial_highlights.change: from negative INR3.5 crores in FY25

financial_highlights.value: 0.8% in Q1 to 5.3% in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation at 93%, with effective spindle utilisation at about 89%. Management is prioritising value-added yarns over volume; cotton melange ranks highest on profitability, followed by PV dyed and 100% cotton.

segments.name: Fiber (Sutlej Green Fiber)
segments.commentary: Recycled polyester and sustainable fiber business operating at over 100% utilisation in FY26, described as a breakout year and a strategic ESG-aligned platform.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA-positive at INR8.4 crores in FY26 versus negative INR3.5 crores. Order pipeline is at 180 days. Management says it expects at least a doubling of EBITDA next year. Nesterra brand is run on a working-capital-light model through LFS and MBO partners, with no franchise or own stores yet.

segments.name: US subsidiary (American Silk Mills)
segments.commentary: Inventory losses sit in this US holding, not India operations. Management has decided to close or mute the unit and will serve US home textile customers directly, with US about 60% of exports.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is expected to be the inflection year: EBITDA to expand meaningfully on the FY26 base, profitability to return after almost two years of losses, and debt metrics to improve as cash generation strengthens. No numeric targets given.
Target to convert about one-third of the yarn portfolio into value-added segments over the next 12 months.
Renewable energy share to rise from 11% to about 40%, aimed at reducing power cost, which is about 50% of yarn manufacturing cost.
Home textiles EBITDA expected to at least double in the coming year, per management, though no number was put on it.
Technical textiles entry, beginning with protective textiles, will be capital-efficient and use existing assets plus incremental capex; protective textile margins cited at 12-15%.
Capex for FY27 is higher than FY26 (about INR70 crores spent in FY26) and milestone-based; more definite numbers expected in one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was roughly INR70 crores; FY27 budget is higher and released quarter by quarter against milestones.
Yarn capacity utilisation 93%; effective spindle utilisation about 89%.
Sutlej Green Fiber running at over 100% utilisation and being revamped further.
Home textile processing capacity of about 2 million meters; technical textiles will add specific equipment on top of this.
demand_pricing: Yarn prices have risen in line with raw material costs (polyester up about 30%, with viscose, acrylic and cotton also rising). Management says there is no incremental margin gain, only margin protection.
Global apparel demand is soft as customers run inventories tight. The US destocked over the last 3-4 quarters, and tariff clarity may be starting to bring in inquiries.
Export mix: about 60% of total business is exports, and about 60% of that goes to the US.
Value-added product feedback loop (sampling to test orders) takes 6-9 months.
Inventory policy: about 30-45 days of cotton and 15-20 days of other fibres.

qa_highlights.question: How much will yarn price increases since March lift the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Srivastava said yarn price increases only match raw material cost increases (polyester up about 30%), so there is no incremental contribution, only margin protection.

qa_highlights.question: Why are there inventory losses when prices are rising, and will more be booked this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory losses in India. The losses are in the US subsidiary American Silk Mills, which is being closed or muted; US exports will now be served directly.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Nesterra revenue stagnated for 4-6 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: The brand follows a calibrated, working-capital-efficient plan with LFS and MBO partners, with no own stores or franchise yet, so growth is deliberately measured.

qa_highlights.question: Will the yarn margin return to 10%+ EBITDA, and what is the blended yarn mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. It cited higher power costs and older cotton machinery as the cause of the dip, with renewables and value-added mix as the fix, and said YoY EBITDA margin improvement is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What margins are expected from technical textiles, and which sectors are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Protective textile margins of 12-15%, depending on inherent or treated FR. Target sectors include oil and gas and steel, with the application base much wider.

qa_highlights.question: Home textile EBITDA trajectory and whether INR18-20 crores in two years is realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it is confident of at least doubling home textile EBITDA next year on the order book and strategic customer commitments.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (polyester, viscose, cotton) and whether yarn price pass-through holds.
Forex hedging discipline, global tariff uncertainty and borrowing cost, named as watch areas.
Losses and closure costs at the US subsidiary American Silk Mills.
Value-added yarn and technical textiles depend on 6-9 month qualification cycles and product consistency.
Capex pace is milestone-linked, and FY27 capex figures are not yet defined.
532782|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the margin-led turnaround and FY27 direction, but evasive on quantified targets for yarn margins, home textile EBITDA and capex. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers and cited milestone-based planning.
key_quotes: That combination, margin expansion through a softer top line year in an environment we have just described is the most important number on this call.
The division swung from a negative INR3.5 crores to a positive INR8.4 crores at the EBITDA level in the last financial year.
We are not chasing growth for the sake of growth.
So what I can tell you is; last year, as per our numbers, we have done roughly about INR70 crores, which has kind of gone in.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 5.3% vs 0.8% in Q1 and FY26 EBITDA up 25% to INR85 crores; gross margin 45% (+329 bps YoY) and management guides FY27 EBITDA to expand meaningfully, though yarn price pass-through is only margin protection (no incremental gain).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Yarn utilisation 93% and Sutlej Green Fiber above 100%, but no new plant, line or size or date was given; only a revamp of Green Fiber and technical textile equipment on existing assets with no numbers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone income fell 3% to INR2,585 crores in FY26 and global apparel demand is soft with US destocking over 3-4 quarters; management prioritises value-added yarn over volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capex about INR70 crores, FY27 budget explicitly higher and milestone-based with more definite numbers promised in one to two quarters, and yarn utilisation at 93%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

532782|2026-06.headline: Sutlej Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (6.7% margin) from INR5 crore, with PBT of INR4.2 crore versus a loss a year ago.
532782|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 17% YoY to INR704 crore, marginally ahead of Q4 FY26. Gross margin expanded about 370 bps to 46.8%, with raw material cost falling to 53.2% of revenue from 56.9%. EBITDA margin has now expanded for five consecutive quarters (0.8%, 2.7%, 3.9%, 5.3%, 6.7%). Management said the quarter was clean with no exceptional items and that all three business clusters and six manufacturing units delivered positive EBITDA. Value-added yarn share is still only about 10-15% against a 30-35% target.

segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR640 crore, up 16% YoY; segment EBITDA INR34.4 crore vs INR6.5 crore a year ago. Management attributes about 60% of the 2.5% raw-material-to-sales improvement to moving up product categories and the balance to operational efficiency.

segments.name: Sutlej Green Fibre (recycled PET)
segments.commentary: Gross sales roughly INR400 crore; about 70-75% is consumed internally by the group's own units. Management is adding performance properties to recycled polyester and discussing collaborations with brands.

segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY and profitability held versus a loss a year ago. Sequentially softer on order phasing, not demand. Management targets doubling the business in about two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal quarterly guidance. Management said it will maintain or better Q1 numbers in Q2 and Q3, but declined to give a clear outlook.
Long-term aim is a double-digit EBITDA margin, described as the near-term benchmark; no timeline was given.
Finance cost in absolute terms expected to rise to about INR75 crore this year from about INR67 crore last year, due to capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.

Home textile growth plans are underway, with the business in investment mode for technical and protective textiles.
demand_pricing: Global demand described as relatively stable; management said legacy yarn makers benefited from China-driven demand in cotton-grade yarn, which Sutlej does not directly target.

Export markets: Far East and Africa, opened last year, have moved from trial volumes to repeat orders. Core markets Latin America and Europe are steady; Bangladesh demand is stable but below levels of two years ago. Exports go to about 60 destinations.
Customers are rebuilding inventories cautiously from very low levels.

Value-added yarn is about 10-15% of yarn products against a 30-35% target. Customer trials take 3-6 months, and first containers of new specialty SKUs have shipped for testing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn portfolio is value-added now, and what EBITDA margin can the business reach at 30-35% value-added?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is about 10-15% of yarn products, with a pipeline and new SKUs under customer evaluation. Management would not give a margin number for the steady state but said double-digit EBITDA is the minimum target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn EBITDA gain came from spread expansion versus mix and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of the raw material-to-sales improvement (about 2.5 percentage points) came from moving up product categories; the rest came from operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost (15-17% of revenue) so far above peers, and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ratio is not at target and will fall in coming quarters. It attributed the gap to melange and dyeing layers, job processing in home textiles, and low realisations, and said absolute costs have not risen.

qa_highlights.question: What will the interest outflow be this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost is expected to rise to about INR75 crore from about INR67 crore last year, because of capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and EBITDA potential of Green Fibre and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Green Fibre gross sales are about INR400 crore, of which 70-75% is consumed internally. Home textiles are to be doubled in about two years, with no margin target given.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt be structured, and how do raw material prices affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital borrowing will rise for the same number of days because of higher raw material prices. Long-term debt is mainly for capex, which is secured. Credit lines will be rebalanced as results move.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Q2 and Q3 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance. Management said it will try to maintain or better the Q1 numbers.

532783|2026-03.headline: LT Foods FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR11,023 crore, but reported EBITDA margin was 11.8% after U.S. tariff pass-through and brand spend.
532783|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue including other income grew 26% YoY to INR11,023 crore, with normalized revenue growth of 19% excluding U.S. tariff effects. Reported gross profit was INR3,692 crore (normalized gross margin about 35.3%) and EBITDA INR1,236 crore, with PAT of INR625 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR2,938 crore, EBITDA INR300 crore and PAT about INR136 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to U.S. tariff pass-through, a doubling of marketing spend in India, UK investment phase and remodelling of the organic segment, and guided to a gradual margin recovery toward 12% EBITDA.

financial_highlights.change: excl. U.S. tariff and shipment-terms change

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to EBITDA / net debt to equity

financial_highlights.value: INR9,742 crore; 88% of revenue; EBITDA margin 12.3%

segments.name: Basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR9,742 crore (88% of total) with 29% reported and 21% normalized growth; EBITDA margin 12.3%. Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19% in FY26.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue crossed INR1,016 crore, up 9% in FY26, but segment is under stress from currency and commodity pressure and is being remodelled; holds 12% share of India's organic food exports.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat (RTH) and ready-to-cook (RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR187 crore in FY26 (2.5x over five years); growth constrained by RTH plant capacity, with new capacity expected from Q2 FY27 (production start around July). Segment gross margin ~32-33% reported, ~35% per management, and 40%+ before sampling and promotion spend.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Value growth 10% and volume growth 12%; quick commerce and e-commerce grew over 45%; premium segment grew 2x the portfolio; market share 23.7% (Nielsen); household reach 64.4 lakh (Kantar).

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Contributed 48% of FY26 revenue with 53% reported growth (about 9% normalized); Royal holds over 60% share; Golden Star is about 10% of segment revenue and was fully consolidated after buying the remaining 49% stake.

segments.name: Europe / UK
segments.commentary: Europe revenue grew 34% in FY26; UK revenue about GBP 45 million with a target of GBP 100 million by 2030; UK is in an investment phase.

segments.name: Middle East and Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Saudi Arabia is a new market launched with about INR50 crore revenue; Southeast Asia contributed INR53 crore; management is not investing heavily in the Middle East.

guidance_outlook: Management expects continued double-digit growth; long-term growth target 10-12% organic.
Gross margin for FY27 expected broadly in line with FY26, around 33-33.5%, as tariff has normalized from 50% to 10%.

EBITDA margin expected to recover toward the ~12% level as brand investments normalize and scale benefits come through; management says it is confident of the 12% range but flagged a disruptive environment.
RTH, RTC and organic segments expected to grow faster than the overall business.
Capex guidance: about INR330 crore in FY26 and similar in FY27; long-term run-rate about INR250 crore a year. Rice capacity cost is about INR3 crore per ton.

RTH revenue target of INR300 crore in about two years; RTC target INR100-120 crore by 2030; RTH/RTC breakeven at about INR400 crore segment revenue, now pushed out about one year due to capacity constraints.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR330-360 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land purchase and RTH facility and warehouse), UK packaging facility, and India land and warehouses.
RTH capacity in the U.S. was 15 million (INR150 crore) this year; a new plant is delayed and is expected to start production around July/Q2 FY27, targeting INR300 crore in two years.
Raichur (Karnataka) facility investment to deepen regional rice play.
India milling capacity is 8 lakh tons of paddy-to-rice; packing capacity is about 8-9 lakh tons. The company adds 50,000-60,000 tons of rice capacity a year.
Europe packaging asset build-out and India warehousing are planned for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the U.S. consumer demand has not been impacted by war and inflation, as food spending is the last to be cut.
Basmati industry paddy prices rose about 20-25% in the domestic season; international deals are 85% closed for the season, with the remaining 10-15% priced 15-20% higher.
Raw material prices are up roughly 25-30% from opening levels; management expects prices will not fall much.
Freight to the Middle East rose 10-15x (Dubai about $200 to $2,200; Jeddah $700-800 to $2,600); Europe freight is the most disrupted; U.S. freight is not materially disrupted.
Premium SKUs grew 2x the overall portfolio in India, and the mix shift is supporting gross margin; value and volume growth in India were roughly equal.
Distribution in India is flat at about 172,000 outlets versus the 170,000 cited earlier, but market share improved year on year.
Regional rice revenue is about INR170 crore, growing at a high double-digit rate.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 U.S. and basmati volume growth, and how much did U.S. tariffs affect them?
qa_highlights.answer: Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19%; U.S. volume rose about 30-38% including Golden Star, or 7-8% excluding it. Management said the tariff disruption helped win customers through better service levels, at some margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment revenue growth numbers not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the India and U.S. figures are normalized for tariffs and Golden Star, while the basmati segment figure includes tariffs. Golden Star moved from a JV to a 100% subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 gross and EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to stay within the FY26 range, about 33-33.5% (FY25 was about 24.6% on the old basis). EBITDA should return toward 12%, which was the prior-year level.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payable days about 100?
qa_highlights.answer: 60-70% of purchases are made in season and 30-40% outside it, with deferred payment terms. Management expects roughly 100 payable days to persist. Inventory is about 190-200 days on average, with 250 days cited as of March 31.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RTH/RTC targets and breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: RTH revenue is INR15 crore this year, with a target of INR300 crore in two years. RTC targets INR100-120 crore by 2030. Breakeven is at about INR400 crore of segment revenue, now about one year later due to capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex breakup and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR350 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land, RTH plant) with UK and India warehousing. FY27 capex is expected to be similar, with a long-term run-rate of about INR250 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bhopal insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: INR136 crore is outstanding from the insurer and INR50 crore has been received against a bank guarantee backed by an FD. No accounting gain has been booked until the final verdict, expected in June.

RTH supply is constrained until the new capacity starts around July/Q2 FY27, which could hold back the segment's growth and breakeven timing.
Organic segment remodelling and currency/commodity pressure are weighing on profitability; capacity will take time to utilize.
Inventory of about 250 days and payable days of about 100 need watching for working capital and cash flow.
Bhopal insurance claim: INR136 crore outstanding with a court verdict expected in June; no accounting gain booked until then.
El Nino and the 1.5-month outlook for the next basmati crop are key open risks for procurement costs.

So this year, we have spent INR330-odd crores. And the next year also will be in the same range.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: U.S. RTH/RTC plant is under construction with capacity coming online from Q2 FY27, targeting INR300 crore segment revenue in about two years from INR15 crore this year; India adds 50,000-60,000 t/yr of rice capacity on top of 8 lakh t milling.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19% in FY26, India volume grew 12%, and management expects continued double-digit growth; RTH/RTC/organic expected to outgrow the group, though RTH is capped by capacity until Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex ran about INR330-360 crore in FY26 and is guided to a similar INR330-odd crore in FY27 with a long-term run-rate of about INR250 crore a year, plus Raichur, Europe packaging and India warehousing projects planned; an incremental announcement is likely but not a step-change.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on margins, citing a dynamic environment, raw material up 25-30%, El Nino risk and an unquantified aged-inventory issue, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA recovery to 12% depends on tariffs holding at 10%, paddy costs and Middle East freight (10-15x) not persisting, and RTH breakeven already pushed out about one year to around INR400 crore segment revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RTH capacity start in Q2 FY27 unlocks the RTH/RTC range growth toward INR300 crore in two years and RTC INR100-120 crore by 2030; Saudi Arabia is a new market at about INR50 crore revenue.

rows.label: International basmati deals 85% closed for season
rows.why: 85% of international deals are closed at prices for the season, with the remaining 10-15% priced 15-20% higher, supporting realisations, while raw material is up 25-30%.

rows.label: Bhopal insurance claim verdict
rows.why: INR136 crore is outstanding from the insurer and INR50 crore already received; no accounting gain booked until the final verdict expected in June, so a one-time gain is possible in the window.

rows.label: Working capital days down to 176 from 196
rows.why: Working capital days fell 20 days YoY to 176, but inventory of about 190-200 days (250 cited at March 31) and roughly 100 payable days leave cash flow exposed.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, market share, RTH growth and the 12% EBITDA target, but cautious on margins, El Nino and unquantified aged inventory; analysts and investors probed on segment growth reconciliation, payable days and inventory.

532783|2026-06.headline: LT Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore, with EBITDA up 20% to INR363 crore but margin down to 11.5% from 12.1%.
532783|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR3,161 crore (19% normalised), with gross profit up 19% to INR1,029 crore and PAT up 9% to INR183 crore. Core basmati and specialty rice revenue rose 34% to INR2,845 crore on 11% volume growth at a stable 13% EBITDA margin. Organic foods revenue fell to INR254 crore at a 4% EBITDA margin during restructuring to a direct-to-retailer CPG model. Management said results are in line with annual estimates and reiterated full-year guidance, with the organic recovery expected over 1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 12.1% in the prior-year period (stated as 11%)

segments.name: Core basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,845 crore, up 34% YoY on 11% volume growth, with EBITDA margin stable at 13%. India revenue grew 23% YoY; market share 23.1% and household penetration 64.4 lakh households.

segments.name: International (incl. North America)
segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of consolidated revenue. North America grew 49% (29% normalised); Middle East and rest of world grew 44%. Europe/UK are in an investment phase with margin pressure from logistics costs.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crore after a temporary decline during the shift from wholesale to direct retailer (CPG) sales. EBITDA margin 4%; management guides to 7-8% by year-end and double digits later.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook (RTH/RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 13% YoY, with biryani kits up 42%. The US RTH facility is expected to become operational this quarter; breakeven is targeted at INR400 crore revenue within 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 results are in line with annual estimates and the company is on track across all financial parameters for the full year.
Organic EBITDA is expected to reach INR70-80 crore by year-end, with margin rising to 7-8% and returning to double digits; full recovery in growth and margin targeted for FY27-FY28.
Medium-term segment growth guidance: basmati 10-12%, RTH 15-20% (small base), organic 10-12%.
FY30 ambition is more than doubling India revenue with expanding margins; RTH revenue to double in about 3 years.
Basmati EBITDA margin historically 13-14%, with a plus or minus 1% variance possible if crop inflation occurs.
Middle East growth expected around 15% from a small base.
capex_capacity: Capacity doubled for ready-to-heat products; US RTH facility expected to become operational in Q1 FY27.
Organic capacity expanded in Europe, with a plant set up and a full sales organisation built there.
No capex planned yet for the newly opened Australia entity, which has received a very small equity infusion.
Rice inventory 346,000 tonnes at an average of INR56/kg and paddy inventory 164,000 tonnes at INR38/kg as of 26 June, described as sufficient for the next year's branded demand.
Quarterly volumes: India 109,000 tonnes; international 117,000 tonnes.
demand_pricing: US tariff on rice fell from about 50% to 10%, which management says reduced the margin distortion from tariffs; pricing volatility from tariffs is now normalising.
Rice revenue growth (32-34%) was above volume growth (11%), driven by commodity inflation pass-through and US duty.
Management said it is charging a premium in basmati and Sona Masoori in organic versus competitors.
Freight rates to the Middle East rose from $200 to $4,000 per container; the competitive landscape limited pass-through there.
Logistics cost was 4.7% of revenue in Q1 FY27 after one-offs (damage retention) in Q4 FY26 phased out.
Nielsen methodology change cited for the India market share decline from 23.7% in FY26 to 23.1%; management claims share gains in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino on the crop, and whether margins are at risk from inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-85% of basmati area relies on canal or groundwater irrigation and 14-15% on rain. About 20% of area faces issues; a clearer crop picture is expected by mid-to-end August. Costs would be passed on to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary gross and EBITDA margins fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to the shift from CIF to C&I shipment terms with a related US subsidiary and a drop in organic gross margin from 35% to 33%. Management said consolidated gross margin improved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR419 crore to INR486 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the increase reflects Golden Star, now 100% owned, being consolidated from this quarter. Previously it was not consolidated, so both revenue and expenses rose.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US growth net of discounts, with discounts still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are recorded net of promotions and discounts under accounting rules, so the reported growth is already net.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior quarter included a one-off gain from revaluation of investments, which has not recurred; other income is now normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did organic margin fall and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the model moved from wholesalers to direct retail, with a new Europe plant and sales organisation. Margin is 4% now, targeted at 7-8% by year-end, and expected back in double digits in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much more working capital can be released from supplier financing?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is near optimum supplier financing, with perhaps 4-5 days of further room but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India's market share falling and will the top two players lose share to the third?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to a Nielsen methodology change. It claims share gains this quarter, with about 40%+ share on e-commerce platforms and a 20 lakh household increase last year.

risks_watch: El Nino and irrigation: crop size clarity expected by mid-to-end August; management says about 20% of basmati area faces issues and a lower crop would bring inflation, which it expects to pass on to consumers.

532784|2026-03.headline: Sobha FY26 real estate sales hit a record INR8,136 crore (+~30%), with Q4 EBITDA of INR194 crore and FY27 sales growth guided at a similar ~30%.
532784|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: real estate sales of INR8,136 crore at an average realisation of INR14,675 per sq ft (up 9.4% from INR13,412), and 3,188 homes (5.4 million sq ft) delivered, up about 19%. Q4 revenue recognition improved after occupancy certificates delayed in Q3 were received, with Q4 total income of INR2,030 crore, EBITDA of INR194 crore and PAT of INR92 crore. Net operating cash flow was INR1,637 crore for FY26 (up 39.4%) and the company moved to a net cash position of about INR800 crore. Management expects margins to improve through FY27, with projects nearing completion guided at 24-26% margins against a 30%+ EBITDA margin on the overall unrecognised revenue of INR18,647 crore. Some FY26 launches slipped, and the Rivana (Greater Noida) launch and the Crescent (Gurgaon) launch in April were the main new-launch data points.

Order book: ~one-third sits with IAC, mostly Mahindra. Order book across verticals: Advanced Plastics first, then Mechatronics, Alternate Fuels and Structures and Control Systems.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company revising FY27 guidance given 33% top-line growth and strong Q1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept unchanged. Q1 and Q2 sit on a low base, so growth looks robust now, but growth rates will slow sharply in Q3 and Q4 after the high post-GST-rationalisation FY26 base. Q1 margins of 15.1% expected to be sustained for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How has Lumax managed margins despite plastics up ~30-40%, and how are OEM pass-throughs timed?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastics are on back-to-back OEM arrangements; 80-90% of the increase is recovered within the same quarter, with spillover to the next quarter for a few OEMs. H2 FY26 margin was ~14.9%. Electronics inflation (30-50%+ in some components) has limited impact because Mechatronics is only 6-7% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfuel's Q1 margin of ~23% — one-off or operational? What is the Mahindra business?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 3 crore of one-off tooling revenue from an existing customer, roughly 3% of margin. Normalised operational EBITDA is ~20%, and 19-20% is the expected range. The Mahindra win is for a passenger-vehicle CNG delivery system, not LCVs.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Bajaj Auto's ~64% revenue growth against much lower volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to wallet-share expansion and new models, including new frames for other models. The metallics division grew ~37-40% in Q1, and Chetak is a key platform for both lighting and frames.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected Mechatronics wallet share and growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: No market-share number given. Management targets top-2 positions in connectivity products such as shark-fin antennas within 3-5 years, and top-2 in switches and sensors within 3 years. FY27 Mechatronics revenue is guided at ~INR 400 crore, rising to ~INR 1,000 crore by FY31. Order book is INR 400-500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Minority interest outlook, and is the 20% CAGR now organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority interest guided at 11-13% of PAT, given the current structure after the IAC merger and Lumax FAE becoming a 100% subsidiary. Management said 15% organic CAGR plus a few hundred crore of inorganic was the earlier framework; 20% CAGR is still maintained, but no inorganic deal is planned this year.

FY26 PAT rose 17% to INR270 crore, helped by cost restructuring, while India volumes fell sharply in Q4 as US tariffs shifted orders to other countries. 532809|2026-03.headline: Firstsource Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.6% YoY in constant currency to INR25.8bn; FY27 guidance is 10-13% CC growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.
532809|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR25.8bn (US$283m), up 19.5% YoY in rupee terms and 11.6% in constant currency, with TeleMedik adding 1.3pp. EBIT margin was 12.2%, up 30bps QoQ and 100bps YoY, marking the sixth straight quarter of sequential expansion. Management said two timing effects (a delayed UK collections deal and paused Medicare Advantage payer ramps) hit Q4, which it views as deferrals rather than structural. FY26 revenue crossed US$1bn at INR95.6bn with 13.6% CC growth and 11.7% EBIT margin. Management framed the strategy as "Intelligence that operates" and guided FY27 CC growth of 10-13%.

segments.name: Banking & Financial Services (BFS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY and 5% QoQ in CC with six new logos. UK collections deal, delayed by regulatory approval, is now live; Q4 exit financial services pipeline described as among the strongest in recent quarters.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 16% YoY and 10% QoQ in CC with one new logo. Payer side saw short-term timing shifts as Medicare Advantage plans paused program ramps from January 2026; rates flat per management.

segments.name: Communications, Media & Technology (CMT)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3% YoY but fell 4% QoQ in Q4 due to timing of work packets and program transitions in large consumer tech engagements; management expects a return to healthier growth.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (retail, utilities)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% YoY but fell 8% QoQ in CC in Q4 on a seasonal retail dip after Q3 peak; four new logos added, and utilities demand described as steady.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% QoQ and 14% YoY in CC; management expects broad-based momentum to continue across the three core verticals.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4% YoY and was flat QoQ in CC; two large deals won in Q4 and pipeline up about 60% over the last four quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guided at 10-13%; management said it has visibility to the lower end (10%) and expects the rest to come from pipeline and ramps.
FY27 EBIT margin guided at 12.25-12.75%, above the Q4 FY26 exit of 12.2%.
Management expects margin expansion of 50-75bps a year, with a longer-term target of 14-15% EBIT margin in the next couple of years.
Inorganic contribution to FY27 growth expected at about 2-2.5% from Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik.
Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters of FY27, not back-ended.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 20-22%.
Management said the two Q4 timing effects (UK collections and Medicare Advantage) are deferrals and should provide tailwinds in FY27.
capex_capacity: TeleMedik acquisition integrated in Q4; gives delivery presence in Puerto Rico, a US-compliant lower-cost location for healthcare and non-healthcare nearshoring.
Sales presence being set up in Canada; UK utilities and retail capabilities being replicated in the US; a North America utilities head was onboarded in the last three months.
Dedicated large-deal pursuit team set up; at least four large deals reported in each of the past five quarters.
Investment in go-to-market and technology continued through FY25 and FY26, with new roles including domain-plus-AI, forward-deployed engineers and builders.
Kairos described as the delivery platform for Intelligence that operates, designed to run in clients' own technology environments and model-agnostic across AI partners.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 added 11 new logos, including six strategic logos (potential of at least US$5m annual revenue each); FY26 added 47 new clients including 24 strategic.
FY26 had 150 clients above US$1m run-rate (up 34 over Q4 FY25); US$5m+ clients up 12 and US$10m+ clients up 2 in the year.
Top five and top 10 clients' revenue share fell 8% and 12% respectively over eight quarters.
Management said about 50% of strategic wins from the past eight quarters have converted into relationships above US$5m annual revenue.
Seven of the FY26 large deals came from new logos versus five in FY25.
Pricing for a US collections deal uses a platform fee plus per-interaction pricing with outcome accountability.
Management said AI is a structural TAM expander through scaffolding work, though clients' data quality and regulated processes slow full automation.
Offshore and nearshore delivery shift is accelerating in Europe; management said it may continue near term.
Management said FY26 organic growth was about 9.8-9.9% CC excluding Ascensos, Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik, versus about 12.1% ex-Pastdue and TeleMedik only.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Firstsource growing strongly when the market narrative says AI is cannibalising BPO revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani cited three drivers: TAM expansion as clients need AI scaffolding; share gains from challenger brands playing offense; and clients willing to move work away from in-house delivery with compelling commercial constructs.

qa_highlights.question: How should the rising debt (near INR1,600 crore) be viewed, and is there room for more acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Jain said 40-50% of cash flow goes to shareholders and the rest to acquisitions or growth; FY26 debt rose only about INR200m versus about INR700m in FY25, so the balance sheet leaves buffer for more acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 softer than expected, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani said Q4 was broadly in line barring two timing items: a UK collections deal delayed by regulatory approval into Q1 FY27 (now live), and Medicare Advantage payers pausing program ramps from January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic contribution in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Pastdue Credit and TeleMedik contributed about 1.5% to FY26 growth (organic about 12.1%). Inorganic contribution to FY27 is expected at about 2-2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the right to win against diversified IT services firms in the full-stack intelligent operations strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani argued that clients buy one continuous motion across implement, run and transform rather than pillars; Firstsource's size and domain depth in regulated workflows let it assemble teams around the customer problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much will investment in the Intelligence that operates strategy affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said efficiency saves from automation and offshoring fund new capabilities, and it remains confident of the FY27 margin guidance; FY26 margin expansion was about 74bps.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth phase across H1 and H2, and why does organic growth appear to slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is expected to be spread evenly across the four quarters, not back-ended. Management said about 2% of FY27 growth is inorganic, and the lower end of guidance is backed by visibility plus pipeline and ramps.

532809|2026-06.headline: Firstsource Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR27.2bn (+2.2% QoQ cc) with EBIT margin 12.4%, but INR717m exceptional charges and a healthcare BPaaS wind-down weigh on outlook.
532809|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.9% YoY and 5.5% QoQ to INR27.2bn (US$288m), or 12.3% YoY and 2.2% QoQ in constant currency, the ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. EBIT margin was 12.4%, up 110bps YoY and 20bps QoQ, the seventh straight quarter of margin expansion. Reported PAT was INR1.7bn after INR563m net exceptional charges, against adjusted PAT of INR2.2bn. Management said a healthcare payer BPaaS program is being wound down by a client after a leadership change, costing roughly 1-1.5% of quarterly revenue, and reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.

financial_highlights.change: +22.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ reported; +12.3% YoY, +2.2% QoQ constant currency
three items: INR357m healthcare program termination, INR284m regulatory penalty indemnity, INR76m contingent consideration fair value (Ascensos)

financial_highlights.value: around 23% in Q1; guided 22-24% for FY27

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 14% YoY and 5% QoQ in constant currency; five new logos added. Management cited a strong exit deal pipeline and collections demand from record US consumer debt.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency; two new logos added. Management cited volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions in Silicon Valley consumer tech.

segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY, driven by both existing clients and new logos.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth reaffirmed at 10% to 13%.
FY27 EBIT margin reaffirmed at 12.25% to 12.75%.
Original guidance had included about 1% to 1.5% of growth from the healthcare BPaaS program now being wound down; management says guidance holds after absorbing this.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be strong as new wins ramp over roughly the next three months.
Long-term aim of a 14% to 15% EBIT margin over the next two to three years, with 50-75bps annual expansion thesis reiterated.
Management expects the exceptional-item amounts (INR357m and INR284m) to be recovered from the client and insurer, though they were expensed on a prudence basis.
capex_capacity: No capex plan, capacity figure or utilisation metric was disclosed on the call.

Healthcare BPaaS program (payer) wound down; client had been at advanced implementation stage on a new technology platform, now reverting to status quo platform.

Five new growth engines (Middle East, South Africa, Canada and others) and three new capability frontiers (US Retail and CPG practice, marketing services, security and resiliency services) stood up in Q1.
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5m) won in Q1, the sixth straight quarter of four or more; ACV intake was the highest in the last four quarters.
12 new logos added, including three strategic logos; 145 clients above US$1m run-rate; US$5m+ clients up 80% and US$1m+ clients up 45% over two years.
Healthcare deal wins were more than a third of Q1 wins, in line with the roughly one-third revenue share from healthcare.

Hedge book at 30 June 2026: GBP61.6m at an average of 118-120 for the next 12 months; US$119m at about INR92.7/US$. Around 25-30% of the portfolio is in options at roughly 125-130 for GBP; blended GBP rate about 123-124 and USD about 94.
Management said the BPaaS client is wound down by client decision after leadership change, and the client has added more work elsewhere in the account.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue impact of the healthcare BPaaS termination in Q1, and what does the INR271m charge include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q1 revenue impact of about 1-1.5%. The charge relates to partner-ecosystem deliverables; Firstsource is the single point of contact and is recovering amounts from the client and repaying partners.

qa_highlights.question: How is guidance maintained despite this hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the best quarter for new deal wins in the last four quarters and that several wins ramp quickly, offsetting the 1-1.5% loss, so the 10-13% range is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the healthcare payer churn a sector-wide issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an isolated, one-off event caused by a new client leader pausing programs, not a secular trend. The same client continues to expand its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How does the wound-down program compare with the USD50m steady-state run-rate expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 1-1.5% contribution was its estimate at the start of the year, reflecting slower ramp and schedule risk; the program will not reach the implied trajectory this fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: How are segment margins evolving versus FY24 (BFS above 20% now, healthcare low double-digit)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly segment movements are aberrations from ramp costs and that company margin is up from 11% eight quarters ago to 12.4%, with no systemic issue seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedge liability and forward book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the GBP book is typically 50-75% of committed year-one value and USD about 25%; GBP 61.6m and USD 119m are hedged for the next 12 months at blended rates of about 123-124 (GBP) and 94 (USD).

We do expect the second half of the year to be strong, but at the same time, I think, it's broadly going to be in line with our ability to hit the guidance that we've reinforced.
I wouldn't read too much into one quarter over the other. These are standard aberrations that would happen.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only reaffirmed at 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin after absorbing the 1-1.5% BPaaS loss, with no sign of a raise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three new capability frontiers (US Retail and CPG, marketing services, security and resiliency) and five new growth engines were stood up in Q1, but no specific product launch dates or revenue figures were given.

rows.label: Recovery of INR357m and INR284m exceptional charges
rows.why: Management expects the INR357m healthcare termination and INR284m regulatory indemnity amounts to be recovered from the client and insurer, but both were expensed on a prudence basis and timing is not committed.

rows.label: Hedge book supports margins at INR92.7/US$ and GBP 118-120
rows.why: GBP61.6m is hedged at 118-120 and US$119m at about INR92.7/US$ for the next 12 months, with 25-30% in options at 125-130 for GBP, so currency moves could shift margins either way.

tone.note: Management was confident on full-year guidance, the deal pipeline and the client relationships, and firm that the healthcare charges are one-off, but cautious and somewhat defensive on segment margin questions and the BPaaS ramp, where it gave no quantified forward segment margin path.

532809|2026-09.headline: Firstsource Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR 28.3bn (12.3% constant currency), EBIT margin 12.5%; FY27 CC revenue guidance floor raised to 10.5%.
532809|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 3.7% QoQ in INR and 2% QoQ in constant currency, the 12th straight quarter of sequential growth, with EBIT margin at 12.5% (up 100 bps YoY, 10 bps QoQ) for an eighth straight quarter of expansion. Management signed four large deals (two from new logos) and added 17 new logos, including six strategic logos. Headcount rose by 3,062 to 39,937, largely from a major banking client transition and offshore/nearshore ramps. FY27 constant currency revenue guidance was narrowed upward to 10.5%-13% from 10%-13%, with the EBIT margin guidance of 12.25%-12.75% reaffirmed. Healthcare declined 2% QoQ, and the company is still pursuing recovery on the exceptional charge tied to two clients from last quarter.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 17.1 billion at end June 2026

segments.name: Banking & Financial Services (BFS)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency, with nine new logos; growth broad-based and led North America and Europe. Management said it would not read anything into a slight dip in BFS margin on a quarterly basis.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY but declined 2% QoQ in constant currency (Q1 was +11% YoY), with four new logos. Management attributed the softness to Medicare Advantage scope recalibration after CMS rate changes and the wind-down of a transformative payer BPaaS engagement.

segments.name: Communications, Media & Technology (CMT)
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; management flagged quarter-to-quarter volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions.

segments.name: Utilities & Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 25% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, with two new logos; retail seasonal ramps expected in Q3 and part of Q4.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY and 1% QoQ in constant currency; BFS led growth while healthcare reflected program ramp timing.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY and 7% QoQ in constant currency, led by BFS with CMT momentum; two large wins in the quarter.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 50% YoY, supported by existing relationships and an improving pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guidance raised at the lower end to 10.5%-13% (earlier 10%-13%); upper end of 13% kept 'very much in play', dependent on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance reaffirmed at 12.25%-12.75%.
Management expects a 50-75 bps annual margin improvement to continue over the next couple of years, targeting a 14%-15% EBIT margin band within two to three years.
FY27 effective tax rate guided at 22%-24%.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1, citing large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos, and a healthy pipeline described as the best ever.

Wage increments: frontline and mid-level staff received hikes in Q2, senior staff in Q3; management said forecasts already reflect this and remain within guidance. Quantification was deferred to an offline follow-up.
capex_capacity: Headcount closed Q2 at 39,937, net addition of 3,062 QoQ; India and Philippines accounted for more than 85% of the increase, with South Africa also contributing.
About 80% of gross hiring is offshore or nearshore; onboarding of around 3,000 people was largely ahead of revenue for the banking client transition.

Kairos platform capitalisation is work in progress; some directly attributable costs are capitalised. Intangible asset under development was INR 232 million; the capitalised Kairos cost figure was to be provided offline.

M&A philosophy: plug capability gaps (healthcare, retail, distribution access). Past deals cited: QBSS (~3 years ago, RCM mid-office), Ascensos (retail, ~2 years ago), TeleMedik (earlier in FY27, Puerto Rico footprint and clinical operations).
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5 million) signed in Q2, the seventh straight quarter of four or more; two from new logos. Management said the large-deal run rate has moved from about 2-3 per quarter historically to 4 and wants to reach 5-6.
51 clients above US$5 million run rate, six more QoQ, the largest sequential addition on an organic basis in five quarters; 23 clients in the US$10 million-plus cohort after adding three.
Top 5 and top 10 client revenue share fell by 6 and 10 percentage points respectively over eight quarters; management says top clients are growing at industry rate.
More than 50% of revenues are non-linear; management is working to increase that share through productised services.
Management said renewals with some scope deflation have been held revenue-neutral by adding new work in adjacent processes.
Hedge book as of 30 September 2026: GBP 69.2 million at an average INR 116.6 per pound and USD 68.5 million at an average INR 95.7 per dollar over the next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be affected by furloughs or holidays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business runs continuous mission-critical operations, so it does not expect the furloughs typical of IT services.

qa_highlights.question: Is attrition structurally higher than peers, and is it by design?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said attrition is not comparable to IT services; BPO-type operations are in line with industry averages. Voluntary attrition for associates with more than 180 days of tenure was 28.4% on a trailing 12-month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 given the Q1 contract termination?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management cited large-deal ramps, the banking client transition, 17 new logos and a healthy pipeline; this is why the lower end of guidance was raised to 10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the healthcare vertical bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some timing issues, including the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes, are behind it. It cited HR1 provider-side tailwinds and voice AI and Denials AI now in production at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed to lift large-deal wins above four per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs more pipeline, proactive deal shaping and creative commercial constructs; it is pushing the sales organisation to reach five or six.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin trajectory expected to evolve beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 50-75 bps annual expansion toward 14%-15%, with levers including right-shoring, automation, pricing, exit of loss-making accounts, talent cost and facility optimisation; some gains are reinvested in capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the lower guidance band 2% QoQ, and what drives the upper end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the floor reflects line of sight from H1 visibility, while the 13% upper end depends on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next two to three months.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting deal sizes and decision cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-driven share-of-wallet expansion can lead to larger ACVs; Kairos intelligent context framework is attached to about 50% of the top 50 clients and has shortened some cycles, with one case going live in 8 weeks.

risks_watch: Healthcare sequential decline (-2% QoQ) continues after the payer BPaaS wind-down and Medicare Advantage scope changes; recovery depends on HR1 provider-side ramps from January 2027.
Recovery of the exceptional charge tied to two clients recognised last quarter is unresolved; management is 'optimistic' but gave no timeline.
H2 acceleration depends on phased transformation programmes hitting milestones and on pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months; the upper end of guidance is conditional.
Wage increments for senior staff in Q3 and continued onboarding ahead of revenue could pressure margins; quantified impact was not given.
AI-driven deal deflation and elongated decision cycles, which management says are offset by share-of-wallet gains.
Capitalisation of Kairos costs and the carrying value (INR 232 million under development) were not fully disclosed on the call.
532809|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with clear reaffirmation of the margin path and a raised revenue floor. Cautious on healthcare and on the upper end of guidance, and evasive on Kairos capitalised costs and the exceptional-charge recovery, both of which were deferred offline.
key_quotes: Last quarter, I called this accountability.
We are actively engaged with them on recovery and we remain optimistic about the outcome.
Our answer rests on the intelligent context framework, part of the Kairos operating system, which gives AI the context it needs to work in a live operation.
AI does the heavy lifting, but a person signs off on anything that affects a customer or a regulator.
I wouldn't read anything into any aberrations on a quarter-by-quarter basis.
We can do it offline.
Kairos is not yet fully capitalized as a platform, but there are some costs which we need to capitalize.
So, the improvement that we are seeing is actually structural, it's broad-based, it's not driven by one single lever.

rows.when: next 2-3 quarters, then over next couple of years
rows.why: EBIT margin at 12.5% (+100 bps YoY, +10 bps QoQ) for eighth straight quarter of expansion; management reaffirmed 50-75 bps annual improvement toward 14%-15% in 2-3 years, though FY27 guide of 12.25%-12.75% and senior wage hikes in Q3 cap near-term upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Headcount rose 3,062 to 39,937 in Q2 mostly via hiring ahead of the banking transition, and no new physical capacity, plant or site is discussed; growth is coming from utilising added headcount rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Constant-currency revenue guided to 10.5%-13% for FY27 (floor raised), with H1 at +12.3% CC and management expecting H2 stronger than H1 on 4 large deals, 17 new logos and the banking client ramp; 51 clients above US$5M run rate (+6 QoQ).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond Kairos capitalisation (INR 232 million under development) and no capex plan or utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
