rows.why: Upper end of 13% CC guidance is 'very much in play' but depends on phased transformation milestones and pipeline conversion over the next 2-3 months; floor already raised from 10% to 10.5%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Healthcare fell 2% QoQ CC after Medicare Advantage scope changes and payer BPaaS wind-down, HR1 provider ramps only from January 2027, and recovery on the exceptional charge tied to two clients has no timeline; senior wage hikes in Q3 are unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is scaling productised services (more than 50% of revenue non-linear) and voice AI and Denials AI are already in production at scale; Kairos is attached to about 50% of top 50 clients, but no specific new launch date was given.

rows.label: Large-deal run rate to 5-6 per quarter
rows.why: Four large deals (ACV above US$5M) in Q2, seventh straight quarter at four or more, versus 2-3 historically; management is pushing sales to reach 5-6 but says it needs more pipeline and deal shaping.

rows.label: Healthcare recovery from HR1 ramps
rows.why: Healthcare grew 5% YoY but fell 2% QoQ CC (Q1 was +11% YoY); management cites HR1 provider-side tailwinds from January 2027 and says timing issues are behind it, but the decline has not yet reversed.

rows.label: Net debt reduction
rows.why: Net debt fell to INR 15.3bn from INR 17.1bn in June 2026 (about INR 1.8bn in one quarter), with Q2 FCF at 150% of PAT and H1 at 126%.

532810|2026-03.headline: PFC FY26 standalone PAT hit a record INR 20,051 crore (+16% YoY), but FY27 spread guided lower at 2.40-2.50% and loan growth at ~10%.
532810|2026-03.overview: PFC reported its highest-ever standalone net profit of INR 20,051 crore for FY26, up 16% YoY, helped by 13% NII growth and about INR 1,800 crore of provision reversals. Net NPA fell to 0.13% and net credit-impaired ratio to a new low of 0.15%, after resolution of Sinnar Thermal and TRN Energy. Disbursements were INR 1,65,414 crore and loan book grew about 7% to ~INR 5.8 lakh crore, with management blaming elevated prepayments in a falling-rate cycle. Management guided FY27 spread to 2.40-2.50% and loan growth to around 10%, and outlined the proposed PFC-REC merger targeted for 1 April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: of which ~INR 800 crore from Sinnar/TRN resolution, ~INR 1,000 crore from DISCOM ECL reversal

financial_highlights.metric: Yield / cost of funds / spread / NIM FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 18.55 per share total; final INR 3.95

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Group renewable book INR 1.65 lakh crore; PFC standalone renewables about 16% of lending. Major FY26 disbursements were hybrid solar-wind; ~INR 16,000 crore sanctioned for battery and pumped storage.

segments.name: Conventional generation
segments.commentary: About 50% of PFC lending now generation, of which 16% renewable and balance conventional (down from ~75% historically). Thermal and nuclear expansion cited as emerging opportunities.

segments.name: Distribution (DISCOMs)
segments.commentary: Lending focused on short- and medium-term DISCOM needs; RBPF short-tenor revolving loans fell as DISCOMs shifted to 3-7 year loans. DISCOM ECL provision reversal of ~INR 1,000 crore on improved ratings; AT&C losses 15.04%; DISCOMs posted first all-India PAT of ~INR 2,700 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 spread guided to 2.40%-2.50% (FY26 actual 2.46%), reflecting yield pressure from competitive pricing and forex-driven funding cost.
FY27 loan growth target around 10%; management says without FY26 prepayments growth would have been within the 10-11% guided range.
Management does not expect further RBI rate cuts in FY27 (repo held at 5.25%); expects prepayment pressure to moderate.
PFC-REC merger targeted to take effect 1 April 2027, subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approvals; government to retain government-company status.
Dividend to follow DIPAM policy of 30% of profit, subject to RBI NBFC dividend rules.
No specific FY27 disbursement guidance; FY26 sanctions INR 2.85 lakh crore with only ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed, so spillover expected.
capex_capacity: India installed capacity crossed 530 GW; about 55 GW non-fossil capacity added in FY26, a record (per management).
Peak power demand hit an all-time high of 256 GW in April 2026.
PFC sanctioned ~INR 16,000 crore cumulatively for battery and pumped storage projects.
Sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool estimated at INR 2.5-3 lakh crore (approximate, per management).
Infrastructure disbursements slow in construction phase; pick-up expected as projects approach commissioning.
demand_pricing: PFC consciously priced new lending competitively in FY26 amid banks' aggressive refinancing of commissioned renewable assets, which drove prepayments.
Banks most willing to refinance renewable portfolios given low gestation, early commissioning, certain cash flows and small ticket sizes.

Forex volatility (rupee depreciation vs USD and EUR, Middle East conflict, trade tariffs) raised FY26 funding costs; hedging covers 97% of USD 10.3 billion foreign currency borrowing, with management saying most mark-to-market losses are notional until maturity.
Borrowing mix: 80:20 domestic-foreign; 65% fixed-rate; 60% bonds, 20% bank term loans, 20% foreign currency (per management).
Repayments from borrowers in FY26 were about INR 1,28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did disbursements and loan growth weaken despite stable disbursement volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said disbursements were broadly flat (INR 1,65,414 crore vs ~INR 1,68,000 crore) but DISCOMs shifted from short-tenor RBPF revolving loans (~6-month average) to 3-7 year loans, reducing rollover-driven disbursement counts; competition from banks also present.

qa_highlights.question: Why is only a fraction of sanctions disbursed and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR 2.85 lakh crore with ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed; infrastructure disbursements are slow due to pre-commitment conditions, environmental and land approvals, and pick up near commissioning. Management said the balance is spilling over, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How will the merger affect the government shareholding and borrowing limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Government shareholding would fall to about 41-42% post share swap; management said the government has committed to keep the merged entity a government company, with modalities yet to be decided. Single-borrower exposure limit to banks would fall from 25% to 20% for the merged entity, which management does not see as a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend and ROE outlook post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 30% of PFC's standalone profit, of which PFC receives REC dividend as income; post-merger dividend will be declared on combined profit under DIPAM's 30% policy, subject to RBI rules. No ROE guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does PFC view the impact of a potential future rate hike?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of borrowings are fixed-rate and bond liabilities average 5-6 years, so repricing is gradual; lending rates are linked to the weighted cost of borrowing, so a rate rise would transmit slowly as older debt matures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 spread decline and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 2.40-2.50% versus 2.46% in FY26, citing competitive lending rates, prepayment pressure and forex-driven funding costs; the spread is calculated on weighted average cost including foreign borrowings.

risks_watch: Continued prepayments and bank refinancing of commissioned renewable assets could keep loan growth below the ~10% target.
Rupee volatility and Middle East conflict could raise hedging and translation costs on USD 10.3 billion foreign borrowing; ~97% hedged.
Shiga Energy (INR 522 crore) co-lender approval pending within the INR 854 crore of Stage-3 assets resolved outside NCLT.
Stage-3 book of INR 6,323 crore across 19 projects; FY26 provision write-backs (~INR 1,800 crore) will not recur at the same level, so credit cost may rise.
Merger execution: government stake falling below 50%, creditor exposure limits, and workforce integration (about 520 PFC and about 1,000 combined employees per management).
New ECL norms from April 2027 under RBI; management says current policy broadly in sync with RBI IRAC norms.
532810|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet strength, asset quality and the merger timeline, but cautious and somewhat defensive on loan growth, prepayments and spread compression. Management repeatedly deflected on exact disbursement, dividend and ROE figures, and said merger structure details are still under discussion.
key_quotes: Our net credit impaired asset ratio is at new low at 0.15%.
For FY27, we do not expect any further rate cut from RBI.
We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.
So, spread is being worked out on the weighted average cost which constitutes both the domestic as well as the foreign borrowings.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Loan growth target of around 10% in FY27 versus ~7% in FY26, backed by a sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool of INR 2.5-3 lakh crore and FY26 sanctions of INR 2.85 lakh crore with only ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Spread guided lower to 2.40-2.50% and no further RBI rate cuts expected, with prepayments and competitive pricing as headwinds; FY26 provision write-backs of ~INR 1,800 crore will not recur at the same level.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Loan growth of ~10% is at risk from prepayments and bank refinancing of renewable assets (FY26 loan book +7%), and credit cost may rise as ~INR 1,800 crore of write-backs do not recur.

rows.label: PFC-REC merger effective 1 April 2027
rows.why: Management outlined the merger targeted for 1 April 2027, subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approvals; government stake falls to about 41-42% post share swap.

rows.label: New ECL norms from April 2027
rows.why: RBI's new ECL norms take effect from April 2027; management says current policy is broadly in sync with IRAC norms, so the impact is expected to be limited.

rows.label: Sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool converting
rows.why: Pool of INR 2.5-3 lakh crore with spillover from FY26 sanctions of INR 2.85 lakh crore; disbursement expected to pick up as projects approach commissioning.

tone.note: Management was confident on balance sheet, asset quality (net NPA 0.13%) and merger timeline, but cautious on loan growth, prepayments and spread compression; analysts pressed on disbursement, dividend and ROE, which management deflected.

532811|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover rose 8.76% to INR1,322.30 crores but PAT fell 3.63% to INR80.14 crores; FY27 growth guided at 15-20%.
532811|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 8.76% YoY to INR1,322.30 crores, while PAT declined 3.63% to INR80.14 crores and EBITDA margin compressed to 9.35% from 10.17%. For FY26, turnover rose 11.38% to INR4,565.20 crores and PAT rose 31.17% to INR264.32 crores, with EBITDA margin at 9.52% versus 8.34%. Management blamed Q4 on labour flight from NCR and Bengal/Assam elections, NGT construction bans, a cash crunch in Assam, and war-driven LPG, fuel and supply-chain disruption. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, with an order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, but gave no formal PAT guidance.

segments.name: Central Vista (EPC, design-build, INR2,600-3,000 crores)
segments.commentary: Awarded 14 January 2026; Nirman Bhawan demolished and excavation/concrete started. Management targets about INR1,000 crores of FY27 execution, with a turnover run-rate of INR100-150 crores per month.

segments.name: CSMT Mumbai (order value INR2,076 crores ex-GST)
segments.commentary: Designs now approved and execution has picked up after a slow 1.5 years. FY27 execution target is about INR600 crores.

segments.name: Dahlias (private)
segments.commentary: FY27 execution target about INR400 crores.

segments.name: IJPM - India Jewellery Park (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Design changes ongoing; ground work expected to start in the last month of Q1 FY27 after the Mumbai monsoon. FY27 target kept modest at about INR100 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, up from the 10-15% guidance given in prior years.
EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits in FY27 (currently 9.5% in FY26); management said margins will rise over the next two years as mechanisation takes effect.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, including two L1 positions worth INR1,620.95 crores (RML Hospital Delhi and an Odisha government university project in Bhubaneswar).
FY27 capex about INR300 crores, down from an earlier guidance of about INR500 crores; FY26 capex was about INR274 crores.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid; ramp-up from Q2 and H2 significantly above H1.
Management said no guidance is prudent beyond FY27 given headwinds; a FY28 number was not given. Share buyback 'not in the offing'.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR274 crores; FY27 capex planned at about INR300 crores, with depreciation rising in line.

Mechanisation (tower cranes, passenger hoists costing INR50-70 lakh each, batching plants, concrete pumps) is the stated response to labour shortage. Management estimated the IRR uplift at 7-10% and payback at 4-5 years on equipment with a 4-year life; other assets have a 7-8 year life.
Q4 depreciation was about INR29 crores; management expects a similar run-rate going forward.
Management is evaluating precast and pre-engineered building technologies, but said these would take 2-3 years to be used on projects.
demand_pricing: Government vs private mix is targeted at roughly half and half. Private clients were over 60% of the order book, per an analyst's read.
Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book; 89% of orders have built-in escalation clauses.
Government contracts use WPI-linked escalation with about a one-quarter lag; private contracts pass through volatile materials (cement, steel, grit, sand) roughly month-on-month.
Management is walking away from some projects, including with existing clients, and is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more.
Pipeline has been slowed by the war, with developers delaying launches. The company is bidding selectively with existing or well-funded clients.
Competitors named: L&T, B&F, Nagarjuna, Shapoorji Pallonji, Kalpataru and Tata Projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in FY27-28, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guided at 15-20% and order inflow target about INR8,000 crores. FY28 was not guided; management said FY28 is 'similar' and gave no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and depreciation rising while margins lag, and is this a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry is at an inflection point due to labour shortage and taller, more complex buildings. Mechanisation benefits will take 2-3 years to show; FY27 capex is about INR300 crores, and depreciation is expected to grow in line.

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and fuel-price increases being protected against?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all contracts have escalation clauses; WPI-linked government recovery is lagging, and the company is seeking government compensation. Private contracts are pass-through for basic materials.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin fall was due to inflation vs. disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gross margin decline mainly to under-absorbed IDC and overheads from lost execution days, plus staff cost increments taken in January; inflation was a smaller factor, largely covered by escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed-price share, and how is margin protected in the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book. The 89% escalation-linked share and a better mix (private/public, geography) underpin the double-digit margin target.

qa_highlights.question: Are IJPM and the two L1 projects likely to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: RML Hospital (Delhi) and an Odisha university project are old tenders with no LOA date. Either side can rebid or cancel if escalation has moved too far.

risks_watch: Prolonged war: fuel, metal and LPG prices, supply-chain delays (electrical panels now 4+ months vs 2 earlier), and a possible rupee impact.
Labour shortage expected to persist for 3-4 years, with labour drawn from only 3-4 states; NGT construction bans in NCR add shutdown days.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very weak, so FY27 growth depends on a strong H2.
Receivables and working capital: working capital days at 104 (103 in the prior period); mobilisation advance INR802 crores, about 37% interest-bearing; retention INR450 crores.
Government WPI-linked escalation is lagging; management has lodged representations with the government.
Pipeline slowdown and possible cancellation or rebidding of the two L1 orders.
Shareholders pressing for a buyback; management declined, citing the need for a war chest. Net cash position is INR817 crores.
532811|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and double-digit margins, with a strong order book and stable state governments cited. Cautious and evasive on FY28 guidance, the buyback and the link between capex and margins. Management repeatedly attributed Q4 weakness to labour and elections, and noted a prolonged war as the key risk.
key_quotes: We are giving a guidance of 15% to 20% in this year.
The margin profile, as I said in my last call I have given an indication of double digit and we are nearly there.
So at the moment, the share buyback is not in the offing. That's not even crossed our mind.
Labour shortage is here to stay.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, rising over next two years
rows.why: Management guides double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27 versus 9.52% in FY26 and 9.35% in Q4 FY26, with mechanisation and a bid-margin increase of a couple of percentage points or more as drivers; 89% of order book has escalation clauses.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity addition is named beyond mechanisation capex of about INR300 crores in FY27 (FY26 about INR274 crores); the precast and pre-engineered technology would take 2-3 years to use on projects.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H2 FY27 (Q1 FY27 very slow, ramp-up from Q2)
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% on FY26 turnover of INR4,565.20 crores, backed by a net order book of INR21,096.31 crores to execute over 24-30 months; Central Vista targets about INR1,000 crores and CSMT about INR600 crores of FY27 execution.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is being cut to about INR300 crores in FY27 from an earlier INR500 crores guidance, with no utilisation figure disclosed and the company citing efficiency gains from machinery.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance was raised to 15-20% from 10-15% in prior years, but management is cautious beyond FY27 and Q1 FY27 is guided very weak, so an upgrade depends on a strong H2 ramp-up.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 is expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid, Q4 PAT fell 3.63% to INR80.14 crores, and the company cites a prolonged war with fuel, LPG and electrical-panel lead times rising from 2 to 4+ months.

rows.label: Order inflow target about INR8,000 crores in FY27 incl. two L1 projects worth IN
rows.why: FY26 inflow was INR10,257.39 crores, but the two L1 projects (RML Hospital Delhi, Odisha university) have no LOA date and either side can rebid or cancel, and developers are delaying launches due to the war.

rows.label: Bid margin increase and walking away from some projects
rows.why: Management is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more and declining some projects, including with existing clients, while fixed-price orders are only 11% of the order book.

rows.label: Working capital days at 104 and mobilisation advance of INR802 crores
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 104 from 103, and about 37% of the INR802 crore mobilisation advance is interest-bearing, with retention at INR450 crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 15-20% growth, double-digit margins and the INR21,096 crore order book, but cautious on FY28 guidance, the buyback and how capex links to margins; analysts pushed on margin dilution, capex and working capital.

532811|2026-06.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.
532811|2026-06.overview: Turnover rose 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore, but PAT fell to INR11.42 crore from INR51.11 crore, with EBITDA margin at 4.29% versus 8.59%. Management attributed the drop to a INR29 crore AIIMS Jammu bill reduction (2.6 percentage points), labour cost increases of roughly 35-40% in NCR (about 50% of the order book), higher staff costs, and SIR/election-related disruption in West Bengal and Assam. Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

financial_highlights.value: Sharp increase YoY; mgmt expects similar ~INR15-16 crore per quarter
financial_highlights.change: due to mobilisation advance for Central Vista

segments.name: NCR projects (about 50% of order book)
segments.commentary: Labour minimum wages rose about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled categories in Haryana and UP, with projects running at 40-50% labour strength. Management estimated a company-level EBITDA hit of about 1.5% this quarter, up to 5% of turnover on some projects where material is client-issued.

segments.name: AIIMS Jammu
segments.commentary: Final bill reduced by INR29 crore after finalisation; the matter is going to arbitration. Impact is 2.6 percentage points on EBITDA. Management says the project is closed and no further hit is expected.

segments.name: Central Vista (Ministry of Housing/CPWD-type govt project)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR700 crore billing in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore in FY28, with Nirman Bhawan demolition complete and Udyog Bhawan 90% demolished. Full project completes in FY29.

segments.name: CST (Mumbai railway station project)
segments.commentary: Q1 billing about INR70 crore; management targets about INR400-450 crore for FY27 (hoping to cross INR500 crore total) and about INR700 crore in FY28. Earlier target was about INR600 crore.

segments.name: Gems and Jewellery Park
segments.commentary: Work on ground delayed by client design changes; expected to start in Q3 FY27. Targets INR100 crore billing in FY27 and about INR450 crore in FY28; 3.5-year completion.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27 retained, with the low end attributed to NGT uncertainty.
No double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26-level margins over the next three quarters, but gave no firm timeline.
Expects some client compensation for labour cost increases to flow over the next two quarters; NGT impact on Q3 unquantified.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus earlier INR8,000 crore guidance; bidding to be less aggressive.
FY27 capex cut to INR220-250 crore (from about INR300 crore); Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Working capital expected to improve from current level (119 days), with Assam receivables collection resuming.
Expects double-digit margin aspiration for FY28 but said it is hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex guided at INR220-250 crore for FY27, down from about INR300 crore earlier; Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Depreciation is elevated and expected to recur given higher capex over the last 2-3 years.
Machinery investment planned to offset labour shortages, and digitisation is in progress.

Central Vista: Nirman Bhawan fully demolished, foundation casting begun, structural steel work from September; Udyog Bhawan handed over about 3 weeks ago with excavation started. About 50% of the job to be commissioned by end of next year.
Dahlias (DLF) and DLF Downtown (about INR1,600-1,700 crore) projects delayed by design changes; billing targets INR30-35 crore/month from Dahlias and INR25-30 crore/month from DLF Downtown.
demand_pricing: Net order book INR20,663.52 crore; private sector about 62% of order book; fixed-price contracts about 10.34%.

Order inflow only INR512.81 crore in FY27 to date; RML (about INR500 crore) is L1 but not converted. Odisha government university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1 hospital/university) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract.

Management is deliberately less aggressive in bidding given material and labour volatility; bid prices now factor in labour, doubled shuttering and steel rates, and staff costs above 5% (up from 3.5-4.5%).

Materials: cement and steel are pass-through (about 30-day lag on private contracts); government contracts use quarterly WPI-based escalation. Switchgear delivery lead times have stretched from 4-6 weeks to 3-4 months due to the war.

Payments: central government payments not an issue, except a Central University project in Himachal unpaid for 5 months. Assam receipts resumed after elections, with major chunks received in the last 15 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 EBITDA margin so low, and was the labour cost rise known at the last call (about 15 days/45 days after quarter end)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the labour increase was not known at the last call, citing a sharp NCR minimum wage hike of about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled labour, with projects at 40-50% labour strength. Management disputed the suggestion it had withheld information and declined further debate, offering site visits instead.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins recover, and when will client compensation flow through; is double-digit margin possible in Q3 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Compensation timing cannot be dated, but some is expected over the next two quarters. Double-digit EBITDA margin is ruled out for FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26 margins over the next three quarters. NGT impact on Q3 is unquantified. FY28 double-digit is an aspiration, hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Is top-line guidance changing (12-15% vs 15%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 12-15% top-line growth is retained, with the lower end linked to NGT uncertainty. Management said it could cross 15% if the year resembles last year.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost jump and recurrence; interest-bearing mobilisation advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to mobilisation advance taken for Central Vista; similar INR15-16 crore per quarter expected. Of INR924 crore mobilisation advance, 31% is interest-bearing at around 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Inflow guidance and bidding stance after Odisha university bid lapsed?
qa_highlights.answer: The Odisha university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract. RML (about INR500 crore) remains L1 but not converted. FY27 inflow now seen at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus INR8,000 crore earlier; bidding will be less aggressive.

qa_highlights.question: How much labour-cost impact is quantifiable, and how much of it is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level EBITDA hit about 1.5% this quarter; project-level impact 2% to about 5% of turnover where material is client-issued. Without escalation the hit is about 1%, as some contracts escalate after 6-12 months. Management cited incentives from developers for stage-wise completion as partial offset.

risks_watch: Client acceptance of labour-cost claims in NCR (about 50% of order book); contracts without labour escalation clauses and no quantified share of book with such clauses provided.
NGT-related restrictions in Delhi-NCR (Haryana, UP) could hit Q3 FY27 execution and margins; impact not quantified.
Order inflow at only INR512.81 crore in FY27 to date; FY27 inflow guidance cut to INR4,000-5,000 crore from INR8,000 crore.
Arbitration on AIIMS Jammu (INR29 crore bill cut) outcome uncertain; management says project closed with no further hit.
Working capital at 119 days; Assam receivables collection resumed but a Himachal central university project unpaid for 5 months.
Switchgear lead times stretched to 3-4 months from 4-6 weeks; material volatility from the war; cement and steel pass-through lag of about 30 days (private) and quarterly WPI escalation (government).
Finance cost to stay at INR15-16 crore per quarter due to Central Vista mobilisation advance; depreciation to stay elevated.
key_quotes: So it would be fair to say that this financial year, we are ruling out having a double-digit EBITDA margin.
Q2 is an aberration.
We are hoping to get back to those margins over the next three quarters.
To be frank, we are no longer very aggressive.
So this is not considered as a statutory increase.
532811|2026-06.management_tone: Defensive and combative under questioning, especially on whether the labour cost rise was known at the last call; management was confident on the order book and recovery path but refused to give firm dates for margin recovery or double-digit margins, and repeatedly cited NGT and other external factors as unquantified risks.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 4.29% from 8.59% (AIIMS Jammu bill cut 2.6pp, NCR labour cost up 35-40%, ~1.5% company-level hit); management hopes to return to Q1 FY26 margins over three quarters but gave no firm timeline and ruled out double-digit margin for FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Turnover up 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore and top-line growth guidance of 12-15% held, backed by INR20,664 crore net order book, with Central Vista billing target of INR700 crore in FY27 and CST at INR400-450 crore; low end tied to NGT uncertainty.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex being cut to INR220-250 crore for FY27 from about INR300 crore (Q1 about INR60 crore), and management is shifting to less aggressive bidding, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 order inflow guidance cut to INR4,000-5,000 crore from INR8,000 crore with only INR512.81 crore inflow to date, and margin guidance cut to no double-digit; management says it could cross 15% growth only if the year resembles last year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NGT restrictions in Delhi-NCR could hit Q3 FY27 execution and margins (impact unquantified), labour cost claims are not yet recovered, and the 12-15% growth low end is linked to NGT uncertainty.

rows.label: Order inflow shortfall vs guidance
rows.why: Only INR512.81 crore inflow in FY27 to date against revised FY27 guidance of INR4,000-5,000 crore (cut from INR8,000 crore), after the INR1,620 crore Odisha bid lapsed and RML (~INR500 crore) is L1 but unconverted.

rows.label: Client compensation for labour cost increases
rows.why: Management expects some client compensation over the next two quarters, but timing cannot be dated; company-level EBITDA hit about 1.5% this quarter and up to 5% of turnover on some NCR projects.

rows.label: Finance cost stays elevated
rows.why: Finance cost expected at INR15-16 crore per quarter from the Central Vista mobilisation advance, of which 31% (of INR924 crore) is interest-bearing at about 8%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR20,664 crore order book and Central Vista/CST billing ramp but refused firm dates for margin recovery or double-digit margins, and turned defensive when analysts asked whether the NCR labour cost rise was known at the last call.

532814|2026-03.headline: Indian Bank Q4 FY26: Q4 net profit Rs 3,103 crore (+1.3% QoQ), FY26 profit Rs 12,156 crore (+11.33%), gross NPA cut to 1.98%.
532814|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a decent year, beating guidance on most parameters except cost-to-income, with advances up 13.43% led by RAM (+15.18%) and corporate growth reviving to 9.19%. Gross NPA fell 111 bps to 1.98% and annualised Q4 slippage eased to 0.85%, while NIM for the year declined 17 bps to 3.24%. Management guided FY27 to tighter NIM (3.10%-3.25%), ROA (1.20%-1.30%) and growth (advances 11%-13%), citing rising cost of deposits and lower treasury income. ECL impact was not quantified; management said it would be absorbed over one to three quarters and that the final guidelines were received only the day before the call.

financial_highlights.change: down from 46.90% in December; above guidance

financial_highlights.value: Rs 31,000 crore (SMA-0 ~Rs 16,000 cr, SMA-1 ~Rs 9,000 cr, SMA-2 ~Rs 6,000 cr)
About Rs 310 crore (management cited Rs 400-500 crore MOC in Q4)

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 18.72% and MSME 16.39% within RAM (+15.18%); about 6 lakh loans and Rs 48,000 crore sanctioned to MSME. Personal loans only Rs 6,500 crore and MFI Rs 3,300 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.19% after about 3% last year; corporate sanctions about Rs 1.31 trillion. Exposure to NBFCs fell about Rs 8,000 crore, with about 99% rated AAA/AA/A.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Overseas book runs through GIFT City and Singapore branches (plus Sri Lanka), mainly syndicated loans and trade finance across sectors.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital business grew 63% to Rs 272,000 crore; mobile banking users 2.36 crore; 94% of transactions digital; 97% of retail and agri loans sanctioned digitally.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 9%-11%; advances growth 11%-13%; CASA around 40%; CD ratio around 80%.
FY27 NIM 3.10%-3.25% (cost of deposits to stay elevated as advances outpace deposits); ROA 1.20%-1.30%.
FY27 gross NPA 1.50%-1.60%; net NPA below 0.25%; credit cost below 1%; slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recoveries Rs 4,500-5,500 crore (vs guidance Rs 5,500-6,500 crore in FY26); written-off book recovery Rs 1,200-1,500 crore.
Treasury profit expected around Rs 1,000-1,200 crore for FY27; LCR to be kept around 115%-120%.
ECL impact to be absorbed over roughly one to three quarters; management said some spill-over into FY28 is likely. Numbers to be given later.
Management said it is comfortable with growth 1%-2% below industry, prioritising NIM and asset quality.
capex_capacity: Opened 102 branches so far; target about 300 branches over three years, described as on track.
IND Optima cash management launched with 150-plus corporate customers onboarded.
Digital pipeline: corporate CRM, corporate ecosystem engine, RFP creator, invoice processing, intelligent document reader, IND UPI app upgrade, and automated suspicious transaction reporting.
Digital and IT budget to be roughly equivalent to employee cost, per Ashutosh Choudhury.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: jewel loans (16%-17% of book, Rs 1.27 trillion) grew about 28% last year on gold price rises; management does not expect similar growth this year.
Around 50% of the loan book is linked to external benchmarks, leaving little repricing lever; MCLR-linked loans are the main remaining lever.
Retail term deposit rates will not be cut because bulk deposit rates are elevated; bulk and CD together are about 18%-19% of deposits, kept under 20%.
Pipeline Rs 51,000 crore, of which sanctioned but unavailed term loans about Rs 34,000-35,000 crore; focus on green energy, transmission, data centres and roads.
Textile remains stressed for about two years; management says little leather exposure.
Average SA balance (ex-BSBD) rose to Rs 46,000 from Rs 30,000; average current account balance rose to Rs 2.64 lakh from Rs 1.88 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the bank for the final ECL guidelines, and how large is the hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final guidelines came the day before and impact will be a little higher than draft estimates, adding the HTM book is now included. It declined to give a number yet, saying it would give concrete figures later, and expects the impact to be absorbed over one to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia war and tariffs raise slippages? What about SMA trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 slippage rose on about Rs 400-500 crore of March MOC, which recurs each March. SMA fell mainly because two government accounts left SMA-2; management also said some stress has been present since tariffs in August but is not visible in SMA.

qa_highlights.question: How will treasury income trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said treasury will be lower but not as severe as last year, since securities have not been sold at low yields. It expects Rs 1,000-1,200 crore of treasury profit for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank measuring the revenue benefit of digital investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits are real but not quantified; cited 94% digital transactions (branch visits cost at least 5x more), and said it will try to quantify going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What levers exist on the asset side if cost of deposits rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few levers remain since about 50% of loans are external-benchmark linked; MCLR-linked loans may reprice up. It is focusing on mid-sized corporates of Rs 50-500 crore for better pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and why is it so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Average LCR was 127% (currently 123%-124%). Management said 115%-120% is a fair operating level and that excess SLR holdings support the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AFS reserve movement?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS reserve moved from about Rs 400 crore in December to minus Rs 200 crore in March, per management.

risks_watch: ECL transition: impact not quantified; some spill-over into FY28 expected; HTM book now included; management has not disclosed existing floating/standard provisions beyond about Rs 500 crore standard-asset provisions in Q4.
Cost of deposits rising with advances outpacing deposits; NIM guidance cut to 3.10%-3.25%.
Recoveries falling (Rs 7,600 crore to Rs 6,600 crore) and treasury income lower in FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio ended FY26 at 46.03%, above guidance; management said course correction is underway.
MSME stress if industry weakens; textile sector weak for about two years; monitor SMA-0 (up to about Rs 16,000 crore).
532814|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability, with a clear message that growth is secondary to NIM and asset quality. Cautious and somewhat evasive on ECL quantum and on the cost-of-deposit outlook, saying numbers will come later.
key_quotes: So, if I summarize the result, I think it has been a decent year, almost all parameters except cost-to- income ratio, we have done better than our guidance.
But, having said that, let me assure you, all of you, that impact is not going to be very huge.
We will give you concrete numbers so that variation is minimum.
So, my focus is, of course, growth, but NIM and asset quality should also remain intact.
So, in NPA, in fact, we are not holding any floating provision, NPA whatever we are making only a specific account-wise provision.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 NIM guided to 3.10%-3.25% vs FY26 3.24% and Q4 3.23%, cost of deposits rising as advances outpace deposits, and treasury profit guided to Rs 1,000-1,200 crore vs lower FY26 base; ROA guided 1.20%-1.30% vs FY26 1.31%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: over next 3 years, 102 opened so far, ~300 targeted
rows.why: Branch rollout of about 300 branches over three years is on track with 102 opened so far, so incremental branch capacity keeps coming live through the window, though it is small relative to the balance sheet.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances guided at 11%-13% and deposits at 9%-11% for FY27 vs FY26 advances growth of 13.43%, backed by a Rs 34,000-35,000 crore sanctioned-but-unavailed term loan pipeline; management is deliberately growing 1%-2% below industry, so volume growth slows from FY26 pace.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or new plant announcements were not discussed; no utilisation metric applies to a bank of this type.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was set as new ranges with NIM cut to 3.10%-3.25% and treasury lower, and management prioritised NIM and asset quality over growth, so no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL impact is unquantified, higher than draft estimates per management, and to be absorbed over 1-3 quarters with some spill-over into FY28; cost of deposits rising could pressure NIM further, and cost-to-income ended FY26 at 46.03% above guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IND Optima cash management is launched with 150-plus corporate clients onboarded, and a digital pipeline (corporate CRM, RFP creator, invoice processing, IND UPI app upgrade) is in progress with no dates given.

rows.label: ECL transition provisioning hit
rows.when: over next 1-3 quarters, with some spill-over into FY28
rows.why: Final ECL guidelines received the day before the call, HTM book now included, impact to be a little higher than draft estimates and not yet quantified; it will be absorbed over 1-3 quarters.

rows.label: Recoveries and treasury income fall in FY27
rows.why: Recoveries guided to Rs 4,500-5,500 crore vs Rs 6,651 crore in FY26 and treasury profit to Rs 1,000-1,200 crore, both lower, removing non-core support to earnings.

rows.label: MCLR-linked loan repricing
rows.why: About 50% of the book is externally benchmark-linked with few levers left, so only MCLR-linked loans (about half the book) may reprice up to offset rising cost of deposits, with focus on Rs 50-500 crore mid-sized corporates.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (gross NPA down 111 bps to 1.98%) and profitability, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the ECL quantum and cost-of-deposit outlook, saying numbers would come later; analysts pressed on ECL hit, SMA trends, treasury income and deposit-cost levers.

532814|2026-09.headline: Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 14.71% to Rs 3,462 crore, helped by Rs 1,134 crore NSE MTM gain; guidance raised to 11-12% deposit and 13-14% advances growth.
532814|2026-09.overview: Indian Bank reported Q2 FY27 with total business up 14.22%, advances up 16.39% and deposits up 12.50% year on year. Profit was lifted by NSE-related gains (Rs 252 crore realised plus Rs 1,134 crore MTM), while operating profit excluding NSE grew about 18%. Management raised deposit and advances growth guidance, and flagged ECL provisioning (Rs 1,500 crore this quarter, Rs 2,500 crore cumulative) and a possible one-time HTM mark-to-market hit from 1 April. CASA ratio improved year on year to 39.36% but slipped sequentially on FCNR(B) inflows.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in total; includes NSE gains of Rs 252 crore realised and Rs 1,134 crore MTM

financial_highlights.change: +8 bps YoY; domestic +1 bp QoQ, global +2 bps QoQ
Up from 38.87% YoY; slightly down QoQ
Down from Rs 1.62 lakh crore QoQ

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 17.37% YoY; 92% of the retail book has CIBIL score above 750. Housing originated 60% via branches and 40% via DSAs, with zero co-lending.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 17.18% YoY. Agri gold loan book reached Rs 1.16 lakh crore, up about 22% YoY and 11% QoQ. Agri book outside drought-declared states is under Rs 1,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.06% YoY. About Rs 10,000 crore of MSME limits remains undrawn.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.92% YoY. Pipeline of Rs 63,000 crore: Rs 30,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed, Rs 10,000 crore in-principle approved, around Rs 23,000 crore early stage. Growth target now 10-12%.

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 17.74% YoY and constitute about 67% of the loan book.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income ex-NSE was Rs 290 crore in Q2 (Rs 293 crore a year ago) and Rs 794 crore in H1 (Rs 854 crore). Net MTM loss of about Rs 11 crore. Management expects muted treasury income going forward.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Loans against FCNR(B) deposits of about USD 2 billion were extended at preferential rates, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value; this drove advances growth and is expected not to recur fully next quarter.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance raised to 11-12% from 9-11%.
Advances growth guidance raised to 13-14% from 11-13%; during Q&A CEO said 14-15% for next quarter and 12-13% in another comment.
NIM expected to expand 5-6 bps in Q3 FY27 (6-7 bps in one response); further moves depend on repo rate.
Recovery guidance unchanged; management expects to do better than guided.
Recurring ECL impact on credit cost maintained at 10-15 bps; one-time ECL impact expected at Rs 3,500 crore in total.
CRAR expected at around 17-17.5% by March-end; Rs 1,000-2,000 crore Tier 2 raise possible in January after Rs 1,000 crore maturity.
Bulk deposits to be raised cautiously; up to Rs 5,000 crore infrastructure bonds approved; CASA ratio target around 40%.
capex_capacity: Corporate credit capacity being built; corporate growth was 1-2% earlier, now targeted at 10-12% with credit training.

CRM launched in July added about Rs 1,500 crore of business in the quarter; fintech solutions to 223 companies and government departments added about Rs 5,000 crore; CMS-linked CASA about Rs 7,000 crore.
AI tools launched in Q2: TARA voice-based conversational banking and Smart Wealth personal finance tool; digital business grew 18% YoY.
Added about 2.5 lakh salary accounts this year so far against 3 lakh in full last year.
demand_pricing: Competition very high across segments; many banks lending housing below 7%. Management not chasing 20-25% growth, citing bottom-line and underwriting risk.
MCLR-linked book is 43.19% of advances; external benchmark-linked book is 49.65%. Benefit of 25 bp repo hike accrued from next day on external-linked loans.
Agri gold loan yield 8.85% (one-year MCLR), unchanged QoQ.
Working capital demand is stagnant: WCDL down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore and cash credit down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore over two to three quarters; management sees no crisis-led drawdown increase.
No stress seen in SME, agriculture or retail; SMA-2 accounts above Rs 25 crore total only about Rs 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standard asset provisions rise from Rs 733 crore to Rs 1,882 crore, and what drove miscellaneous income to Rs 468 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL provision of Rs 1,500 crore this quarter and Rs 1,000 crore last quarter, totalling Rs 2,500 crore, against an expected total impact of Rs 3,500 crore. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of interest on an income tax refund, which may not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Where will treasury income come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects muted treasury income and does not expect high profits; not budgeted for high treasury gains. Forex income guidelines from RBI are being assessed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit and credit growth continue, and what drives NIM?

532827|2026-03.headline: Page Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.1% to INR12,526 million on 10.8% volume growth; FY26 EBITDA margin 22%, guided to 19-21% for FY27.
532827|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.1% YoY to INR12,526 million, with volume up 10.8% to 54.5 million pieces and PAT up 9% to INR1,787 million. Management attributed the pickup to better consumer sentiment, a correction in distributor inventory that aligned secondary and primary sales, and product upgrades, with March the strongest month. EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the quarter and 22% for FY26, but management guided to a 19-21% range for FY27 citing marketing normalising to 5% of sales, input cost inflation and technology investments. Price increases were small: a 2% weighted average taken in January on product enhancements, with a further price increase planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input costs.

Management reads consumer sentiment from EBO jockey.in, where Q4 showed a decent uplift versus the first three quarters.

segments.name: Category: Outerwear and athleisure
segments.commentary: Athleisure is reviving after distributor inventory correction; outerwear and value-added premium products are supporting premiumisation. Management did not give category-level growth numbers.

segments.commentary: About 116,600+ multi-brand outlets, 1,615 exclusive brand stores and 893 large-format stores. One large-format store was exited over commercial negotiations, reducing LFS count.

Marketing spend to rise from a little over 4% of sales in FY26 to close to 5% in FY27.
Management targets double-digit volume growth into FY27 and a better volume-value performance than FY26 (value-volume gap of about 4 points in Q4).

demand_pricing: Q4 demand improved across categories and channels; March was strong, with January and February also ahead of the first three quarters. Management attributed this to better tertiary sell-out and tighter primary-secondary alignment after distributor inventory correction.

Price increase: 2% weighted average taken from mid-January production, flowing into revenue only from mid-March under FIFO; management said the Q4 price contribution was minimal. Management said the January increase was for product enhancements, not inflation.

Competitive intensity is lower than 1-1.5 years ago in men's and women's, as several D2C brands exited or shrank offline distribution and cut discounting and marketing spend.
Input costs: fresh purchases are seeing elevated inflation, particularly cotton; management declined to quantify the current rate, calling the situation dynamic.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

532827|2026-06.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
532827|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

532832|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit record INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ), but FY26 reported PAT was a loss of INR872 crores on revenue-recognition timing and merger accounting.
532832|2026-03.overview: Embassy Developments posted record Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores and FY26 presales of INR4,631 crores (+128% YoY), with 93% of the INR5,000 crore guidance achieved. FY27 guidance is INR6,000 crores own presales (plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects), INR3,000 crores collections and about INR19,400 crores of new launch GDV. Two legal overhangs (CIRP petition and KIADB resumption order) were resolved, and the ASM framework exit took effect 6 May 2026.

532832|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.

Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?

532834|2026-03.headline: Camlin Q4 FY26 revenue about INR424 crores and EBITDA INR21 crores (5% margin), hit by a roughly 20% quarterly sales shortfall from shipping and war-related disruption.
532834|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was weak: management said sales were hit by about 20% from shipment delays, freight shortages and longer transit times linked to the Middle East conflict. Revenue was about INR424 crores in the quarter, with total revenue of INR1,723 crores after moving discontinued operations out. EBITDA was INR21 crores (5%), with vanillin sales largely from channel stock and Blends growth of 17%, short of the 20% target. Management said FY27 guidance is unchanged: revenue INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin 12-14%. The CFS Europe liquidation produced a gain of about INR100 crores and removes ongoing cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year.

rows.label: Syensqo price increase to $19-20/kg

532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.

CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

532835|2026-03.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.
532835|2026-03.overview: ICRA reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 28.4% YoY, with Research and Analytics up 56.8% on the Fintellix acquisition and Ratings up 10.6%. Q4 consolidated PBT before exceptional items and tax was INR 72.8 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 20.4% and PBT grew 10%, with exceptional charges from the new Labour Code excluded for comparability. Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. Capital allocation questions (buyback, cash of over INR 700 crores, acquisition IRRs) were largely deflected, with the dividend raised and a special dividend declared.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10.6% in Q4 and 14.2% for FY26. Management said the segment is a leverage play on economic activity, and Q4 growth was below some peers, which management attributed to a different base and strategic focus on growth segments.

segments.name: Research and Analytics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)
segments.commentary: Stable in core areas but growth moderated due to discontinued engagements and automation. Management expects a structural margin shift as non-KnowTech businesses, with different margin profiles, gain mix.

segments.name: Moody's-related non-ratings work
segments.commentary: Growth has been muted over the last couple of years and management expects moderation, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Some periodic in-sourcing by the parent continues.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management cited a BankTech product-led EBITDA range of 20% to 35%, depending on geography mix.
Management expects Fintellix to drive reasonable growth over the next 2 to 3 years, partly offsetting Knowledge Services moderation, without quantifying it.
ICRA projects India GDP growth moderating to 6.2% in real terms in FY27, assuming average crude of $95 per barrel.

Management expects bank credit to drive most ratings growth in the near term, with bond market activity subdued due to higher yields; no significant slowdown seen in the first couple of months of FY27.
Bank transition to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027 is expected to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions.
Management expects roughly INR 180 to 200 crores of cash flow generation in FY27, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Research and Analytics reorganised into KnowTech, BankTech and CapTech, supported by a unified IT and product engineering organisation.
Ongoing investment in analytics platforms, compliance capabilities and AI-powered agents; AI layer being integrated into subsidiary analytical tools.
demand_pricing: Ratings demand is tied to bank credit and bond issuance; the first couple of months of FY27 showed no significant slowdown, but geopolitical headwinds persist.
Fintellix competitors cited: Regnology and Nasdaq Technologies (global, PE or public-backed, acquisition-driven), plus system integrators and some Indian CRAs with risk and regulatory solutions.
About USD 18 million of FY26 revenue is dollar-denominated (roughly one-third of about INR 600 crores revenue, per management's figure); dollar-denominated costs are not significant.
Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Ratings growth materially lower than peers, and what is the non-ratings growth ex-Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICRA is in a similar band to peers, with double-digit growth over the last 4 years, and that growth-segment focus is the strategy. Ex-Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly while Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration given over INR 700 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a rising dividend (normal dividend INR 60 to INR 70 per share plus special dividend) and said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated, subject to Board approval and tax changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ratings outlook for FY27, and what are April-May borrowing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bond activity to stay subdued given higher yields, with bank credit driving growth. No significant slowdown was seen in the first couple of months of FY27. No revenue growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&A margins evolve as the mix shifts, and could Ratings margins exceed 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said product-led BankTech-type businesses earn 20% to 35% EBITDA margins, and that double-digit Ratings revenue growth typically brings margin expansion as employee cost growth stays below 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's-related work and in-sourcing from the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been muted and is expected to moderate, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Periodic in-sourcing continues, with new project work arriving on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fintellix segment profit and business description?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Fintellix-specific contribution, citing parity of disclosure, but referred to notes to accounts showing around 26% EBITDA margin. Fintellix was described as RiskTech and RegTech, covering regulatory reporting and credit analytics for banks, insurers and asset managers.

risks_watch: Elevated energy prices from the West Asia conflict and a possible weak monsoon could weigh on FY27 growth and credit demand.
Knowledge Services growth moderation and automation trends could continue to pressure segment margins during the mix shift.
Limited disclosure of acquisition returns and Fintellix-specific financials, which shareholders have asked about.
Ratings margin gap versus other CRAs; management intends to close it through sales growth.
Capital allocation: whether cash above INR 700 crores is returned to shareholders via buyback or other means, pending Board decision.

532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR7,773 crores (+19.1%), operating EBITDA margin 22.2% vs 20.5%; ~85% of consolidated revenue and EBITDA. Q4 revenue INR2,023 crores (+19%), Q4 EBITDA margin 22.1%. Occupancy 68% vs 69%; ARPOB up 3.4% to INR2.51 crores.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue INR1,527 crores (+8.5%), operating EBITDA INR360 crores (23.6% margin vs 17.7%; 23.2% ex one-offs). Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69%; occupied beds up 15% (management cited 3,270 to 2,838, a figure order inverted in the transcript). FMRI at 85-95% occupancy; BG Road at ~55% vs ~63-64% area norm.
International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not consolidate Gleneagles and does not track full-year numbers; it is trending around INR70 per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Jaipur and FEHI improving, and why build a Bangalore hospital in a competitive market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational efficiency, new facilities and clinical talent at FEHI; Jaipur expected to grow ~15% at 13-14% margin. The People Tree site is a less competitive micro-market with underserved catchment, per Ashutosh Raghuvanshi.

risks_watch: Oncology drug price caps under CGHS/ECHS and the pace of revenue loss in Punjab, with no resolution timeline.

International patient growth slowing (Q4 ~11%) and sustainability of domestic growth offsetting it.
Shalimar Bagh approval delays moving ~300 beds from FY28 to FY29.
Debt rise to 1.09x net debt/EBITDA after acquisitions; FY27 capex about INR900 crores.
Pending Gleneagles transaction and IHH equity infusion, both without timelines.

532843|2026-06.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.
532843|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.5% YoY to INR 2,545 crore, with hospital revenue up 19% to INR 2,187 crore and diagnostics gross revenue up 10.2% to INR 407 crore. Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP rose 15.8% to INR 568 crore, but margin eased to 22.3% from 22.6%, with hospitals at 21.5% versus 22.1%. Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

532851|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.

Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

532851|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.
532851|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 12% YoY to INR612 crore from INR691 crore, with management attributing the drop to a delayed and uneven monsoon and high temperatures that pushed back crop protection demand. Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

Raw material volatility: solvent prices moved 25-30% week to week and some doubled; gross margin of 31.6% partly reflects older inventory, and management said the net effect was mixed.
Sales returns: management expects returns to fall to at least half of last year's INR200 crore, with only one or two herbicides showing failures; placements were kept lower this year.
Kaeros early-stage costs: about 100 people hired in Q1, normalised margin in single digits and not expected to reach double digits soon.
Pricing power: one hike in March, two in April, a May hike rolled back; no significant price increase realised through July.
Working capital: June inventory was slightly elevated and management expects a sharp decline in Q2; buyback or dividend to be decided after Q1.
key_quotes: So, I believe that the total turnover of the company dropped, so that was the reason there was impact in the profitability, which we should be able to recover in Q2 with improved sales number, which are expected after the August ends .
So, after that we'll review that what type of growth will be possible in this year and will give you revised targets.
I think that we should be able to reduce the sales return numbers to at least half what was there in the previous year.

Performance has been mixed with some progress well and some requiring sharper execution, better visibility now available on key drivers, area of opportunity, area of requiring corrective actions, need to move from initiatives to measurable outcomes is realized
